8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295
```

Accessibility Specialist persona review of UI redesign

```text
Now I have both documents. Let me write a structured accessibility specialist review of the proposed redesign.

---

## Accessibility Specialist

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Document-centric layout reduces tab-switching cognitive load** — by consolidating 26 tabs into 7 document tabs with auto-switching, users with cognitive or motor disabilities benefit from fewer navigation context switches and a clearer mental model of workflow progression.
- **Inline editing preserves focus locality** — Section 12 (In-Place Editing) keeps edits in-place within the document viewer rather than requiring users to jump to separate modal dialogs or tabs, reducing the burden on users with short-term memory challenges.
- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Section 4 moves questions adjacent to the analysis sections they relate to, eliminating the need to context-switch between chat and structured data; answers post back to chat, creating a bidirectional flow that is more discoverable for screen reader users.
- **Explicit keyboard alternative for drag-to-reorder** — Section 8 documents ↑↓ buttons as a full keyboard pathway, directly addressing current critical gap GAP-120 (tab keyboard access) and allowing keyboard-only users to manage element ordering without relying on drag-and-drop.
- **Consistent expand/collapse model** — Section 6 establishes a single ▶/▼ toggle pattern across all sections and elements, reducing the learning curve for keyboard navigation and making expand/collapse semantics predictable for screen readers.
- **Master CV always accessible** — moving Master CV from a locked finalise-stage tab to an always-present document tab (Section 2) removes the barrier preventing keyboard users from reaching critical data-entry during earlier phases.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Hover-only controls remain critical accessibility red flags** — Sections 8 and 9 describe "floating control bars" and "floating toolbars" that appear "on hover." Hover is inaccessible to keyboard-only users, users on touch devices, and many assistive technologies. No alternative activation method (focus trigger, keyboard shortcut, or persistent button) is documented. This **replicates and amplifies the current hover-control gap** and would fail WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus).
- **Contenteditable accessibility unspecified** — Section 12 lists "contenteditable or inline textarea" for all inline edits, but provides no implementation guidance for screen-reader announcements of edit-mode entry/exit, cursor positioning, or undo availability. Contenteditable poses known accessibility risks (cursor movement, selection announcement, undo stack) that require explicit ARIA labeling and focus management, which are absent.
- **No mention of announcement strategy for accept/decline actions** — Sections 8 and 9 define ✓/✗ and ✅/❌ accept/decline buttons, but Section 4 (Analysis view) does not specify whether accepting/declining a clarification question answer or suggestion generates a live-region announcement. Screen reader users will not be notified that their action succeeded without `aria-live` support.
- **Auto-scroll and flash-highlight animations conflict with prefers-reduced-motion** — Section 7 documents "auto-scrolls to element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)" when the agent references a specific element. This violates WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3 (animation from interactions) for users with vestibular disorders or motion sensitivity; no prefers-reduced-motion alternative is provided.
- **Tab bar overflow behavior unresolved** — Section 15 (question 1) acknowledges tab-bar overflow on narrow viewports but defers the accessibility solution. Scroll buttons, overflow menus, and auto-hide patterns all require keyboard-operable alternatives and visible focus indicators (GAP-120 recurrence).
- **Contenteditable reorder mode lacks keyboard feedback** — Section 8 specifies "Enter drag-to-reorder mode," but does not document how keyboard users activate ↑↓ buttons or receive confirmation that an element has moved. Without live-region announcements of reorder success, keyboard users lack the haptic/visual feedback sighted drag users receive.

### Suggested enhancements

1. **Replace hover-only controls with focus-triggered disclosure** — Modify Sections 8 and 9 to state: "When a section or element receives keyboard focus or is hovered, the toolbar appears and remains visible until focus leaves or a toolbar action is taken. The toolbar is a `role="toolbar"` container with standard keyboard navigation (Tab to move between buttons, Enter/Space to activate)." This ensures keyboard-only users can discover and operate all controls.

2. **Document contenteditable accessibility requirements** — Add a new subsection under Section 12: "Each editable field (contenteditable or textarea) must carry an `aria-label` identifying its purpose, an `aria-describedby` linking to inline help text if complex, and an `aria-live="polite"` announce region for undo/save confirmations. Screen readers must be informed when edit mode begins and ends via live-region text such as 'Editing: Bullets section, item 2 of 5. Press Escape to exit.'"

3. **Add live-region announcements for suggestion actions** — Expand Sections 8 and 9 to include: "When a user activates ✅ Accept or ❌ Decline on a suggestion, an announcement is immediately posted to a hidden `aria-live="assertive"` region: 'Suggestion accepted. Bullet 3 updated. Press ↑ to move, Ctrl+Z to undo.' This informs screen reader users of state change and next-step keyboard options."

4. **Implement prefers-reduced-motion wrapper for animations** — Modify Section 7 to state: "When the agent references an element and the right pane auto-scrolls to it, the scroll is instant (no animation). If a visual highlight is needed, it is a static colored background (no flash or pulse) that persists for 2 seconds, or is skipped entirely if `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` is set." Provide CSS: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .element-highlight { animation: none; background-color: #fffacd; } }`.

5. **Define keyboard alternatives for tab-bar overflow** — Resolve Section 15 question 1 explicitly: "Overflow tabs are hidden behind a 'More documents' button with `aria-label="Show more documents"`. Activating it opens a dropdown menu with the remaining tab names. The dropdown is keyboard-operable (arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select). The active tab's name is always visible in the scrollable tab bar, and Tab steps through visible tabs left-to-right, then to the More button."

6. **Specify reorder confirmation via live region** — Add to Section 8 reorder behavior: "Activating ↑ or ↓ moves the element and immediately announces via live region: 'Moved up. Item 2 of 5' or 'Moved down. Item 3 of 5.' The element receives focus after move. Consecutive up/down presses are allowed without re-focusing the toolbar."

These enhancements directly resolve the critical gaps (GAP-120, GAP-72) by ensuring keyboard accessibility and screen reader awareness of all interactive controls and state changes.
```

11	**Last Updated:** 2026-04-22 10:00 ET
12	
13	**Executive Summary:** The modal and dialog layer is well-structured with focus management, ARIA roles, and Escape-key handling, but the workflow step bar and second-level tab bar are built from non-interactive `<div>` elements with no `tabindex`, making the primary navigation unreachable by keyboard. Several compounding gaps — a labelless message input, an ARIA-free confirm dialog, and missing programmatic state announcements on workflow steps — place US-X1 at a critical fail level.
14	
15	---
16	
17	## Application Evaluation
18	
19	### US-X1: Workflow Navigation Accessibility
20	
21	#### Criterion 1 — Workflow-step elements reachable and operable by keyboard
22	
23	❌ **Fail** — `web/index.html:105–119`
24	
25	All 8 workflow step pills are `<div>` elements with `onclick` handlers and no `tabindex` attribute.
26	
27	```html
28	<div class="step clickable" id="step-job" onclick="handleStepClick('job')">📥 Job Input</div>
29	<div class="step" id="step-analysis" onclick="handleStepClick('analysis')">🔍 Analysis</div>
30	<!-- × 8 steps -->
31	```
32	
33	`updateWorkflowSteps()` (`web/workflow-steps.js:660–668`) adds class `clickable` to completed steps but never sets `tabindex="0"` or `role="button"`. The ↻ re-run spans injected into completed steps (`workflow-steps.js:673`) are also plain `<span>` elements with `onclick` only — no `tabindex`, no `role="button"`.
34	
35	**Impact:** Keyboard-only users cannot reach or activate any workflow step pill or re-run button.
36	
37	#### Criterion 2 — Stage tabs expose correct tab semantics, selected state, and panel association
38	
39	⚠️ **Partial** — `web/index.html:176–196`
40	
41	The tab container has `role="tablist"` and `aria-label="Application workflow tabs"`. Every tab `<div>` carries `role="tab"`, `aria-selected`, and `aria-controls="document-content"`. `aria-selected` is toggled correctly in `switchTab()` (`web/review-table-base.js:80–87`).
42	
43	However, the tab `<div>` elements carry no `tabindex` attribute, making them non-focusable. The arrow-key handler in `ui-core.js:490–504` calls `nextTab.focus()` but a `<div>` without `tabindex` cannot receive programmatic focus — arrow-key navigation silently fails. The `aria-controls` value is `"document-content"` for all tabs (not unique panel IDs), which is a technical workaround rather than the recommended per-tab panel pattern.
44	
45	**What passes:** ARIA roles, `aria-selected` toggling, and `aria-controls` linkage are present.
46	**What fails:** Tabs are not keyboard-operable (missing `tabindex="0"`); arrow-key focus calls do not work.
47	
48	#### Criterion 3 — Active and completed states conveyed beyond colour alone
49	
50	⚠️ **Partial** — `web/styles.css:147–157`
51	
52	Step states are differentiated by background and text colour (upcoming: gray, active: blue, completed: green, stale: amber). The `.viewing` class adds a visible blue box-shadow ring, providing a non-colour indicator of current view position. The `.browsing-away` class adds a pulsing amber ring. These provide some non-colour signal.
53	
54	However, no `aria-current`, `aria-label`, or additional screen-reader text distinguishes active from completed from upcoming for screen reader users. The pill text label is identical regardless of state (`📥 Job Input` stays `📥 Job Input`). A screen reader user receives no programmatic signal of workflow position.
55	
56	#### Criterion 4 — Changes in active stage announced
57	
58	❌ **Fail** — `web/index.html:100–121`
59	
60	The `.workflow` div has no `aria-live` attribute. `updateWorkflowSteps()` mutates step classes and innerHTML but nothing announces advancement to assistive technology. (The `#document-content` panel does have `aria-live="polite"` so tab content changes are announced, but that is a separate region.)
61

64	### US-X2: Modal and Dialog Accessibility
65	
66	#### Criterion 1 — Opening a modal moves focus into it
67	
68	⚠️ **Partial** — `web/ui-core.js:239–245`, `1458–1460`; `web/session-switcher-ui.js:199–213`

The `confirmDialog()` helper (`ui-core.js:364`) never captures or redirects focus at all.
71	
72	#### Criterion 2 — Focus is trapped inside the modal while open
73	
74	✅ **Pass** — `web/ui-core.js:294–330`
75	
76	`trapFocus(modalId)` installs a keydown listener that cycles Tab/Shift+Tab within the focusable elements of the modal and is cleaned up on close. The `_showReRunConfirmModal` helper in `workflow-steps.js:171` also calls `trapFocus`.

83

85	
86	⚠️ **Gap:** `confirmDialog()` does not call `restoreFocus()` on dismiss. Focus position is lost.
87

89	
90	✅ **Pass** (static modals) / ❌ **Fail** (`confirmDialog`)

92	All static modals carry `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and `aria-labelledby`:

94	- Alert: `aria-labelledby="alert-modal-title"`, `aria-describedby="alert-modal-message"` (line 242)
95	- Ownership conflict: `aria-labelledby="ownership-conflict-title"` (line 256)

97	- Settings: `aria-labelledby="settings-modal-title"` (line 433)
98	- Re-run confirm: `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby="rerun-confirm-title"` (`workflow-steps.js:155`)

100	`confirmDialog()` (`ui-core.js:355`) creates a plain div with no `role`, `aria-modal`, or `aria-labelledby`. Its text content is not associated as a dialog description.

```text
1	<!--

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="unknown" data-tool-name="Agent"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **Agent**</summary>
Graphical Designer persona review of UI redesign

```text
---

## Graphical Designer

### What the proposed design gets right

- **"The document is the UI" thesis** — Moving the rendered CV into the center of the workflow instead of relegating it to the Layout Review tab is fundamentally sound. Editing in place within the live preview eliminates context-switching friction and preserves the "what you see is what you get" promise throughout the customization phases.

- **Inline controls over separate tabs** — The proposed hover toolbars (Section 8 & 9) and inline element-expand pattern replace the current fragmented tab-per-section navigation. This concentrates all actions (include/exclude, reorder, suggest, edit) near the elements they affect, reducing cognitive load and discoverability problems that plague the current 26-tab model.

- **Ghost-item visibility pattern** — The proposed "show hidden" badge and inline rendering of excluded elements (strikethrough, 50% opacity, dashed border) is more coherent than the current checkbox-in-a-table approach. Users immediately see the impact of inclusion/exclusion decisions on the final document layout without mental math.

- **Collapsible sections with summary badges** — The proposed section collapse/expand model ("3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions") creates scannability for dense documents and reduces visual clutter on first load, which the current expanded-by-default tables do not provide.

- **Sticky settings bar (Section 5)** — Consolidating Length, Style, ATS Score, and Regenerate into a persistent header above the CV eliminates the need to hunt for controls scattered across modals and sidebars. The radio/dropdown controls are standard web patterns and integrate naturally with the document viewer.

- **Analysis clarification questions embedded inline (Section 4)** — Moving questions from chat-only to embedded annotations adjacent to extracted requirements creates stronger context and avoids requiring users to toggle between the chat and viewer to understand what each question relates to.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline hover toolbars risk visual clutter and accidental activation** — The proposed Section 9 toolbar (10+ buttons: expand, include/exclude, move, edit, suggest, accept, decline, retry) appears on every hover. On a dense resume with 30+ bullets, this creates cognitive overload and UI flicker. The current modal-based approach feels slower but less visually chaotic. Recommendation: consider reducing visible buttons to 3–4 core actions (expand, include/exclude, move) with a "more" menu to avoid toolbar-width bloat.

- **Pending-suggestion amber boxes may conflict with the CV's visual hierarchy** — Section 10 proposes amber borders around elements with pending suggestions. On a professional resume with existing visual structure (section titles, carefully weighted typography), amber boxes could appear as editorial artifacts rather than integrated guidance. The current separate "Rewrite Review" tab keeps suggestions visually isolated from the final output, which avoids this aesthetic tension.

- **In-place contenteditable text fields may not preserve final PDF fidelity** — The proposal assumes that inline edits (contenteditable or textarea in an HTML-rendered CV) will save exactly as they will appear in the PDF. However, formatting state (bold, italic, list nesting) is easy to accidentally introduce in contenteditable and hard to validate before file generation. The current DataTable-per-section approach enforces plaintext input, which guarantees PDF fidelity. Mitigation needed: strict input validation and visual feedback showing how edited text renders in the final PDF.

- **Expanded element panel typography and whitespace may not scale** — Section 6 specifies a multi-row expanded panel ("Original", "Current", "Proposed", "Model recommendation", "ATS comments", "Persuasion comments"). On a 1920px monitor, this may fit; on a typical laptop (1366px), the expanded element grows very tall, pushing unrelated sections off-screen. Consider whether the expanded detail should use a modal/drawer instead of in-place expansion, or whether some rows should be relegated to an "advanced details" collapse.

- **No guidance on how inline editing integrates with undo** — Section 15 (Open Design Question 5) acknowledges that undo is unresolved. contenteditable undo is browser-dependent and fragile; users editing a bullet, moving an element, editing again, and then pressing Ctrl+Z may lose all three changes if the undo stack is not carefully managed. The proposal needs a concrete undo strategy (app-level undo stack, not browser-default) before implementation.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Reduce the default element hover toolbar to 3 core buttons, with a secondary "more" menu** — Keep ▼ (expand/collapse), ✗ (exclude), and ↑↓ (reorder) always visible. Tuck ✓, ✏️, ✨, ✅, ❌, 🔄 into a three-dot menu that appears on explicit interaction. This reduces visual noise on dense sections and prevents accidental clicks while scrolling.

- **Apply a subtle background tint (not an amber border) to pending-suggestion elements** — Replace the Section 10 amber border with a soft 10–15% amber background fill behind the element text. This signals "pending action" without introducing a strong graphic element that competes with the CV's typography. Add a small amber dot (6px) to the left of the element text as a secondary indicator.

- **Require explicit Save confirmation for all contenteditable fields, with a preview diff** — Before saving a bullet edit, show a side-by-side diff (original vs. edited) with a "Save" and "Cancel" button. This prevents accidental unsaved state and gives users final validation that their edit looks correct before it persists to the session. Display a green checkmark briefly on confirm (as Section 10 proposes).

- **Constrain the expanded element panel height and add an overflow scroll** — If the expanded element panel exceeds 60% of the viewport, add `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;` to the element card. This allows expanded details to be scrollable within the element without pushing the rest of the resume off-screen. Clearly mark the scrollable area with a subtle scrollbar indicator.

- **Add a "Settings" link in the sticky settings bar to control CV template font family and colour theme** — Currently (per your existing review), font family and colour are hardcoded in the template and not exposed. The proposed sticky bar should include a dropdown or icon link: "Settings → Font family (Inter/Garamond/Calibri) · Theme (Professional Blue / Warm Neutral / Bold Contrast)". This addresses the existing gap (US-G3) and gives users control over the visual output without requiring CSS knowledge.

- **Display a live word-count or page-break preview within the sticky settings bar** — The proposed "Pages: ~2.1" indicator is helpful, but adding a small visual representation (a mini page-stack icon with colour-coded warning: green ≤ 2 pages, amber 2–2.5, red > 2.5) makes the impact of length/style choices immediately obvious. Consider also adding a "View page breaks" toggle to highlight where page breaks occur in the rendered CV.
```

9	# Graphical Designer Review Status
10	
11	**Last Updated:** 2026-04-22 10:00 ET
12	
13	**Executive Summary:** The application's visual system is functionally coherent — a consistent Tailwind-inspired blue/grey palette, well-structured workflow navigation, and a clean two-panel layout deliver a usable and professional experience. The generated CV template (`cv-template.html`) is the genuine design highlight: a sophisticated two-column layout with a professional Inter/Merriweather font pairing, user-adjustable base typography via rem, and careful print/page-break controls. Primary design debt is in the app layer: no CSS design-token system (all hex values hardcoded), system-emoji navigation icons that render inconsistently across OS/browser, multiple inline-style overrides in `index.html` that bypass the CSS class system, Bootstrap-vs-custom button mixing on the Layout tab, and no user control over CV template font family or colour theme.

82	
83	## Top 5 Gaps (by Severity)
84	
85	### Gap 1 — Layout control labeling not designer-accessible (MEDIUM)
86	
87	**Evidence:** `layout-instruction.js:273–278`
88	```html
89	<label>Base font size (px):</label>
90	<input min="6" max="16" step="0.5" value="13"
91	  title="Controls the root font size for the CV. All rem-based sizes scale with this value." />
92	```
93	A non-developer who sets this to 13 cannot tell whether the output will look like 10pt or 12pt body text, because the CSS root-font-size-to-rem relationship is opaque. The tooltip is accurate but requires CSS literacy. The unit label "px" is a CSS unit, not a print unit — designers think in pt.
94	
95	---
96	
97	### Gap 2 — Button class system mixing on Layout tab (MEDIUM)
98	
99	**Evidence:** `layout-instruction.js:258, 289, 292, 308, 315, 322` use `btn btn-warning`, `btn btn-secondary`, `btn btn-primary`, `btn btn-success` (Bootstrap 5). All other tabs use `action-btn`, `action-btn primary`, `btn-primary`, `btn-secondary` (custom `styles.css` classes).
100	
101	Bootstrap 5's `.btn` has `padding:.375rem .75rem` (≈6×12px) vs. `.action-btn` with `padding:10px 16px` (10×16px). Buttons inside the layout pane are visibly smaller than action buttons in the chat panel.
102	
103	---
104	
105	### Gap 3 — Layout settings row uses inline styles (LOW)
106	
107	**Evidence:** `layout-instruction.js:271`:
108	```js
109	style="display:flex; align-items:center; gap:10px; margin-bottom:14px; padding:8px 10px; background:#f8fafc; border:1px solid #e2e8f0; border-radius:6px;"
110	```
111	This row cannot be themed from `styles.css` and will not respond to future design-system updates. Should be extracted to a named CSS class (e.g., `.layout-settings-row`).
112	
113	---
114	
115	### Gap 4 — Instruction textarea placeholder reads as developer copy (LOW)
116	
117	**Evidence:** `layout-instruction.js:294–298`
118	```
119	placeholder="e.g., Move Publications section after Skills&#10;or: Make the Summary section smaller&#10;or: Keep the Genentech entry on one page"
120	```
121	The `or:` prefix is a code-documentation convention, not natural user guidance language. The examples are technically accurate but feel like developer-written documentation rather than in-product guidance.
122	
123	---
124	
125	### Gap 5 — "Confirm Layout" button duplicated with no visual disambiguation (LOW)
126	
127	**Evidence:** `layout-instruction.js:307–310 and 320–323`
128	Two identical `<button>Confirm Layout</button>` elements appear — one above and one below the instruction history, both sharing the same green `btn btn-success` style. First-time users may be confused about whether both must be clicked. There is no visual hint (e.g., secondary label, anchor icon) that the second is a scroll-convenience duplicate.
129	
130	---

135	> As a graphical designer, I want layout controls to display values in designer-familiar units (pt for font size, in for margins) and show a live equivalence note (e.g., "≈ 10pt body text") so I can make informed typographic decisions without CSS knowledge.
136	
137	**Proposed US-G5:**
138	> As a graphical designer, I want the layout instruction textarea to show user-friendly placeholder examples that demonstrate natural language input so that users understand the kind of language the system accepts.
139	
140	**Proposed US-G6:**

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
