Resume Expert persona review of UI redesign

```text
## Resume Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Eliminates context-switching penalty** — The "document is the UI" thesis moves final resume rendering from the isolated Layout Review tab into the CV tab itself, allowing users to edit bullets and skills while seeing live output. This directly addresses the pain point of "editing bullets gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document."

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Positioning questions adjacent to the analysis data they relate to (e.g., "years of ML experience" appearing next to "Machine Learning" requirement) reduces the friction of bouncing between chat and analysis data. This is a significant upgrade to understanding the job context.

- **Expanded element panel with original/current/proposed comparison** — The multi-row detail panel (Section 6) surfaces all three versions of a piece of content in one place. For resume strategy, this is critical: users can now see what they started with (original), what they've edited (current), and what the AI recommends (proposed) without tab-switching.

- **Ghost item reveal pattern for excluded content** — Section 11's "show hidden (N)" approach keeps the excluded/hidden resume content visible in grayed, struck-through state within the section. This preserves context and prevents the dangerous situation where a user forgets they excluded a strong bullet.

- **Section-level bulk actions with explicit accept/decline** — Section 8's "Accept all" and "Decline all" buttons (with prominent toolbar placement) make it possible to act on suggestions quickly. However, this raises a safety concern addressed below.

- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Unlocking Master CV from the finalise-only restriction (GAP-41) allows users to correct source data mid-session without waiting for the end.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Bulk-accept safety risk** — The "Accept all" button on section headers (Section 8) accepts all pending suggestions in a section with one click. For Experience bullets or Skills, this is dangerous: an LLM batch suggestion may contain subtle errors (e.g., keyword placement, terminology inconsistency from US-R3) that require per-item review. The current Rewrite Review tab forces explicit per-item decisions. Recommend adding a confirmation modal ("This will accept N suggestions") or demoting bulk-accept to a less prominent secondary option.

- **Formatting preservation during in-place editing unclear** — Section 12 specifies that bullet text is "editable in-place" (contenteditable or inline textarea). The concern: when a user edits a bullet, what ensures resume formatting conventions are preserved? If a user deletes a line break or removes the implicit parenthetical context of a sub-skill, will the edited text break formatting? Current design is silent on validation or guidance (e.g., "Keep this under 85 characters"). Current implementation (web/rewrite-review.js) enforces constraints via review UI, not in-place inline editing.

- **Missing severity sort in spell-check integration** — Section 13 shows flagged text by hover-over underline, but does not commit to sorting critical misspellings before minor style suggestions (per current review GAP on US-R7, Section 115). If spell issues are shown in order-received, a user might miss a name typo while addressing comma placement.

- **ATS comments row lacks synonym grouping context** — Section 6 mentions "ATS comments — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues" in the expanded element panel. The current review (US-R1, Section 36) flags that synonyms (ML / Machine Learning) are not grouped visually. This proposal does not clarify whether ATS comments will show grouped keyword matches (canonical ↔ alias) or remain ungrouped as they are today.

- **CV style switcher clarity — Sidebar vs Plain/ATS** — Section 5's style dropdown offers "Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]". The term "Plain/ATS" is ambiguous: does it mean a plain-text ATS-friendly style, or a third style? The current app (web/rewrite-review.js context) uses style profiles that may have different rendering. The proposal should clarify which styles are available and how they differ in the generated output.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a confirmation modal for "Accept all" actions** — Before accepting all N suggestions in a section, show a dialog: "Accept all N suggestions in [Section]?" with options to "Review each" (return to current flow), "Accept all", or "Cancel". This preserves the bulk-action speed while preventing accidental acceptance of borderline proposals.

- **Validate in-place edits against resume conventions** — When a user edits a bullet in-place, provide real-time or on-blur validation: line-length warning (ideal: 70–85 chars), fragment check (does this look like a resume bullet?), and keyword consistency check (does the edited text introduce a new tool term that should appear elsewhere?). Surface these as non-blocking warnings ("⚠ This bullet is X chars — consider shortening") rather than hard blocks.

- **Sort spell-check issues by severity before display** — In Section 13, commit to sorting flagged text: priority 1 = spelling errors (name/company misspellings), priority 2 = grammar/fragment issues in non-bullet context, priority 3 = stylistic suggestions. Implement this in the inline spell-check popover by re-sorting issues on render.

- **Add a "Grouped Keywords" view to ATS comments** — In the expanded element panel (Section 6, "ATS comments" row), group keyword matches by canonical term and show aliases: e.g. **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]. This directly closes the current GAP (US-R1, Section 36) and helps users understand why the ATS is matching their skills to the job.

- **Clarify CV style switcher with previews** — Update Section 5's style dropdown: include a radio option "Show style preview" or "Compare styles" that renders the current section in both Sidebar and Plain/ATS side-by-side in a collapsible preview pane. This removes ambiguity about which style is best for the target ATS and allows users to make informed choices.

- **Preserve section-expand state across tab switches** — In Section 6, specify that when a user switches from the CV tab to (e.g.) the Job tab and back, the section expand/collapse state is remembered per session. This prevents the annoyance of re-expanding a section you were working on. Store state in sessionStorage keyed on section name.

 `./tasks/ui-redesign-proposal.md`

```text
1	<!--

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295
```

Hiring Manager persona review of UI redesign

```text
Now I'll write the structured review from the hiring manager persona's perspective, focusing on CV output quality, visual appearance, and professional standards.

## Hiring Manager

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live preview throughout customisation** — The CV is always visible in the right pane while editing, eliminating the context-switching problem that forces users to guess how bullets appear in the final document. This directly addresses the hiring manager's primary concern: seeing a well-formatted, role-tailored resume before submission.

- **In-place inline editing preserves document integrity** — Rather than abstracting content into separate DataTables (Experience, Bullets, Skills tabs), the "document is the UI" thesis keeps all edits within the visual context of the rendered resume. Users see immediately when a rewritten bullet becomes too long, when a skill addition disrupts visual balance, or when section headings are malformed.

- **Ghost-style hidden elements solve a credibility risk** — Excluded bullets appear as muted strikethrough within their section when revealed, preventing the accidental submission of incomplete job entries (only 1 accepted bullet per job). This catches the current GAP-HM-01 silent failure and makes inclusion decisions visually explicit.

- **Sticky settings bar for output control** — The Length / Style / ATS / Pages controls are always accessible without tab-switching. The style dropdown (Sidebar vs. ATS Plain) is critical: hiring managers receive either a polished human-readable version or an ATS-optimized plain-text variant, with visual feedback on which is active.

- **Embedded clarification questions in Analysis view** — Moving job-analysis questions from chat-only to inline next to their analysis data (e.g., "years of ML experience" question appearing within the Requirements section) reduces ambiguity and keeps the analysis rationale transparent.

- **Element expansion panels provide decision context** — Each bullet/skill/publication expands to show Original (master data), Current (edited version), Proposed (LLM suggestion), Model recommendation badge, ATS comments, and Persuasion score. This four-sided view is far richer than the current Rewrite Review tab's simple before/after.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks accidental quality degradation** — The proposal makes *all* CV content editable in-place (contenteditable or inline textarea). Unlike the current tab-based model where changes happen in a controlled environment, inline editing can introduce formatting errors (stray newlines, copy-paste artifacts) that users may not notice until Download. The proposed design must enforce strong autosave + undo, and ideally a "Preview as PDF" step before Download.

- **No mention of final validation gates before export** — The current design fires validation warnings at the Download tab (page count, persuasion acknowledgment, etc.). The proposal does not specify whether these gates remain, move to a new "Export Review" modal, or are surfaced as persistent warnings in the settings bar. If warnings shift to inline (e.g., amber border on a section), users may dismiss them casually instead of reading the message.

- **Master CV tab always-present may create version-control confusion** — Currently, Master CV is locked until the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), preventing mid-workflow overwrites. The proposal exposes Master CV as an always-available tab with "explicit Save confirmation" but does not define: (a) whether edits to Master CV persist across sessions, (b) whether a user can revert to their previous Master CV state, (c) how to prevent accidental overwrite of a working master if the user makes an exploratory edit and clicks Save. This is a regression if Master CV edits are not reversible.

- **No specification for style-switcher state persistence** — If a user selects "ATS Plain" in the settings bar and then navigates to another document tab (Analysis, Cover Letter), does the style persist when they return to the CV tab? If the user downloads twice (once in Sidebar, once in ATS), is there a risk of version mismatch if they only notice the style mismatch after sending one version?

- **Drag-to-reorder accessibility deferred** — Section 15 (Open Design Questions) calls out that keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag, but the proposal does not yet define this. For hiring managers, reorder errors (e.g., most-relevant job moved to second position) are high-stakes. The keyboard alternative must be first-class, not an afterthought.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a pre-Download validation checklist modal** — Before entering the Download workflow, prompt the user to confirm: (1) page count is 2–3 pages (with visual indicator), (2) persuasion warnings (weak verbs, single-bullet jobs) are acknowledged, (3) no inline edits are pending save, (4) spell-check issues are resolved. This preserves the current safety gates but integrates them into the new flow without breaking immersion.

- **Implement a "Preview as PDF" button in the settings bar** — Alongside "Regenerate Preview," add a button that opens a real PDF preview in a modal or new tab before Download. This catches formatting errors, widow/orphan words, and page-break surprises that HTML rendering may not catch. This is especially critical because inline contenteditable editing can introduce soft-break artifacts.

- **Mark Master CV edits with a "dirty" indicator and require explicit confirmation** — If Master CV is always accessible, add a visual indicator (e.g., red dot on the tab, "Unsaved changes" warning) when the user has made edits to Master CV fields. Require an explicit "Save to Master CV" confirmation (not just a blur save) to prevent accidental overwrites. Ideally, log the timestamp and old value of any Master CV change for auditability.

- **Add a "Revert to Session Start" option for CV edits** — Since inline editing can cascade (rewrite one bullet, which then affects keyword scoring, which then affects skills priority), provide a quick "Revert all CV changes" button (in the settings bar or a modal) to restore the CV to the state it was in when the user entered the Customisation phase. This is a safety valve if inline edits go wrong mid-workflow.

- **Specify style-switcher behavior and provide a visual badge** — When the user switches from "Sidebar" to "ATS Plain" in the settings bar, the badge should prominently display the active style (e.g., "Style: Sidebar ▾" → "Style: ATS Plain ▾" with background color change). On Download, the filename should include the style (e.g., `resume_ATS.pdf` vs. `resume_Sidebar.pdf`). This prevents version-confusion mistakes.

- **Integrate page-count warnings into the settings bar directly** — Instead of relying on a modal or separate validation step, show the page-count badge in the sticky settings bar with live color feedback (green ≤2 pages, amber 2–2.5 pages, red >2.5 pages). Include a tooltip explaining the warning threshold so users understand the hiring manager preference without reading external docs.
```
</details></tool-use>

Now I'll write a structured review from the Applicant persona, addressing the workflow efficiency, ease of use, and whether the redesign reduces effort needed to produce a good tailored CV.

---

## Applicant

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live context preservation** — Seeing the CV rendered throughout the workflow (not just at Layout Review) finally closes the gap between editing suggestions in isolation and understanding their impact on the actual document. This directly addresses the current "no sense of the whole" pain point.

- **Inline decision-making** — Element hover toolbars with accept/reject/edit buttons eliminate the mental context-switching burden of jumping between a Rewrite Review tab and the final output. I can now see a rewrite suggestion, evaluate it against the rendered context, and act on it without leaving my view.

- **Ghost elements and inclusion visibility** — Excluded items shown inline with strikethrough and reduced opacity finally make it clear what's *not* going into the CV during the customisation phase. This reduces the risk of accidentally omitting important achievements while also preventing accidental inclusion of irrelevant ones.

- **Embedded clarification questions** — Moving questions from chat-only to inline within the Analysis view (e.g., a gap-detection question appearing next to the "Machine Learning" requirement) is a major usability win. Questions are now paired with the analysis data they relate to, not buried in conversation history.

- **Always-available Master CV tab** — Unlocking Master CV edit access from the finalise-only gate means I can update my baseline data (fix typos, add new skills) at any moment, rather than being forced to wait until the end of a session or park the application to do maintenance.

- **Consistent section/element expansion model** — The two-state collapse/expand pattern (collapsed → summary badge; expanded → full detail) is predictable and reduces overwhelm when facing 20+ experience bullets or 30+ skills. The summary badges give me a quick inventory without forcing me to read everything.

---

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Performance and interactivity risk** — The proposed design requires real-time rendering of the full CV with inline hover toolbars, contenteditable fields, and inline spell-check underlines. The current tab-based model defers rendering until needed. If the live preview lags or becomes sluggish as the CV grows, the entire interaction model feels broken. No performance baseline is proposed; this is a high-risk assumption.

- **Conflation of editing surfaces** — The proposal merges Master CV, Job description, Analysis, and CV in one right-pane viewer with different interaction models (Master CV requires Save confirmation; CV changes are immediate). This multiplies the complexity of understanding which edits are safe, which require confirmation, and which affect which downstream data. The current separation, while fragmented, makes these boundaries explicit.

- **Loss of comparison workflow in Rewrite Review** — The current before/after card UI with word-level diff highlighting (✅ Pass in US-A4) is completely absent from the proposal. The new inline "Proposed" text field within an expanded element panel loses the visual diff comparison that currently helps me judge the rewrite's magnitude. I see old text and new text, but not what *changed*.

- **Lack of workflow progression feedback** — The current step header with horizontal pills shows at a glance where I am in the 8-phase workflow and how much is left. The proposal mentions moving to a "compact top bar" or "collapsible left-sidebar strip" but provides no concrete UX. Without a clear milestone indicator, I may lose confidence in how far through the application I've progressed, especially on longer sessions.

---

### Suggested enhancements

- **Prototype and performance-test the inline edit model** — Before committing to in-place contenteditable fields and live hover toolbar rendering, validate that the browser's DOM rendering and your text-diffing logic can keep up with a 500+ bullet CV. Offer a fallback "modal edit" mode for elements that are expensive to render inline, so the inline model doesn't degrade user experience.

- **Preserve the word-level diff for rewrites** — When an element has a "Proposed" rewrite, show the before/after with LCS word-diff highlighting (removed text in red, added text in green) alongside the inline textarea. This maintains the current rewrite-review fidelity without requiring a separate tab.

- **Add explicit "Master CV Save" confirmation modal** — The proposal states Master CV edits "require an explicit Save," but doesn't specify the UX. Make it visually distinct from CV session changes: a modal diff preview ("You're about to update your Master CV profile with these changes") before write, matching the pre-harvest-write diff review that's missing from US-A11.

- **Define workflow phase indicators** — Clarify how the applicant knows which phase they're in when the right pane is full of content. Propose a sticky breadcrumb in the left-pane chat header ("Phase: Customisation › Experience › Bullet 3") or a subtle badge on the primary section being worked on. Without this, the workflow feels directionless.

- **Specify keyboard navigation for section/element expand** — The proposal mentions ▶/▼ togles but doesn't define keyboard shortcuts. Applicants using keyboard-only (or accessibility tools) need consistent bindings: e.g., `Ctrl+Space` to expand/collapse focused element, `Tab` to move between elements, `Ctrl+Enter` to save inline edits.

- **Add a "changes since last re-run" persistent badge** — The current review's US-A12 gap (delta highlighting is transient) remains unfixed in the proposal. After a re-run, changed/new elements should have a lasting orange "new" badge (not just a 2.5 s flash) so I can quickly scan which items were affected by the re-analysis without manually comparing.

9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295
```

Now I'll write a structured HR/ATS specialist review comparing the current design to the proposed redesign.

---

## HR / ATS Specialist

### What the proposed design gets right

- **ATS Score badge and drill-down in settings bar** — Moving the ATS score to a sticky "Settings Bar" (Section 5) keeps ATS compliance visibility constant while scrolling, eliminating the current "Compute ATS Score" empty-state button that users overlook. Clicking opens a drill-down modal, which directly addresses the current hidden-by-default behavior.

- **Keyword highlighting in Job view** — The "Job Description View" (Section 3) adds amber highlighting for matched terms and red for missing required keywords. This directly teaches users which job terms the CV already covers and what gaps remain—critical for hard-requirement compliance before customization begins.

- **ATS comments in expanded element panel** — The proposed "Element States" (Section 6) embed **"ATS comments — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues"** directly within the expanded element detail panel. This is a major improvement: users making editorial decisions see ATS impact alongside persuasion and model recommendation in one place, rather than hunting between the "ATS Report" button and the text itself.

- **Plain/ATS style option clarity in settings bar** — The "Style" dropdown (Section 5) explicitly lists "Plain/ATS" as a selectable rendering mode, replacing the current scattered approach. Users can toggle between human-readable (Sidebar) and ATS-safe layout inline, making the tradeoff visible.

- **Hard-requirement keyword coverage now visible inline** — By collapsing sections to show summary badges (e.g., *"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"*), users at a glance see how many elements are included per section. Expanding individual elements and reading ATS comments together creates a direct pathway to asking: *"Do my included bullets cover the hard requirements?"*

- **Master CV always accessible** — The "Master CV" tab (Section 2) is no longer locked to the `finalise` stage. This enables users to update the underlying data at any time, reducing re-work and ensuring consistent skill classification across sessions.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks ATS-safe formatting** — The proposed in-place editing model (Section 12) allows users to edit bullet text, skills, and summary directly in the rendered CV view. If the ATS DOCX generation blindly copies edited text without re-normalizing formatting (e.g., removing bold/italic runs, ensuring single-column layout), inline edits could introduce formatting artifacts that break ATS parsing. The current design's separate tab-based review reduces this risk because bulk generation and validation happen in a controlled batch step.

- **ATS validation gate missing in proposed workflow** — The current "File Review" tab enforces a 17-check validation report and blocks downloads on failures. The proposed design mentions "Download & Validate" (Section 2) but does not detail how the validation report integrates into the new CV view or whether the checks still gate downloads. If validation is deferred to a separate step after CV editing is complete, users may not discover downstream ATS failures until too late.

- **Spell-check underline could interfere with ATS scoring** — The proposed "Spell Check Integration" (Section 13) renders red/blue underlines inline on the CV view. If these underlines or their associated metadata (e.g., suggestion popover HTML) leak into the DOCX export, they could corrupt the ATS text extraction or introduce unexpected characters into keyword matching.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add an ATS safety mode toggle in the settings bar** — Alongside the "Style" dropdown (Plain/ATS), add a checkbox: **"ATS Safe Editing — disable inline formatting; reject HTML-rich edits."** When enabled, contenteditable fields strip formatting on blur, and the settings bar shows a reminder: *"Inline edits will be normalized for ATS compliance."* This gives users explicit control over the risk/benefit tradeoff.

- **Embed ATS validation status in the settings bar** — Extend the sticky settings bar (Section 5) to include a "Validation Status" badge (green ✓ / amber ⚠ / red ✗) that updates live as users edit. Display the count of failing checks: *"3 issues: font name, 15+ keywords unchecked, overlapping dates."* Clicking opens the full 17-check report. This ensures the validation gate remains visible throughout the CV view, not relegated to a separate tab.

- **Add a "Hard Requirements Coverage" widget to the Analysis view** — In the Analysis View (Section 4), after the embedded clarification questions, add a dedicated widget showing: **Hard Required Keywords: [matched count] / [total count]**, with a red warning if coverage < 100%. Each unmatched keyword should link to a section where users can add it (e.g., *"Click to add 'Kubernetes' to the Technical Skills section"*). This makes the hard-requirement compliance task concrete and actionable.

- **Clarify the ATS DOCX export path from inline edits** — The proposal does not explain how changes made via in-place editing in the CV view are serialized into the ATS DOCX. Document a clear rule: *"When a user edits a bullet or skill inline, that change is immediately persisted to session state. On ATS generation, all text is re-normalized (formatting stripped, line breaks standardized) before export."* Include a validation check that compares the ATS DOCX text to the edited session state to detect formatting corruption.

- **Define synonym / variant handling in ATS comments** — The current ATS review (hr-ats.md) flags that `compute_ats_score` uses `synonym_map.json` but `validate_ats_report` does not (GAP-H-E). The ATS comments field (Section 6) should note when a keyword is matched via synonym (e.g., *"Matched as: 'ML' variant of 'Machine Learning'"*), and the validation gate should apply the same synonym rules to avoid false negatives.

- **Add a "Missing Keywords" panel to the element expand state** — When a user expands an element (e.g., a bullet), and the ATS comments note missing hard-requirement keywords, auto-suggest insertion points: *"This bullet mentions DevOps but not Terraform. Consider appending: '… using Terraform and containerization.'* Users can accept the suggestion inline or manually edit. This bridges the gap between "seeing a problem" and "acting on it."
```

Now I'll provide a structured first-time user review of the proposed redesign, comparing it to the current state assessment.

---

## First-Time User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document context during editing** — The "Document is the UI" principle directly addresses the current design's worst gap (US-F3.2 fail): users will finally see how their edits appear in the actual CV rather than working blind in isolated tabs. This transforms the workflow from abstract to concrete.

- **Inline suggestion acceptance eliminates tab-switching fatigue** — Instead of toggling between "Rewrites" and "Generated CV" tabs, users see pending suggestions (amber border) *in place* and can accept/decline/regenerate without leaving context. This substantially improves discoverability compared to today's "Rewrite Review tab, separate from output" pattern.

- **Master CV always accessible** — Removing the finalise-stage lock (GAP-41) lets users update master data at any time, not just at the end. This is a significant usability win for professionals managing their own data.

- **Collapsible expand/collapse model is learnable** — The two-state pattern (collapsed one-liner → expanded detail panel) is consistent across sections and elements, reducing cognitive load compared to today's 26 tabs. A user learns it once and applies it everywhere.

- **Ghost items (excluded elements in-place) clarify inclusion decisions** — Showing strikethrough/muted excluded items *within the section* (not in a hidden sidebar) makes the include/exclude decision visible in context, directly fixing the current fragmentation gap.

- **Embedded clarification questions in Analysis view** — Moving questions from chat-only to adjacent-to-relevant-data solves the current "buried in chat" problem and lets users answer inline without scrolling away.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Toolbar proliferation risks cognitive overwhelm** — The proposed element hover toolbar has 9+ buttons (expand, include/exclude, reorder, edit, suggest, accept, decline, retry). A first-time user encountering this on their first bullet point may freeze. The current tab UI, while fragmented, is at least less visually dense. **Proposal mitigation needed:** confirm that secondary/context-dependent buttons (e.g., retry only if a suggestion failed) are truly hidden or deprioritized in the UI mock.

- **No persistent help entry point** — The proposal does not mention onboarding, help, or persistent "?" access after the user dismisses the welcome modal. The current review (GAP-FT-3) flags this; the redesign should include a Help toggle or onboarding reminder that surfaces inline when a user encounters an unfamiliar control (e.g., "first time seeing ghost items?" tooltip).

- **Settings bar competes for cognitive real estate with the CV** — The sticky settings bar (Length, Style, ATS Score, Regenerate buttons) occupies valuable vertical space on an already-dense document view. For users on smaller screens or narrower splits, this may push CV content far down. **Test required:** How does this look at 1366×768 (laptop) or 1920×1080 (desktop)?

- **Expand/collapse state persistence is underspecified** — Section 6 and open question 3 raise ambiguity: do expanded element panels persist if the user switches tabs and returns? Or do they always reset? A first-time user who expands several bullets, switches to Screening, then returns may be frustrated if all their expansions collapsed. **Proposal action:** Clarify state persistence and document it in the spec.

- **Preview vs. Final output distinction is not yet addressed** — The current design's critical failure (US-F3.2 fail: users cannot distinguish a preview CV from final output) is *not mentioned* in the proposal. The proposal shows a CV view and a Regenerate button but never says "this is a preview until you confirm layout" or equivalent. **Risk:** The new design repeats the old mistake.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a "Preview/Final" label and stage-transition prompt in the CV View settings bar** — Place a badge near the page count indicator: "🔄 Preview mode — confirm layout to finalize" when the layout is stale, "✅ Layout confirmed — ready to download" when fresh. On stale→fresh transition, inject a brief modal: "Your layout is confirmed. You can now download final files or continue refining."

- **Create a three-tier help system** — (1) Inline tooltips for inline controls (e.g., hover over ghost item → "Excluded items appear grayed out; click ✓ to include"). (2) A persistent Help toggle (?) in the top-right corner or left sidebar footer that opens a "Workflow Overview" panel. (3) A "Tips" badge on first-encounter controls (e.g., "first time expanding an element?" with a brief animation).

- **Implement button visibility tiers in the element toolbar** — Show only essential buttons by default (expand, include/exclude, ✏️ edit). Secondary buttons (reorder, suggest, retry) appear only on hover-over-hover or within the expanded panel. This reduces initial cognitive load for first-time users while keeping advanced controls discoverable.

- **Add confirmation feedback for in-place edits on Master CV** — The proposal states Master CV changes "require an explicit Save confirmation" but does not specify UI feedback. First-time users need clear confirmation that they saved (green checkmark, toast message, or persistent "Save" button state). Without this, they may fear data loss.

- **Include a "You've completed X. Next up: Y" stage-transition message** — The current design (US-F2.3 caveat) lacks this; the proposal should inject a brief agent message when the user confirms layout: "Layout confirmed. You can now review the final files in the File Review tab or download directly." This bridges the current gap (no message guides the next step).

- **Explicitly surface ATS score trend or confidence** — The proposal mentions "ATS Score: 87%" in the settings bar but does not say whether this updates live or only on explicit regenerate. For a first-time user, "87%" is a point-in-time mystery; add context: "ATS Score: 87% (based on current CV)" and a note "Click to see which keywords are matched/missing" (see Section 5 control). This makes the score feel actionable, not arbitrary.

---

**Overall Assessment:** The proposal substantially improves the current design's worst pain point (preview/context visibility) and eliminates tab-fatigue through inline controls. However, it introduces visual density risks and does not yet address the preview-vs-final gap. With the six enhancements above, this design will be navigable and even intuitive for first-time users; without them, the learning curve remains steep.

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │

74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.

77

79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |

83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.

92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.

98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation

109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)

115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │

128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |

137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147

149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.

168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)

179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190

193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227

229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237

240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
