8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295

Now I'll write a structured Power User review of the proposed design.

---

## Power User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Persistent resume visibility** — The proposed CV View keeps the actual document visible at all times during customization, rewrite, and spell-check phases, eliminating the current workflow where edits happen blind until Layout Review. This directly solves a major power-user pain point: understanding how each decision affects the final output.

- **In-place element controls eliminate tab churn** — Hover toolbars and expand panels on each element (Section 9, Element-Level Controls) replace the current DataTable-per-tab model. For a power user processing 5–10 applications per week, eliminating the tab-switch cost (click tab → find row → click button → return) is a meaningful efficiency gain.

- **Section-level batch actions** — The proposed "Accept all", "Decline all", and "Suggest section" controls on section headers (Section 8) provide the bulk-review path that the current UI lacks for rewrites and publications. If click-once activates all pending suggestions in a section, this is faster than per-element clicking.

- **Inline editing across all document types** — The proposal allows edits to bullets, skills, cover letter text, and screening responses directly on the rendered document (Section 12). No intermediate "save to DataTable" step; changes are session-immediate. For power users, this feels more responsive.

- **Auto-tab switching as workflow context** — The auto-switching between Job, Analysis, and CV tabs as phases advance (Section 2) reduces the mental overhead of "which tab should I be in now?" — the UI anticipates the next logical view. Users can override by clicking, so autonomy is preserved.

- **Ghost-style excluded elements stay visible** — Showing excluded/hidden items with strikethrough and muted opacity (Section 11) inside the section keeps them in context. The current DataTable hides them unless you check a filter. Power users can now see at a glance what's been ruled out and why, without a toggle hunt.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Hover-only controls still risk discoverability** — The proposal replaces DataTable bulk toolbars with hover toolbars on section headers and elements (Sections 8–9). While hover-on-element is natural, hover-on-section-header for "Accept all" is not immediately obvious. A power user unfamiliar with the new design may miss that section headers are interactive. The current UI's always-visible "✨ Accept All Recommended" toolbar is actually more discoverable, despite the tab-switching tax.

- **No keyboard shortcuts mentioned** — The redesign is completely silent on keyboard acceleration. The current review identifies "zero keyboard shortcuts" as the #1 power-user gap. The proposed design does nothing to address this: there are no Alt+A, Alt+→, Alt+↓ bindings mentioned for accept/decline/move actions. For a high-throughput user, this is a significant regression if the implementation relies entirely on mouse hover.

- **Auto-tab switching may disrupt keyboard-driven workflows** — If a user is reviewing elements via keyboard (pressing ↓ to move through bullets, pressing E to expand/edit, etc.) and the auto-switch logic fires (e.g., "workflow advanced, switching to Cover Letter tab"), focus is lost and keyboard flow is broken. No mention is made of how focus is managed or whether auto-switch can be disabled. This directly conflicts with the stated power-user need for keyboard-driven workflows.

- **Expand/collapse UX for 30+ items** — The proposal uses a universal expand/collapse model (Section 6): sections are collapsed by default, showing a one-line summary badge ("3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"). For a researcher with 50+ publications or a senior engineer with 15+ experiences, collapsing sections by default may actually increase navigation overhead. Users must expand each section, then expand elements within, then collapse them again. The current DataTable, once filtered, keeps all rows visible at once. A full-text search on a DataTable row can find a single bullet in seconds; the proposed expand-then-search may be slower.

- **Inline editing on contenteditable elements introduces UX friction** — Section 12 mentions that all edits are "contenteditable or inline textarea" with save-on-blur. The proposal also notes "Undo — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough?" (Section 15). This is a real problem: contenteditable is notoriously fragile across browsers. A power user who relies on Ctrl+Z to undo rapid-fire edits will have a worse experience if the undo behavior is unpredictable. The current DataTable uses native form inputs, which have solid undo support.

- **No bulk-selection loss** — The current DataTable supports multi-row selection (checkbox column, select-all-visible header checkbox). The proposal does not mention per-element checkboxes or a "select all" affordance. If a power user wants to select and act on a subset of elements that do not fit the section-level "Accept all" model (e.g., "accept all skills in the Python category"), the proposed design offers no path. The section-level controls are coarse-grained.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add keyboard shortcuts for all hover-toolbar actions** — Implement Alt+A for "Accept this element", Alt+D for "Decline", Alt+↓ for "Move down", Alt+E for "Expand", etc. Bind these at the element level so they apply to the currently focused element (via Tab navigation). Document in a persistent keyboard help overlay (? key, discoverable from settings). This directly addresses the #1 power-user gap and makes the hover-only UI tolerable.

- **Make hover-toolbar buttons visible at rest, with opacity muting** — Instead of pure hover-reveal, render section header and element toolbars at ~30% opacity at rest, increasing to 100% on hover. This maintains the current design's clean visual hierarchy while making the affordance discoverable without accidental interaction. Reduces discoverability friction without adding clutter.

- **Add a "flat list" or "DataTable" view toggle for high-item sections** — For sections with 15+ items (publications, achievements), provide a checkbox-based DataTable view alongside the expand/collapse model. Power users can switch between "rendered view" (for final output preview) and "table view" (for bulk selection and filtering). This preserves the DataTable's speed and multi-row selection while keeping the proposal's in-place editing model as the default.

- **Implement explicit focus management and optional auto-tab-switch disable** — When the workflow phase advances and the auto-switch fires, set focus to the newly-switched tab's first interactive element (e.g., first section header or first element). Provide a Settings toggle: "Auto-switch document tabs on workflow phase change". For keyboard-driven users, auto-switch can be disabled while preserving manual tab clicking.

- **Add a "collapse all" button at the top of the CV view** — When reviewing a section with many expanded elements, provide a "Collapse all" button in the sticky settings bar. This saves users from clicking the collapse icon on every element. Paired with a "Expand all" button for sections where reviewing all details at once is necessary.

- **Expose "inline edit mode" via keyboard shortcut and preserve undo natively** — Bind Ctrl+E (or I) to enter inline edit mode on the currently focused element. Use a native `<textarea>` instead of contenteditable for all editable fields, which gives users predictable Ctrl+Z undo. If visual formatting (e.g., strikethrough on ghost items) is needed, wrap the textarea in a styled container rather than relying on contenteditable. This solves the undo-unpredictability issue while keeping inline editing fast.

---

## Graphical Designer

### What the proposed design gets right

- **"The document is the UI" thesis** — Moving the rendered CV into the center of the workflow instead of relegating it to the Layout Review tab is fundamentally sound. Editing in place within the live preview eliminates context-switching friction and preserves the "what you see is what you get" promise throughout the customization phases.

- **Inline controls over separate tabs** — The proposed hover toolbars (Section 8 & 9) and inline element-expand pattern replace the current fragmented tab-per-section navigation. This concentrates all actions (include/exclude, reorder, suggest, edit) near the elements they affect, reducing cognitive load and discoverability problems that plague the current 26-tab model.

- **Ghost-item visibility pattern** — The proposed "show hidden" badge and inline rendering of excluded elements (strikethrough, 50% opacity, dashed border) is more coherent than the current checkbox-in-a-table approach. Users immediately see the impact of inclusion/exclusion decisions on the final document layout without mental math.

- **Collapsible sections with summary badges** — The proposed section collapse/expand model ("3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions") creates scannability for dense documents and reduces visual clutter on first load, which the current expanded-by-default tables do not provide.

- **Sticky settings bar (Section 5)** — Consolidating Length, Style, ATS Score, and Regenerate into a persistent header above the CV eliminates the need to hunt for controls scattered across modals and sidebars. The radio/dropdown controls are standard web patterns and integrate naturally with the document viewer.

- **Analysis clarification questions embedded inline (Section 4)** — Moving questions from chat-only to embedded annotations adjacent to extracted requirements creates stronger context and avoids requiring users to toggle between the chat and viewer to understand what each question relates to.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline hover toolbars risk visual clutter and accidental activation** — The proposed Section 9 toolbar (10+ buttons: expand, include/exclude, move, edit, suggest, accept, decline, retry) appears on every hover. On a dense resume with 30+ bullets, this creates cognitive overload and UI flicker. The current modal-based approach feels slower but less visually chaotic. Recommendation: consider reducing visible buttons to 3–4 core actions (expand, include/exclude, move) with a "more" menu to avoid toolbar-width bloat.

- **Pending-suggestion amber boxes may conflict with the CV's visual hierarchy** — Section 10 proposes amber borders around elements with pending suggestions. On a professional resume with existing visual structure (section titles, carefully weighted typography), amber boxes could appear as editorial artifacts rather than integrated guidance. The current separate "Rewrite Review" tab keeps suggestions visually isolated from the final output, which avoids this aesthetic tension.

- **In-place contenteditable text fields may not preserve final PDF fidelity** — The proposal assumes that inline edits (contenteditable or textarea in an HTML-rendered CV) will save exactly as they will appear in the PDF. However, formatting state (bold, italic, list nesting) is easy to accidentally introduce in contenteditable and hard to validate before file generation. The current DataTable-per-section approach enforces plaintext input, which guarantees PDF fidelity. Mitigation needed: strict input validation and visual feedback showing how edited text renders in the final PDF.

- **Expanded element panel typography and whitespace may not scale** — Section 6 specifies a multi-row expanded panel ("Original", "Current", "Proposed", "Model recommendation", "ATS comments", "Persuasion comments"). On a 1920px monitor, this may fit; on a typical laptop (1366px), the expanded element grows very tall, pushing unrelated sections off-screen. Consider whether the expanded detail should use a modal/drawer instead of in-place expansion, or whether some rows should be relegated to an "advanced details" collapse.

- **No guidance on how inline editing integrates with undo** — Section 15 (Open Design Question 5) acknowledges that undo is unresolved. contenteditable undo is browser-dependent and fragile; users editing a bullet, moving an element, editing again, and then pressing Ctrl+Z may lose all three changes if the undo stack is not carefully managed. The proposal needs a concrete undo strategy (app-level undo stack, not browser-default) before implementation.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Reduce the default element hover toolbar to 3 core buttons, with a secondary "more" menu** — Keep ▼ (expand/collapse), ✗ (exclude), and ↑↓ (reorder) always visible. Tuck ✓, ✏️, ✨, ✅, ❌, 🔄 into a three-dot menu that appears on explicit interaction. This reduces visual noise on dense sections and prevents accidental clicks while scrolling.

- **Apply a subtle background tint (not an amber border) to pending-suggestion elements** — Replace the Section 10 amber border with a soft 10–15% amber background fill behind the element text. This signals "pending action" without introducing a strong graphic element that competes with the CV's typography. Add a small amber dot (6px) to the left of the element text as a secondary indicator.

- **Require explicit Save confirmation for all contenteditable fields, with a preview diff** — Before saving a bullet edit, show a side-by-side diff (original vs. edited) with a "Save" and "Cancel" button. This prevents accidental unsaved state and gives users final validation that their edit looks correct before it persists to the session. Display a green checkmark briefly on confirm (as Section 10 proposes).

- **Constrain the expanded element panel height and add an overflow scroll** — If the expanded element panel exceeds 60% of the viewport, add `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto;` to the element card. This allows expanded details to be scrollable within the element without pushing the rest of the resume off-screen. Clearly mark the scrollable area with a subtle scrollbar indicator.

- **Add a "Settings" link in the sticky settings bar to control CV template font family and colour theme** — Currently (per your existing review), font family and colour are hardcoded in the template and not exposed. The proposed sticky bar should include a dropdown or icon link: "Settings → Font family (Inter/Garamond/Calibri) · Theme (Professional Blue / Warm Neutral / Bold Contrast)". This addresses the existing gap (US-G3) and gives users control over the visual output without requiring CSS knowledge.

- **Display a live word-count or page-break preview within the sticky settings bar** — The proposed "Pages: ~2.1" indicator is helpful, but adding a small visual representation (a mini page-stack icon with colour-coded warning: green ≤ 2 pages, amber 2–2.5, red > 2.5) makes the impact of length/style choices immediately obvious. Consider also adding a "View page breaks" toggle to highlight where page breaks occur in the rendered CV.

123	## Terminology Clarity
124

129	- **Bulk toolbar labels** ("✨ Accept All Recommended", "✓ Include All") — precise and scannable.
130	- **Session ownership labels** ("Owned by another tab") — precise enough for multi-tab coordination.
131	- **Re-run confirm modal** downstream-stage list — correctly communicates that "these steps will be marked stale".
132	
133	---
134	
135	## Story Tally
136	
137	| Story | Result     | Summary                                                                                   |
138	| ----- | ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
139	| US-W1 | ⚠️ Partial | Bulk covers experience/skills/achievements; absent for rewrites/publications/spell; no keyboard shortcuts; sequential pane-only navigation |
140	| US-W2 | ✅ Pass    | Session labels, ownership metadata, and position bar meet all three criteria              |
141	| US-W3 | ⚠️ Partial | Re-run context preservation ✅; re-run affordance discoverability ⚠️ (hover-only ↻)     |
142	
143	---
144	
145	## Top 5 Gaps
146	
147	1. **No keyboard shortcuts for workflow navigation** (High severity) — Zero keyboard acceleration for any stage action (analyze, recommend, generate, accept rewrite, proceed) or pane navigation. Power users processing multiple applications per week must navigate entirely by mouse across a 8-stage, 5-pane workflow. Evidence: no `keydown` / `keyup` handlers found in `web/app.js`, `web/workflow-steps.js`, or `web/review-table-base.js` beyond Enter and Escape.
148	
149	2. **No bulk accept/reject for rewrites** (Medium severity) — The rewrite stage can surface 10–30 individual proposals. Each requires an explicit Accept / Edit / Reject click. There is no "Accept All", "Reject All", or filter-based bulk path. Evidence: `web/rewrite-review.js` — per-card buttons only; no `.bulk-toolbar` rendered.
150	
151	3. **Re-run affordance is hover-only and not visible at rest** (Medium severity) — The ↻ icon injected into completed step pills is `opacity:0` until the user hovers the pill (workflow-steps.js:690). A power user processing many sessions back-to-back will not reliably discover re-run exists without prior knowledge. The layout stage is the exception — it has a persistent stale callout banner — but all other stages depend on accidental discovery via hover.
152	
153	4. **No forward stage skip** (Medium severity) — Users who trust the AI recommendations cannot jump directly from Job Input to Generate. All panes and Spell Check must be traversed in order. Evidence: `web/review-table-base.js:626–641`, `web/app.js`.
154	
155	5. **Bulk toolbar absent for publications** (Low-Medium severity) — Publications pane has per-row include/exclude buttons with no bulk toolbar, inconsistent with the Experience, Skills, and Achievements panes. A researcher or academic user may have 20–50 publications to review individually. Evidence: `web/publications-review.js` — no `.bulk-toolbar` rendered.
156	
157	6. **No custom prompt injection surface** (Low severity) — There is no freeform "instructions to AI" field that power users can use to guide LLM behaviour (e.g., "avoid first-person phrasing", "do not include management experience"). The Settings modal exposes model/temperature/token controls but not user-controlled system-prompt context. Evidence: `web/ui-core.js:saveSettingsModal()` — no prompt-injection field in the form.
158	
159	---
160	
161	## Proposed Story Items
162	
163	- **US-W4: Keyboard shortcut layer** — Power users can trigger common workflow actions via keyboard: Alt+→ / Alt+← to advance/retreat workflow stages, Alt+A to run analysis, Alt+G to generate, Enter to confirm a re-run modal. Shortcuts are documented in a discoverable help overlay (? key).
164	
165	- **US-W5: Batch accept/reject for rewrites and spell-check** — A "✨ Accept All" and "✗ Reject All" button appears at the top of the Rewrites tab and Spell-Check tab, applying to visible (filtered) proposals. Optionally: "Accept All High-Confidence" using the persuasion-check severity field already stored per proposal.
166	
167	- **US-W6: Stage gating override** — Power users can advance past optional stages (Questions, Spell Check, Layout) without completing them via a "Skip stage →" affordance, recording the skip in the session audit trail. The re-run confirm modal offers a "Don't ask again this session" option.
168	
169	- **US-W8: Persistent hover-bypass for re-run** — Power users can pin the ↻ re-run icon to be visible at rest on completed step pills (via a preference toggle in Settings), rather than requiring a hover interaction to discover. As a minimum: add a persistent tooltip or step-tooltip that mentions "hover to re-run" as onboarding text.
170	
171	---
172	
173	**Reviewed against:** web/index.html, web/app.js, web/ui-core.js, web/state-manager.js, web/styles.css, web/workflow-steps.js, web/layout-instruction.js, web/master-cv.js, web/session-manager.js, web/session-switcher-ui.js, web/experience-review.js, web/skills-review.js, web/achievements-review.js, web/rewrite-review.js, web/publications-review.js, scripts/web_app.py, scripts/utils/conversation_manager.py
174	
175	**Evidence standard:** Every conclusion is supported by source evidence. No documentation or prior review documents were used as inputs for factual claims.

```text
1	<!--

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 2026-06-13 17:26:27Z)**_

## Resume Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Eliminates context-switching penalty** — The "document is the UI" thesis moves final resume rendering from the isolated Layout Review tab into the CV tab itself, allowing users to edit bullets and skills while seeing live output. This directly addresses the pain point of "editing bullets gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document."

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Positioning questions adjacent to the analysis data they relate to (e.g., "years of ML experience" appearing next to "Machine Learning" requirement) reduces the friction of bouncing between chat and analysis data. This is a significant upgrade to understanding the job context.

- **Expanded element panel with original/current/proposed comparison** — The multi-row detail panel (Section 6) surfaces all three versions of a piece of content in one place. For resume strategy, this is critical: users can now see what they started with (original), what they've edited (current), and what the AI recommends (proposed) without tab-switching.

- **Ghost item reveal pattern for excluded content** — Section 11's "show hidden (N)" approach keeps the excluded/hidden resume content visible in grayed, struck-through state within the section. This preserves context and prevents the dangerous situation where a user forgets they excluded a strong bullet.

- **Section-level bulk actions with explicit accept/decline** — Section 8's "Accept all" and "Decline all" buttons (with prominent toolbar placement) make it possible to act on suggestions quickly. However, this raises a safety concern addressed below.

- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Unlocking Master CV from the finalise-only restriction (GAP-41) allows users to correct source data mid-session without waiting for the end.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Bulk-accept safety risk** — The "Accept all" button on section headers (Section 8) accepts all pending suggestions in a section with one click. For Experience bullets or Skills, this is dangerous: an LLM batch suggestion may contain subtle errors (e.g., keyword placement, terminology inconsistency from US-R3) that require per-item review. The current Rewrite Review tab forces explicit per-item decisions. Recommend adding a confirmation modal ("This will accept N suggestions") or demoting bulk-accept to a less prominent secondary option.

- **Formatting preservation during in-place editing unclear** — Section 12 specifies that bullet text is "editable in-place" (contenteditable or inline textarea). The concern: when a user edits a bullet, what ensures resume formatting conventions are preserved? If a user deletes a line break or removes the implicit parenthetical context of a sub-skill, will the edited text break formatting? Current design is silent on validation or guidance (e.g., "Keep this under 85 characters"). Current implementation (web/rewrite-review.js) enforces constraints via review UI, not in-place inline editing.

- **Missing severity sort in spell-check integration** — Section 13 shows flagged text by hover-over underline, but does not commit to sorting critical misspellings before minor style suggestions (per current review GAP on US-R7, Section 115). If spell issues are shown in order-received, a user might miss a name typo while addressing comma placement.

- **ATS comments row lacks synonym grouping context** — Section 6 mentions "ATS comments — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues" in the expanded element panel. The current review (US-R1, Section 36) flags that synonyms (ML / Machine Learning) are not grouped visually. This proposal does not clarify whether ATS comments will show grouped keyword matches (canonical ↔ alias) or remain ungrouped as they are today.

- **CV style switcher clarity — Sidebar vs Plain/ATS** — Section 5's style dropdown offers "Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]". The term "Plain/ATS" is ambiguous: does it mean a plain-text ATS-friendly style, or a third style? The current app (web/rewrite-review.js context) uses style profiles that may have different rendering. The proposal should clarify which styles are available and how they differ in the generated output.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a confirmation modal for "Accept all" actions** — Before accepting all N suggestions in a section, show a dialog: "Accept all N suggestions in [Section]?" with options to "Review each" (return to current flow), "Accept all", or "Cancel". This preserves the bulk-action speed while preventing accidental acceptance of borderline proposals.

- **Validate in-place edits against resume conventions** — When a user edits a bullet in-place, provide real-time or on-blur validation: line-length warning (ideal: 70–85 chars), fragment check (does this look like a resume bullet?), and keyword consistency check (does the edited text introduce a new tool term that should appear elsewhere?). Surface these as non-blocking warnings ("⚠ This bullet is X chars — consider shortening") rather than hard blocks.

- **Sort spell-check issues by severity before display** — In Section 13, commit to sorting flagged text: priority 1 = spelling errors (name/company misspellings), priority 2 = grammar/fragment issues in non-bullet context, priority 3 = stylistic suggestions. Implement this in the inline spell-check popover by re-sorting issues on render.

- **Add a "Grouped Keywords" view to ATS comments** — In the expanded element panel (Section 6, "ATS comments" row), group keyword matches by canonical term and show aliases: e.g. **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]. This directly closes the current GAP (US-R1, Section 36) and helps users understand why the ATS is matching their skills to the job.

- **Clarify CV style switcher with previews** — Update Section 5's style dropdown: include a radio option "Show style preview" or "Compare styles" that renders the current section in both Sidebar and Plain/ATS side-by-side in a collapsible preview pane. This removes ambiguity about which style is best for the target ATS and allows users to make informed choices.

- **Preserve section-expand state across tab switches** — In Section 6, specify that when a user switches from the CV tab to (e.g.) the Job tab and back, the section expand/collapse state is remembered per session. This prevents the annoyance of re-expanding a section you were working on. Store state in sessionStorage keyed on section name.

```text
Now I'll write a structured review from the Recruiter-Ops perspective, focusing on throughput, multi-session workflows, and batch operations.

---

## Recruiter-Ops

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document visibility** — rendering the CV throughout the customisation phase (not just at Layout Review) eliminates the context-switching cost of flipping between Bullets, Summary, Skills tabs and wondering how changes appear in the final output. This reduces cognitive overhead per session.
  
- **Section-level batch controls** — the "Suggest section", "Accept all", and "Decline all" buttons (Section 8) directly address high-volume throughput by allowing a recruiter to approve multiple suggestions per section with one click, rather than element-by-element confirmation in the current Rewrite Review tab.

- **Ghost-style excluded items inline** — revealing hidden elements within the section (Section 11) rather than in a separate table eliminates a navigation step. A recruiter can see at a glance which experience bullets or skills were excluded and why, without opening another tab.

- **Master CV always accessible** — unlocking the Master CV tab from the `finalise` stage (Section 2) is a major win. Recruiters often need to add a new skill, correct a date, or update contact info mid-workflow; currently this is blocked.

- **Contextual auto-tab-switching** — automatically showing the Analysis tab during job-analysis phase, then switching to the CV tab during customisation (Section 7) reduces manual navigation and keeps the focus aligned with the current task.

- **Embedded clarification questions** — moving questions from chat-only to inline within the Analysis view (Section 4) keeps the context near the data being questioned, reducing the need to scroll back in chat history to understand what was asked.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing as a throughput tax** — contenteditable elements and inline text fields (Section 12) require careful blur-save handling and introduce a risk of accidental edits. The current DataTable model, while fragmented, enforces explicit save actions. For high-volume users, the proposal's always-on editing surface may slow down workflows where the user wants to review *without* changing anything.

- **Auto-tab-switching could be disruptive** — if a recruiter is flipping between the Job description and the CV to do side-by-side comparison, auto-switching (Section 7) might interrupt the flow. The proposal mentions this as an open question (Section 15.2), but for Recruiter-Ops users managing dozens of applications in sequence, unprompted tab changes could introduce friction.

- **Context-driven highlighting (blue borders) may fatigue** — if the active section changes frequently (e.g., agent posts a suggestion for a different section), the blue left-border accent and tint (Section 7) could create visual noise for power users scanning multiple sections at once.

- **Element expand persistence undefined** — Section 15.3 leaves open whether expanded element panels collapse when switching tabs. If they collapse, the user loses their scroll position when jumping to the Job tab to check a requirement, then back to the CV tab. If they persist, the UI could become cluttered with many expanded panels.

- **No session-level multi-application overview mentioned** — the proposal focuses on improving the single-application UI (job intake → CV → finalise), but does not address GAP-RO4 (current review: "No Cross-Application Summary View"). For Recruiter-Ops managing 20+ active applications, this remains a gap.

- **Batch operations limited to section level** — "Accept all suggestions in a section" is helpful, but the current design does not mention accepting suggestions across *multiple sections* at once (e.g., all accepted suggestions for Experience, Skills, and Summary in a single action). High-volume workflows may benefit from document-level or even session-level accept-all patterns.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Explicit "Review-only mode"** — add a toggle in the CV settings bar (Section 5) to lock the document to read-only, disabling contenteditable and inline saves. This prevents accidental edits during rapid scanning and gives experienced users a fast path through multiple applications.

- **Session-level batch actions** — extend batch controls (Section 8) beyond the section to include a document-level or session-level "Accept all pending suggestions across all sections" button, surfaced in the CV settings bar. This would allow a recruiter who has reviewed all sections to finalise the CV's suggestions in one action.

- **Tab-switch confirmation when in active edit** — if the user is editing an element or has unsaved inline changes, auto-tab-switching (Section 7) should either be suppressed or should prompt "You have unsaved changes in [section]; switch anyway?". This prevents loss of work during agent-driven context switching.

- **Collapsed section summary badges showing suggestion count** — the proposal mentions a summary badge in expanded state (Section 6: `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"`). Ensure this badge is always visible even when the section is collapsed, so a recruiter can scan all sections at a glance to identify how many pending suggestions remain in each, without opening each section.

- **Cover letter and screening DOCX in the proposal** — the redesign focuses on the CV, Master CV, Job, Analysis, Cover Letter, and Screening tabs but does not clarify whether cover letter and screening responses (currently missing from File Review — see current review GAP-1) will be visible in the File Review / Finalise phase. Explicitly confirm that these documents are included in the proposed document-tab model.

- **Provide a "fast finalise" flow** — add a finalise summary card in the CV settings bar or as a dedicated collapsible section (similar to Section 6's expand/collapse model) that shows generated files, ATS score, application status dropdown, and notes textarea. This allows a recruiter to finalise an application without leaving the CV view, reducing context switches and clicks during the submission-readiness phase (Recruiter-Ops' final action per application).
```

153	## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items
154	
155	### GAP-RO1: Application Status Not Visible in Session List
156	The session switcher (`web/session-switcher-ui.js:_renderSavedSessionRows`) shows position name, phase label, created date, and last-modified date — but not `application_status` from `metadata.json`. A recruiter scanning multiple applications cannot see which packages are `sent`, `ready`, or `draft` from the session list.
157	
158	**Proposed story:** *As a recruiter-ops user, I want to see each application's submission status (draft/ready/sent) in the session list so I can quickly identify which packages need action.*
159	
160	### GAP-RO2: No Post-Archive Metadata Update
161	After archiving, `application_status` and `notes` are frozen in `metadata.json`. There is no mechanism to update status from `sent` to `interview`, add follow-up notes, or mark an application as closed without re-entering the finalise flow (which advances phase to `refinement` and re-triggers the harvest section).
162	
163	**Proposed story:** *As a recruiter-ops user, I want to update the application status and add follow-up notes after archiving without re-running the full finalise workflow.*
164	
165	### GAP-RO3: "Done" Phase Label Does Not Reflect Archive State
166	The session switcher shows `Done` for the `refinement` phase (`web/utils.js:282`). This does not indicate whether the application was archived and sent, or only generated. A recruiter-ops user cannot distinguish an archived application from one that reached the finalise step but was never submitted.
167	
168	*Evidence:* `web/utils.js:282` — `SESSION_PHASE_LABELS_SHORT.refinement = 'Done'`
169	
170	### GAP-RO4: No Cross-Application Summary View
171	The session list is the only multi-application surface, capped at 20 entries, showing only position name, phase, and timestamps. There is no dashboard summarising company, role, submission status, ATS score, and date across all applications.
172	
173	**Proposed story:** *As a recruiter-ops user managing multiple applications, I want a summary list showing each application's company, role, submission status, ATS score, and date so I can track my pipeline in one place.*
174	
175	### GAP-RO5: No Generation Timestamp in File List
176	The File Review tab renders no "generated at" timestamp alongside file names. This means users cannot confirm files are current after a back-to-phase re-run, and cannot audit which generation pass produced the displayed files.

178	*Evidence:* `web/download-tab.js:276–325` — `populateDownloadTab()` renders no generation metadata

346	## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items
347	
348	### GAP-1 (HIGH): Cover letter and screening DOCX excluded from File Review and Finalise package view
349	- **Evidence:** `web/download-tab.js:_collectDownloadableFiles` reads only CV-format keys; `web/finalise.js:populateFinaliseTab` shows only `generated.files` from status endpoint; cover letter DOCX saved by `scripts/routes/master_data_routes.py:1590` is not added to `generated_files` session state.
350	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want the File Review and Finalise tabs to list and allow download of cover letter and screening response DOCX files alongside CV files, so I can confirm the complete application package before archiving."
351	
352	### GAP-2 (HIGH): No submission readiness checklist
353	- **Evidence:** No UI element cross-checks: CV generated + cover letter saved + screening responses saved + ATS passing. The user must visit File Review and Finalise tabs separately and verify mentally.
354	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want a readiness checklist visible before finalising that confirms which components (CV, cover letter, screening responses) are generated and whether ATS validation passed, so I have a single-glance confirmation before archiving."
355	
356	### GAP-3 (MEDIUM): Application status not shown in session list
357	- **Evidence:** `web/session-switcher-ui.js:55–72` renders rows with phase label, timestamps, and position name — but not the status field set during finalisation. The status is stored in `metadata.json` on disk but not exposed back to the session switcher.
358	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want the session list to display the archived application status (draft / ready / sent) so I can track my active pipeline without opening individual sessions."
359	
360	### GAP-4 (MEDIUM): Cover letter and screening DOCX naming not surfaced
361	- **Evidence:** `scripts/routes/master_data_routes.py:1574–1640` generates a DOCX from the cover letter but the filename is not displayed to the user and is not confirmed to use the `CV_{company}_{role}_{timestamp}` pattern.
362	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want cover letter and screening DOCX files to use consistent job-relevant naming so files are identifiable outside the application."
363	
364	### GAP-5 (LOW): ATS keyword failure blocks all formats with no bypass
365	- **Evidence:** `web/download-tab.js:113–114`. No override option for deliberately targeting human reviewers.
366	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want to override ATS keyword blocking for specific format downloads when submitting to a human reviewer who does not use automated screening."
367	
368	### GAP-6 (LOW): No package export / bundle download
369	- **Evidence:** No "Download Package" or "Export ZIP" feature in File Review or Finalise tab. Each file must be downloaded or located on disk individually.
370	- **Proposed story:** "As a recruiter-ops reviewer, I want to download the complete application package (CV files + cover letter + screening responses) as a single archive, so I can attach all materials in one operation."
