8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |

158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.

167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised

178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.

Now I'll write the structured review from the hiring manager persona's perspective, focusing on CV output quality, visual appearance, and professional standards.

## Hiring Manager

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live preview throughout customisation** — The CV is always visible in the right pane while editing, eliminating the context-switching problem that forces users to guess how bullets appear in the final document. This directly addresses the hiring manager's primary concern: seeing a well-formatted, role-tailored resume before submission.

- **In-place inline editing preserves document integrity** — Rather than abstracting content into separate DataTables (Experience, Bullets, Skills tabs), the "document is the UI" thesis keeps all edits within the visual context of the rendered resume. Users see immediately when a rewritten bullet becomes too long, when a skill addition disrupts visual balance, or when section headings are malformed.

- **Ghost-style hidden elements solve a credibility risk** — Excluded bullets appear as muted strikethrough within their section when revealed, preventing the accidental submission of incomplete job entries (only 1 accepted bullet per job). This catches the current GAP-HM-01 silent failure and makes inclusion decisions visually explicit.

- **Sticky settings bar for output control** — The Length / Style / ATS / Pages controls are always accessible without tab-switching. The style dropdown (Sidebar vs. ATS Plain) is critical: hiring managers receive either a polished human-readable version or an ATS-optimized plain-text variant, with visual feedback on which is active.

- **Embedded clarification questions in Analysis view** — Moving job-analysis questions from chat-only to inline next to their analysis data (e.g., "years of ML experience" question appearing within the Requirements section) reduces ambiguity and keeps the analysis rationale transparent.

- **Element expansion panels provide decision context** — Each bullet/skill/publication expands to show Original (master data), Current (edited version), Proposed (LLM suggestion), Model recommendation badge, ATS comments, and Persuasion score. This four-sided view is far richer than the current Rewrite Review tab's simple before/after.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks accidental quality degradation** — The proposal makes *all* CV content editable in-place (contenteditable or inline textarea). Unlike the current tab-based model where changes happen in a controlled environment, inline editing can introduce formatting errors (stray newlines, copy-paste artifacts) that users may not notice until Download. The proposed design must enforce strong autosave + undo, and ideally a "Preview as PDF" step before Download.

- **No mention of final validation gates before export** — The current design fires validation warnings at the Download tab (page count, persuasion acknowledgment, etc.). The proposal does not specify whether these gates remain, move to a new "Export Review" modal, or are surfaced as persistent warnings in the settings bar. If warnings shift to inline (e.g., amber border on a section), users may dismiss them casually instead of reading the message.

- **Master CV tab always-present may create version-control confusion** — Currently, Master CV is locked until the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), preventing mid-workflow overwrites. The proposal exposes Master CV as an always-available tab with "explicit Save confirmation" but does not define: (a) whether edits to Master CV persist across sessions, (b) whether a user can revert to their previous Master CV state, (c) how to prevent accidental overwrite of a working master if the user makes an exploratory edit and clicks Save. This is a regression if Master CV edits are not reversible.

- **No specification for style-switcher state persistence** — If a user selects "ATS Plain" in the settings bar and then navigates to another document tab (Analysis, Cover Letter), does the style persist when they return to the CV tab? If the user downloads twice (once in Sidebar, once in ATS), is there a risk of version mismatch if they only notice the style mismatch after sending one version?

- **Drag-to-reorder accessibility deferred** — Section 15 (Open Design Questions) calls out that keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag, but the proposal does not yet define this. For hiring managers, reorder errors (e.g., most-relevant job moved to second position) are high-stakes. The keyboard alternative must be first-class, not an afterthought.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a pre-Download validation checklist modal** — Before entering the Download workflow, prompt the user to confirm: (1) page count is 2–3 pages (with visual indicator), (2) persuasion warnings (weak verbs, single-bullet jobs) are acknowledged, (3) no inline edits are pending save, (4) spell-check issues are resolved. This preserves the current safety gates but integrates them into the new flow without breaking immersion.

- **Implement a "Preview as PDF" button in the settings bar** — Alongside "Regenerate Preview," add a button that opens a real PDF preview in a modal or new tab before Download. This catches formatting errors, widow/orphan words, and page-break surprises that HTML rendering may not catch. This is especially critical because inline contenteditable editing can introduce soft-break artifacts.

- **Mark Master CV edits with a "dirty" indicator and require explicit confirmation** — If Master CV is always accessible, add a visual indicator (e.g., red dot on the tab, "Unsaved changes" warning) when the user has made edits to Master CV fields. Require an explicit "Save to Master CV" confirmation (not just a blur save) to prevent accidental overwrites. Ideally, log the timestamp and old value of any Master CV change for auditability.

- **Add a "Revert to Session Start" option for CV edits** — Since inline editing can cascade (rewrite one bullet, which then affects keyword scoring, which then affects skills priority), provide a quick "Revert all CV changes" button (in the settings bar or a modal) to restore the CV to the state it was in when the user entered the Customisation phase. This is a safety valve if inline edits go wrong mid-workflow.

- **Specify style-switcher behavior and provide a visual badge** — When the user switches from "Sidebar" to "ATS Plain" in the settings bar, the badge should prominently display the active style (e.g., "Style: Sidebar ▾" → "Style: ATS Plain ▾" with background color change). On Download, the filename should include the style (e.g., `resume_ATS.pdf` vs. `resume_Sidebar.pdf`). This prevents version-confusion mistakes.

- **Integrate page-count warnings into the settings bar directly** — Instead of relying on a modal or separate validation step, show the page-count badge in the sticky settings bar with live color feedback (green ≤2 pages, amber 2–2.5 pages, red >2.5 pages). Include a tooltip explaining the warning threshold so users understand the hiring manager preference without reading external docs.

Now I'll write the structured review from the Returning User perspective, focusing on session restoration, prior decisions, and the workflow experience.

---

## Returning User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Persistent session context via auto-tab-switching** — The proposal to auto-switch to the most relevant document tab (Section 2, "Auto-switching") as the workflow advances naturally restores the working session. A returning user reopening a saved session will automatically land on the CV tab during customisation or the Analysis tab during review, making the session feel continuous rather than requiring manual tab navigation. This directly improves US-S1.2 (current stage indicated).

- **Master CV always accessible** — Unlocking the Master CV tab from the `finalise` stage gate (Section 2, "Master CV" row) means a returning user can now verify and update foundational data at any point in the session, not just at the end. This removes the anxiety of discovering errors too late and restores control.

- **Prior decisions visible in-place via ghost items** — The inline reveal of excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (Section 11, "Hidden Element Reveal Pattern") makes a returning user's prior inclusion/exclusion choices immediately observable within the context of the rendered CV, without hunting through tabs. The **(+N hidden)** badge serves as a quick visual summary of what was excluded—addressing GAP-R1 (restored-decisions summary).

- **Inline suggestion workflow reduces tab-switching fatigue** — Pending AI suggestions appear directly on elements with amber borders (Section 10, "Has pending suggestion") rather than forcing a detour to the Rewrite Review tab. A returning user can accept/decline/edit suggestions without losing visual context of where they appear in the final output.

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Rather than being buried in the chat, inline questions (Section 4, "Clarification questions embedded inline") appear adjacent to the analysis data they relate to. A returning user resuming job analysis work immediately sees what needs clarification without scrolling chat history.

- **Live document-as-UI pattern eliminates the "resume only at layout stage" problem** — The CV view remains visible throughout customisation, rewrite, and spell-check phases. A returning user can immediately see the cumulative effect of prior decisions and new changes, making the session feel coherent rather than fragmented.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **No explicit restored-decisions summary on initial re-entry** — While ghost items and collapsed badges help, there is no "welcome back" panel or summary message (e.g., "Session restored: 4 experiences selected, 12 skills, 7 approved rewrites") that greets a returning user the moment they reload. The current design includes a confirmation message like "✅ Session restored: {positionName} ({phase})" (returning-user.md:87); the proposed design does not yet specify an equivalent. A returning user might not immediately notice their prior work is intact until expanding sections.

- **Workflow step pills location unclear—may reduce visibility of session progress** — The proposal to move step pills from the current horizontal header to a "compact top bar" or "collapsible left-sidebar strip" (Section 2, "Workflow Step Pills") risks burying the session's stage progress. The current design's horizontal step bar provides a persistent, scannable sense of "where am I in this session?" (returning-user.md:37, `SESSION_PHASE_LABELS_SHORT`). A returning user glancing at the screen should immediately see their position. If collapsed or in a sidebar, this becomes a hunt.

- **Expanded elements may not persist across tab switches** — Section 15 ("Open Design Questions") explicitly leaves unresolved whether expanded element detail panels remain open when switching tabs or auto-collapse. For a returning user mid-edit of an experience bullet, switching tabs and returning could either preserve the expanded state (intuitive continuity) or collapse it (forcing re-expansion). The design does not yet commit to either path.

- **No explicit mention of scroll position restoration** — When a returning user restores a session, should the CV view scroll back to the last-edited section, or reset to the top? The current design (returning-user.md:88) does not specify, but the proposal is silent on this detail. Returning to a multi-page CV and finding the view scrolled to the top rather than the section being worked on breaks continuity.

- **Inline editing increases state-save complexity** — Section 12 ("In-Place Editing Across All Documents") allows contenteditable fields throughout the CV. The proposal states changes "update session state immediately" for CV/Cover Letter/Screening, but does not specify debounce timing, conflict handling if the session is edited in multiple tabs, or rollback on validation failure. A returning user making a quick edit could face UI confusion if the save fails or races with the agent's updates.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a restored-decisions summary banner on session re-entry** — On initial load after session restore, display a collapsible banner below the header showing: "Session restored: 4 of 7 experiences selected • 12 skills • 3 pending rewrites • 2 clarification questions open." Include an option to dismiss or auto-hide after 10 seconds. This directly addresses GAP-R1 and gives a returning user immediate confirmation their work is intact.

- **Pin the workflow step pills to a sticky header or left-panel strip with visible labels** — If moving away from the current horizontal header, ensure step pills remain always visible with full (not abbreviated) phase names (e.g., "Job Analysis" not "Analysis"). Consider a compact sticky top bar with breadcrumb-style labels ("Phase: Customisation › Experience") or a persistent left-panel strip below the chat. A returning user glancing at the screen should know their session's position at a glance, without hovering or scrolling.

- **Define and document element expand-state persistence** — Specify in Section 15 that expanded element panels persist across tab switches (store in session state) so a returning user's in-progress edits remain visible if they briefly check another tab and return. Include a visual indicator (e.g., a small dot) on the section badge showing "N elements expanded."

- **Implement scroll position restoration on session reload** — After session restore, scroll the CV view to the section that was last active in the prior session (stored in `status.last_active_section`). Include a smooth scroll-to behavior rather than instant jump. A returning user should land exactly where they left off, not at the top of the document.

- **Specify contenteditable debounce and conflict handling** — Document (in Section 12 or a new implementation guide) that CV edits debounce with a 2-second delay before sending to `/api/update-session`, that concurrent edits from multiple tabs or agent rewrites show a "conflict detected—reload?" modal, and that failed saves rollback the UI to the last-known state. A returning user editing a bullet while the agent rewrites a skill should see clear conflict resolution, not silent overwrites.

- **Extend the Analysis view to show clarification answer history** — When a returning user resumes job analysis, show not only open clarification questions but a collapsible "Answered" section with prior responses (e.g., "You said: 10 years of Python experience"). This reinforces session continuity and prevents re-answering the same questions. Include a "Clear and re-answer" option if the user wants to revise.

Only on hover does ↻ appear. Keyboard-only and touch users cannot discover it. The element carries `title="Re-run ${step} with updated inputs"` (standard HTML title, not a Bootstrap tooltip).
59	
60	Since the previous review, Bootstrap tooltips via `_getStepTooltip()` + `_updateViewingIndicator()` (`web/workflow-steps.js:195-253`) now show `'Click ↻ to rerun from here'` when the user is *currently viewing* a completed step, and `'Click to view'` on other completed steps. This is an improvement but still hover-dependent.
61	
62	**Failure modes:**
63	- "Users unintentionally overwriting downstream work" — ✅ mitigated: step-click does not change phase; re-run requires ↻ + confirmation dialog.
64	- "Re-run behavior visually indistinguishable from navigation" — ⚠️ partially addressed: Bootstrap tooltip on the step pill now distinguishes 'Click to view' from 'Click ↻ to rerun from here', but this distinction remains hover-only and invisible to keyboard/touch users.
65	
66	**Acceptance criteria:**
67	- "Returning users receive sufficient warning before downstream state changes" — ✅ for re-run path.
68	- "Distinction between re-entry and recomputation is understandable" — ⚠️ implicit only; requires hover discovery.
69	
70	---
71	
72	### US-S3: Trustworthy Session Continuity
73	
74	#### S3.1 — Saved decisions can be re-observed when their stage is revisited
75	
76	⚠️ **Partial** — State restoration is real: `_hydrateStatusDerivedState()` (session-manager.js:351) reloads all decision maps. For `rewrite_review` phase, the rewrite panel is pre-populated from `/api/rewrites` (session-manager.js:646-659). For customization tabs, `_hydrateStatusTabState()` sets `stateManager.setTabData('customizations', ...)` which is read by review table rendering. However, whether each tab correctly re-renders prior selections (e.g. checked/unchecked states in the experience table) on revisit depends on tab-specific rendering code outside the files reviewed here. The session-manager restore confirms data is present, but legibility within each tab is unverified from this set of source files alone.
77	
78	#### S3.2 — Generated/previewed outputs remain logically connected to current state
79	
80	✅ **Pass** — The layout freshness system is fully implemented. `getLayoutFreshnessFromState()` (`web/state-manager.js:100-144`) computes `isStale` and `isCritical` from `contentRevision` vs. `lastPreviewContentRevision`/`lastFinalContentRevision`. `applyLayoutFreshnessNavigationState()` (`web/workflow-steps.js:50-84`) shows "Outdated" badges on the Layout step and downstream download/finalise tabs. CSS in `web/styles.css:118-119,153-154,487-489` styles the stale/critical states distinctively.
81	
82	#### S3.3 — Session restoration does not mislead about which version is current
83	
84	✅ **Pass** — `_resolveRestoredPhase()` (`web/session-manager.js:225-249`) has two defensive guards:
85	- If `job_analysis` is absent, forces `PHASES.INIT` regardless of stored phase.
86	- If phase is `CUSTOMIZATION` or `REWRITE_REVIEW` but customizations are missing (e.g. server restarted mid-workflow), falls back to `PHASES.JOB_ANALYSIS`.
87	Restore messages include the session name and phase: "✅ Session restored: {positionName} ({phase})" (`web/session-manager.js:666`).
88	
89	**Acceptance criteria:**
90	- "Previously saved work is recoverable and legible on return" — ⚠️ Recoverable: yes. Legible: depends on per-tab rendering (partially verified).
91	- "Current vs. earlier outputs distinguishable when multiple passes occurred" — ✅ stale/critical badge system covers this.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## Generated Materials Evaluation
96	
97	The returning user persona does not directly evaluate generated CV files; the relevant questions are whether a returning user can find their previous outputs and whether those outputs are marked as current or outdated. The layout freshness system (US-S3.2 above) addresses this. No additional generated-materials gaps identified that are specific to this persona.

The action is reversible via Trash, but users receive no in-app confirmation before the session disappears from the list. |

115	
116	## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items
117	
118	**GAP-R1 (HIGH) — No restored-decisions summary on return**
119	After session restore, there is no human-readable summary of what was recovered (e.g. "4 experiences selected, 12 skills, 7 rewrites approved"). The user must navigate to each tab individually to verify their prior work.
120	> Proposed story: "As a returning user, I want a brief summary of my restored session decisions so that I can quickly verify my prior work is intact before continuing."
121	
122	**GAP-R2 (RESOLVED ✅) — "Delete" label corrected to "Move to Trash"**
123	Previously flagged as HIGH. The button at `web/session-switcher-ui.js:85` was relabelled from "Delete" to "Move to Trash" since the 2026-04-20 review. The `title` attribute also reads "Move session to Trash". The Trash view with Restore and Delete Forever actions provides the full recovery path. No further action needed on this specific gap.
124	
125	**GAP-R2b (LOW) — "Move to Trash" executes without confirmation**
126	The `_deleteSessionFromModal()` function (`web/session-switcher-ui.js:317`) calls the API directly with no `confirmDialog()`. While the action is reversible (session goes to Trash), a click on the red "Move to Trash" button immediately removes the session from the list with no "Are you sure?" step. Compare: "Delete Forever" (`web/session-switcher-ui.js:454`) and "Empty Trash" (`web/session-switcher-ui.js:471`) both use `confirmDialog()` before proceeding.
127	> Proposed fix: Add a `confirmDialog('Move this session to Trash? You can restore it from the Trash view.')` before the API call in `_deleteSessionFromModal()`.
128	
129	**GAP-R3 (MEDIUM) — ↻ re-run icon is invisible until hover; not keyboard-accessible**
130	The ↻ re-run button is `opacity:0` by default and reveals only on hover (`web/workflow-steps.js:686-691`). Keyboard and touch users cannot discover it. Returning users who want to re-run a stage cannot find the action without prior knowledge.
131	> Proposed story: "As a returning user, I want re-run actions on completed steps to be persistently visible (or discoverable via keyboard) so that I can re-run a stage without needing to know to hover."
132	
133	**GAP-R4 (MEDIUM, partially addressed) — Step-click vs. ↻ distinction now conveyed via hover tooltip only**
134	`handleStepClick` (`web/workflow-steps.js:712`) switches the view tab without showing any modal or banner. Since the 2026-04-20 review, Bootstrap tooltips via `_getStepTooltip()` / `_updateViewingIndicator()` now show `'Click to view'` and `'Click ↻ to rerun from here'` on completed step pills. This is an improvement, but the tooltip is hover-only — keyboard and touch users still receive no explanation, and there is no persistent on-screen label differentiating the two actions.
135	> Remaining gap: "As a returning user who uses a keyboard or touch device, I want the distinction between view-navigation and re-run to be discoverable without hover so that I can find the re-run action without prior knowledge."
136	
137	**GAP-R5 (MEDIUM) — Abbreviated phase labels may be opaque to returning users**
138	`SESSION_PHASE_LABELS_SHORT` (`web/utils.js:274-285`) maps `refinement` → "Done" (misleading if work is ongoing) and `customization` → "Custom" (non-obvious). These labels appear in the session switcher header and the sessions modal.
139	> Proposed story: "As a returning user, I want session phase labels in the session switcher to be human-readable so that I can immediately understand where a prior session was left off."
140	
141	**GAP-R6 (LOW) — No session duplicate/copy action**
142	The sessions modal offers Load, Rename, and Move to Trash, but no Duplicate. A returning user who wants to try a different approach cannot easily create a copy of an existing session.
143	> Proposed story: "As a returning user, I want to duplicate an existing session so that I can explore an alternative customization without risking my prior decisions."
144	
145	**GAP-R7 (LOW) — Session rename uses browser `prompt()` rather than in-app modal**
146	`promptRenameCurrentSession()` (`web/session-manager.js:735`) uses `window.prompt()` (`web/session-manager.js:737`), which browsers can block. The sessions modal already provides inline rename (`web/session-switcher-ui.js:294-315`), but the header rename button ✏️ (visible next to the position title bar) takes a different (fragile) path.
147	> Proposed fix: Replace `promptRenameCurrentSession()` with an in-app modal consistent with `confirmDialog()`.
148

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295

## HR / ATS Specialist

### What the proposed design gets right

- **ATS Score badge and drill-down in settings bar** — Moving the ATS score to a sticky "Settings Bar" (Section 5) keeps ATS compliance visibility constant while scrolling, eliminating the current "Compute ATS Score" empty-state button that users overlook. Clicking opens a drill-down modal, which directly addresses the current hidden-by-default behavior.

- **Keyword highlighting in Job view** — The "Job Description View" (Section 3) adds amber highlighting for matched terms and red for missing required keywords. This directly teaches users which job terms the CV already covers and what gaps remain—critical for hard-requirement compliance before customization begins.

- **ATS comments in expanded element panel** — The proposed "Element States" (Section 6) embed **"ATS comments — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues"** directly within the expanded element detail panel. This is a major improvement: users making editorial decisions see ATS impact alongside persuasion and model recommendation in one place, rather than hunting between the "ATS Report" button and the text itself.

- **Plain/ATS style option clarity in settings bar** — The "Style" dropdown (Section 5) explicitly lists "Plain/ATS" as a selectable rendering mode, replacing the current scattered approach. Users can toggle between human-readable (Sidebar) and ATS-safe layout inline, making the tradeoff visible.

- **Hard-requirement keyword coverage now visible inline** — By collapsing sections to show summary badges (e.g., *"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"*), users at a glance see how many elements are included per section. Expanding individual elements and reading ATS comments together creates a direct pathway to asking: *"Do my included bullets cover the hard requirements?"*

- **Master CV always accessible** — The "Master CV" tab (Section 2) is no longer locked to the `finalise` stage. This enables users to update the underlying data at any time, reducing re-work and ensuring consistent skill classification across sessions.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks ATS-safe formatting** — The proposed in-place editing model (Section 12) allows users to edit bullet text, skills, and summary directly in the rendered CV view. If the ATS DOCX generation blindly copies edited text without re-normalizing formatting (e.g., removing bold/italic runs, ensuring single-column layout), inline edits could introduce formatting artifacts that break ATS parsing. The current design's separate tab-based review reduces this risk because bulk generation and validation happen in a controlled batch step.

- **ATS validation gate missing in proposed workflow** — The current "File Review" tab enforces a 17-check validation report and blocks downloads on failures. The proposed design mentions "Download & Validate" (Section 2) but does not detail how the validation report integrates into the new CV view or whether the checks still gate downloads. If validation is deferred to a separate step after CV editing is complete, users may not discover downstream ATS failures until too late.

- **Spell-check underline could interfere with ATS scoring** — The proposed "Spell Check Integration" (Section 13) renders red/blue underlines inline on the CV view. If these underlines or their associated metadata (e.g., suggestion popover HTML) leak into the DOCX export, they could corrupt the ATS text extraction or introduce unexpected characters into keyword matching.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add an ATS safety mode toggle in the settings bar** — Alongside the "Style" dropdown (Plain/ATS), add a checkbox: **"ATS Safe Editing — disable inline formatting; reject HTML-rich edits."** When enabled, contenteditable fields strip formatting on blur, and the settings bar shows a reminder: *"Inline edits will be normalized for ATS compliance."* This gives users explicit control over the risk/benefit tradeoff.

- **Embed ATS validation status in the settings bar** — Extend the sticky settings bar (Section 5) to include a "Validation Status" badge (green ✓ / amber ⚠ / red ✗) that updates live as users edit. Display the count of failing checks: *"3 issues: font name, 15+ keywords unchecked, overlapping dates."* Clicking opens the full 17-check report. This ensures the validation gate remains visible throughout the CV view, not relegated to a separate tab.

- **Add a "Hard Requirements Coverage" widget to the Analysis view** — In the Analysis View (Section 4), after the embedded clarification questions, add a dedicated widget showing: **Hard Required Keywords: [matched count] / [total count]**, with a red warning if coverage < 100%. Each unmatched keyword should link to a section where users can add it (e.g., *"Click to add 'Kubernetes' to the Technical Skills section"*). This makes the hard-requirement compliance task concrete and actionable.

- **Clarify the ATS DOCX export path from inline edits** — The proposal does not explain how changes made via in-place editing in the CV view are serialized into the ATS DOCX. Document a clear rule: *"When a user edits a bullet or skill inline, that change is immediately persisted to session state. On ATS generation, all text is re-normalized (formatting stripped, line breaks standardized) before export."* Include a validation check that compares the ATS DOCX text to the edited session state to detect formatting corruption.

- **Define synonym / variant handling in ATS comments** — The current ATS review (hr-ats.md) flags that `compute_ats_score` uses `synonym_map.json` but `validate_ats_report` does not (GAP-H-E). The ATS comments field (Section 6) should note when a keyword is matched via synonym (e.g., *"Matched as: 'ML' variant of 'Machine Learning'"*), and the validation gate should apply the same synonym rules to avoid false negatives.

- **Add a "Missing Keywords" panel to the element expand state** — When a user expands an element (e.g., a bullet), and the ATS comments note missing hard-requirement keywords, auto-suggest insertion points: *"This bullet mentions DevOps but not Terraform. Consider appending: '… using Terraform and containerization.'* Users can accept the suggestion inline or manually edit. This bridges the gap between "seeing a problem" and "acting on it."

Now I'll write a structured Trust & Compliance review comparing the current design to the proposed redesign.

---

## Trust & Compliance

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Expanded element panel retains original/current/proposed three-row audit trail** (Section 6). The proposed design explicitly surfaces all three versions side-by-side during inline editing, making it impossible to lose sight of what changed and why—a clear improvement over the current tab-scattered review model. Users can see the provenance of every edit at the moment of decision.

- **Inline suggestion acceptance with mandatory decision visibility** (Sections 6, 8). By anchoring AI suggestions directly on the document element they affect—with amber border boxes and toolbar buttons—the design forces users to encounter each suggestion in context, reducing the risk of accidental bulk acceptance without reviewing the actual output.

- **Ghost item reveal pattern provides explicit inclusion/exclusion audit** (Section 11). Hidden elements are rendered inline with strikethrough and 50% opacity, preserving traceability of what was excluded and why. This is a substantial improvement over the current design, where exclusion decisions are made in separate tabs and never visually reconciled with the final output.

- **Master CV always-accessible tab removes gate** (Section 2, goal row 5). The current design locks Master CV editing to the finalise stage (GAP-41), forcing users to re-run or work through undocumented side paths to update source data. Always-visible access improves trust by making the authoritative source permanently reachable.

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** (Section 4). Current design buries clarification questions in chat-only, making it easy for users to miss context-specific follow-ups. Inline placement adjacent to the analysis data they relate to ensures users cannot accidentally ignore AI-derived questions before generating rewrites.

- **Contextual section highlighting during workflow phases** (Section 7). The blue left-border accent and subtle tint on the currently active section, combined with left-pane breadcrumb, grounds users in *which* section is being customized, reducing the risk of blind bulk-accept operations on the wrong section.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Section-level bulk "Accept all" control introduces compliance risk** (Section 8, "✅ Accept all"). While inline element-level acceptance improves visibility, the section-level accept-all button bypasses the one-at-a-time review pattern that the current rewrite-review tab enforces. If a user clicks "Accept all" on Experience suggestions without expanding any elements, they could merge dozen of LLM-proposed rewrites without seeing them. The proposal should gate this action behind the same per-item acknowledgement model as the current rewrite stage (e.g., requiring each pending element to be expanded before "Accept all" is enabled).

- **In-place contenteditable editing without explicit save-on-change confirmation** (Section 12). The proposal states that CV/Cover Letter/Screening changes "update session state immediately" on blur or explicit save. This implicit-persist model is weaker than the current explicit "Save" confirmation on Master CV writes. For high-stakes content (bullets, summary), users may inadvertently edit and lose focus, triggering an invisible state update. The design should clarify whether a "Saved" badge or undo-stack is provided, and whether session state persists to disk before explicit finalisation.

- **Element-expand persistence question left open** (Section 15.3). The proposal defers the decision: "should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?" If panels collapse on tab-switch, users viewing Job → Analysis → CV may lose context of which elements were being evaluated, reintroducing the context-loss problem the redesign aims to solve. This must be decided before implementation.

- **Undo/rollback mechanism not defined** (Section 15.5). Inline edits across CV, Cover Letter, Screening, and Master CV lack a clear undo path. The proposal notes that "Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element [may not] behave predictably," but proposes no fallback. Users who misclick or accidentally overwrite content mid-session have no documented recovery path.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Gate "Accept all" at section level behind element-expansion checkpoint.** Require that at least one pending element in the section has been expanded and explicitly accepted/edited/rejected before the "Accept all" button becomes enabled. This preserves the current rewrite-review's defense against blind bulk acceptance while keeping the control accessible.

- **Explicit "Session checkpoint" before finalisation.** Before proceeding from CV phase to layout/finalisation, display a read-only summary of all pending suggestions (by section: e.g., "Experience: 3 pending · Skills: 1 pending · Summary: 0 pending"). This mirrors the current rewrite-review acknowledgement pattern and prevents users from inadvertently accepting undecided items via "Accept all" in the final phase.

- **Add a persistent "Draft" badge and audit breadcrumb to inline edits.** When a user edits an element in-place, append a brief `(edited by user on Session #123 · 2026-06-13)` footer to the expanded element panel. This preserves traceability in session state and helps users distinguish LLM-proposed rewrites from manual edits.

- **Clarify Master CV save workflow with explicit lock/unlock pattern.** Master CV writes should require an explicit "Unlock & Save" confirmation (similar to current `_save_master` in web_app.py:1166–1188). The proposal currently states "changes to Master CV require an explicit Save," but does not explain whether that save is local-session-only or writes back to the authoritative file. Document the backup-before-write and schema-validation-on-write pattern.

- **Replace implicit blur-save with explicit Save button in contenteditable fields.** For CV, Cover Letter, and Screening edits, show an inline "Save" button that appears after the user types. Only on Save should session state update. This prevents accidental persistence and aligns with the Master CV model.

- **Embed confession-of-limitation for AI-suggested data.** In the Proposed row of each expanded element panel, add a small `(⚠ AI-generated)` label. This mirrors the current "⚠ Candidate to confirm" weak-badge pattern and ensures users apply appropriate scrutiny to LLM-generated rewrites, particularly for skill additions and summary variants.

11	**Last Updated:** 2026-04-22 10:30 ET
12	**Executive Summary:** The cv-builder application has a solid foundation for trust and compliance: AI suggestions are visually distinguished from source content with word-level diffs, confidence levels are tracked and displayed for all recommendation types, and the rewrite stage enforces explicit per-item decisions gated by a persuasion-warning acknowledgement. Two gaps weaken the posture: (1) LLM provider data-retention disclosure is accessible only via a wizard popover and disappears after setup, leaving users who selected a non-confidential provider (Gemini free-tier, Groq) with no persistent reminder; (2) the customization stage (experiences, skills, achievements) carries no blocking gate requiring explicit per-item decisions before generation, so items can reach the final CV with only LLM defaults applied.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## Application Evaluation
17	
18	### US-C1: Transparent AI Suggestions
19	
20	**Criterion 1 — Proposed rewrites and additions are visibly presented as suggestions**
21	
22	✅ **Pass**
23	
24	Every proposed rewrite is rendered as a card in the dedicated Rewrites tab with a word-level inline diff (red = removed, green = added) computed by `computeWordDiff` and `renderDiffHtml` (web/rewrite-review.js:204–229). Three explicit action buttons (✓ Accept, ✎ Edit, ✗ Reject) appear on each card. The tab is never populated with a pre-accepted or merged result — the user sees only the unresolved proposals on arrival.
25	
26	Skill additions with weak evidence carry a `⚠ Candidate to confirm` badge rendered at web/rewrite-review.js:238–240:
27	```js
28	const isWeakSkillAdd = r.type === 'skill_add' && r.evidence_strength === 'weak';
29	const weakBadge = isWeakSkillAdd
30	  ? `<span class="weak-badge">⚠ Candidate to confirm</span>` : '';
31	```
32	
33	**Criterion 2 — Weak-evidence or confirm-first cases are clearly flagged**
34	
35	✅ **Pass**
36	
37	Persuasion warnings are collected in a dedicated red panel (`background:#fef2f2; border:1px solid #fecaca`) above the rewrite cards (web/rewrite-review.js:79–109). The panel lists each warning by `flag_type` and location. Submission is blocked until the user explicitly clicks "✓ Acknowledged" (web/rewrite-review.js:105). The backend computes eight structural checks (strong action verb, passive voice, word count, result clause, named institution, CAR structure, summary generic phrases — conversation_manager.py:1009–1070) so the flag set is grounded in concrete heuristics, not heuristic-free.

42	
43	✅ **Pass**
44	
45	`rewriteDecisions` is module-level state in web/rewrite-review.js; it starts empty and is only populated when the user clicks Accept, Edit+Save, or Reject. The backend's `approve_rewrites` method (conversation_manager.py:879–928) persists only decided entries to `approved_rewrites` and records all outcomes in `rewrite_audit`. No merging of undecided proposals into the session state occurs.

57	if (submitBtn) submitBtn.disabled = (pending > 0 || !persuasionWarningsAcknowledged);

If the user confirms, pending items are auto-resolved to `'ignore'`. 144	
145	1. The disclosure is **only visible during initial setup**. Once a provider is configured and the wizard is closed, there is no persistent indicator in the header pill or settings panel warning that the active provider is non-confidential.
146	2. The header pill shows "LLM: [model name]" with a ready/not-ready badge (web/index.html:50–55) but no `confidential` status.
147	3. For a user who selected Gemini's free tier at startup and never re-opened the wizard, their CV content and job descriptions are being sent to Google for potential review — with no visible UI reminder.

151	## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items
152	
153	**GAP-TC-1: Persistent non-confidential provider warning**
154	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want a persistent visual indicator when the active LLM provider is non-confidential, so that users who send sensitive career data to providers like Gemini free-tier or Groq are continuously reminded of data-retention risk.
155	Evidence: `confidential: False` for gemini (provider_registry.py:171) and groq (provider_registry.py:190); header pill shows only model name and auth status (web/index.html:50–55).
156	
157	**GAP-TC-2: Per-item decision gate in customization stages**
158	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want the customization stage (experience/skill/achievement review) to require explicit decisions on AI-recommended items rather than allowing undecided items to inherit LLM defaults silently, so that users remain in active control of what enters their CV.
159	Evidence: customization tabs allow submission with undecided items; rewrite tab already demonstrates the correct gating pattern (web/rewrite-review.js:358).
160	
161	**GAP-TC-3: Summary variant AI-proposal labeling**
162	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want all AI-generated summary variants to be clearly labeled as AI-proposed (not authored by the user) in the Summary review tab, so that users apply appropriate scrutiny before accepting AI characterizations of their career.
163	Evidence: no "AI-proposed" label found for summary variants; contrast with weak-badge pattern in web/rewrite-review.js:238–240.
164	
165	**GAP-TC-4: Session audit panel**
166	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want a read-only session audit view accessible from the Finalise tab that shows the full `rewrite_audit` log (what was proposed, what was accepted, what was edited), so that users can reconstruct the approval chain after the fact.
167	Evidence: `rewrite_audit` exists in session.json (conversation_manager.py:920) but is not exposed in any UI tab.
168	
169	**GAP-TC-5: AI attribution option in generated files**
170	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want the option to include an "AI-assisted" attribution in the metadata or footer of generated PDF/DOCX files, so that users can disclose AI involvement where required by the role or institution.
171	Evidence: no attribution mechanism found in cv_orchestrator or template renderer.
172	
173	**GAP-TC-6: LLM data-transmission disclosure**
174	*Proposed story:* As a trust/compliance reviewer, I want users to see a clear one-time disclosure that their CV content and job description are transmitted to the configured LLM provider, so that the data flow is transparent before any sensitive career data leaves the local machine.
175	Evidence: no in-app disclosure of external data transmission found; onboarding modal (web/index.html:264–313) mentions AI but not external data transmission.

216	**Criteria 1: Proposed rewrites are visibly presented as suggestions.**
217	
218	✅ **Pass** — The Rewrites tab renders a panel headed "✏️ Review Text Improvements" with explicit messaging: "Look over each suggestion… accept, edit, or reject each one before continuing to spell check" (`web/rewrite-review.js:64`). Each card shows original and proposed text with an LCS word-level inline diff.

220	**Criteria 2: Weak-evidence or confirm-first cases are clearly flagged.**
221	
222	⚠️ **Partial** — The persuasion-warning system (Phase 10) is implemented. `web/rewrite-review.js:46–58` fetches `persuasion_warnings` from `/api/rewrites`, groups them by type, and renders a red collapsible banner at the top of the panel. `conversation_manager.py:980–1064` defines `run_persuasion_checks`, applying 8 heuristic checks (strong action verb, passive voice, word count, result clause, named institution, CAR structure, summary generic phrases). **Gap**: the warning detail section is collapsed by default (`rewrite-review.js:85` `style="display:none"`), and the "✓ Acknowledged" button lives inside the collapsed panel (`rewrite-review.js:92–96`). A user can submit rewrite decisions without ever expanding the warning. Individual cards carry no inline severity badge distinguishing `warn` vs `info`.
223	
224	**Criteria 3: The UI does not blur approved output with proposed changes.**
225	
226	✅ **Pass** — Session state separates `pending_rewrites`, `approved_rewrites`, and `rewrite_audit` (`conversation_manager.py:74–77`). The customization stage never auto-promotes any pending rewrite. The tally bar tracks accepted / rejected / pending independently (`rewrite-review.js:338–358`). The `submit-rewrites-btn` is rendered `disabled` on mount (`rewrite-review.js:125`) and stays disabled while `pending > 0` (`rewrite-review.js:358`).
227	
228	**Acceptance Criterion — AI-proposed content is reviewable before acceptance.**
229	
230	✅ **Pass** — Every rewrite card exposes explicit accept / edit / reject controls. `submitRewriteDecisions` is blocked by the button-disabled guard.
231	
232	**Acceptance Criterion — Higher-risk suggestions receive stronger visual signalling.**
233	
234	⚠️ **Partial** — A red banner aggregates counts by type. The severity field (`warn` | `info`) from `run_persuasion_checks` is stored but is not rendered as a per-card badge or visual distinction at the card level.
