238	### US-C2 — User Approval Integrity
239	
240	**Criteria 1: Review-required stages block progression until decisions are made.**
241	
242	⚠️ **Partial** — Rewrite review: submit button is blocked while any pending item remains (`rewrite-review.js:358`). **Gap**: when zero rewrites exist, the workflow auto-advances directly to `generate_cv` without showing the Rewrites tab at all (`current-implemented-workflow.md` §Rewrite Review). The user never sees a confirmation that the review stage was evaluated cleanly.
243	
244	Spell check: a similar fast-path exists — if no flags are returned, the frontend auto-continues to generate (`current-implemented-workflow.md` §Spell Check, note 1).
245	
246	Customise stage: experience/skill/achievement decisions are not gated. The Generate button (`app.js:117`) checks `userSelections` for already-submitted decisions but does not block if the user has never opened the decision panels.
247	
248	**Criteria 2: Acceptance, rejection, and edit paths remain distinguishable.**
249	
250	✅ **Pass** — Three distinct rewrite actions: accept (green), reject (red), edit (opens textarea). Card class names reflect state (`.accepted` / `.rejected`, `rewrite-review.js:301–307`). Active buttons receive the `.active` class.
251	
252	**Criteria 3: The UI does not silently auto-accept items expected to be user-controlled.**
253	
254	⚠️ **Partial** — When rewrites exist, no item is auto-accepted. When zero rewrites exist the workflow treats absence as implicitly accepted and advances silently. Same applies to the zero-flags spell-check path.
255	
256	**Acceptance Criterion — Approval-dependent stages enforce explicit decision-making.**
257	
258	⚠️ **Partial** — Satisfied for non-empty rewrite review. Not satisfied for: (a) empty rewrite review fast-path, (b) empty spell-check fast-path, (c) Customise stage with no decision gating.

262	### US-C3 — Provenance and Audit Cues
263	
264	**Criteria 1: Diff-like review is available where text is being changed.**
265	
266	✅ **Pass** — `computeWordDiff` (`rewrite-review.js:196–259`) implements a full LCS word-level diff, tokenising by whitespace and producing `unchanged` / `removed` / `added` tokens. Removed tokens render as red strikethrough, added tokens as green. Diffs regenerate live when a user edits a card.
267	
268	**Criteria 2: The UI retains or exposes rationale where promised.**
269	
270	✅ **Pass** — Each rewrite proposal carries a `rationale` field. `rewrite_audit` in session state (`conversation_manager.py:920`) stores every proposal merged with its outcome and `final` text. The harvest candidate table (`finalise.js:276`) renders `c.rationale` in a dedicated column for every candidate.
271	
272	**Criteria 3: Finalisation and harvest flows remain traceable to reviewed changes.**
273	
274	✅ **Pass** — `_compile_harvest_candidates` (`generation_routes.py:897`) sources candidates exclusively from `conversation.state['approved_rewrites']`. Harvest apply (`generation_routes.py:1961–1978`) creates a git commit with message `"chore: Update master CV data from {company}_{role}_{date} session"`. `_save_master` (`web_app.py:1166–1188`) creates a timestamped backup before overwriting and restores it if post-write schema validation fails.

276	---
277	
278	## Generated Materials Evaluation
279	
280	Generated output files (HTML, PDF, DOCX) do not embed provenance metadata — session ID, LLM provider, model, date, or rewrite-audit summary — in the file itself. Users cannot verify after the fact which session or model produced a given file from the artifact alone. This is an expected limitation of the single-user local architecture but is not disclosed anywhere in the UI.
281	
282	The harvest rationale column (`finalise.js:276`) renders LLM-generated text without attribution. No label indicates that rationale is AI-inferred rather than factually sourced. Users evaluating candidates in the harvest table cannot distinguish the basis of the rationale.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## Additional Story Gaps / Proposed Story Items
287	
288	**GAP-T1 (HIGH) — Persuasion warning acknowledgement can be bypassed**
289	Warning detail is collapsed by default (`rewrite-review.js:85`, `style="display:none"`). The "✓ Acknowledged" button is inside the collapsed section (`rewrite-review.js:92–96`). Users can submit rewrite decisions without ever reading or expanding the warning.
290	*Proposed US-C4*: The Submit button must remain disabled until each `warn`-severity persuasion warning has been individually acknowledged via the button inside the expanded panel.
291	
292	**GAP-T2 (MEDIUM) — Silent auto-advance through empty review stages**
293	Zero-rewrite and zero-flag paths advance without any user-visible confirmation that the stage was evaluated. Users cannot distinguish "nothing needed review" from "review was skipped."
294	*Proposed US-C5*: When a review stage produces zero items, display an explicit confirmation screen with a summary ("0 rewrites required" / "0 spell flags found") before advancing.
295	
296	**GAP-T3 (MEDIUM) — No in-app disclosure that CV content is transmitted to external LLM APIs**
297	The application sends the user's full CV data and job description to third-party LLM providers. There is no in-app notice or one-time acknowledgement of this data flow. The localhost URL and file-path settings imply local storage, but the transmission path is invisible.
298	*Proposed US-C6*: First session creation must show a one-time disclosure ("Your job description and CV excerpts are sent to the configured LLM provider for analysis") with an explicit acknowledgement checkbox before proceeding.
299	
300	**GAP-T4 (MEDIUM) — Customise stage decisions not gated before Generate**
301	A user can reach the Generate step without visiting or deciding on any item in the Customise stage. The customizations used for generation may not reflect any user intent.
302	*Proposed US-C7*: The Generate action must require that at least one explicit decision has been submitted from the Customise stage, or show a blocking warning that no customisation decisions were made.
303	
304	**GAP-T5 (LOW) — Harvest rationale column is AI-generated but unlabelled**
305	Rationale in the harvest table (`finalise.js:276`) is LLM-produced and displayed without attribution or caveat.
306	*Proposed US-C8*: Harvest candidate rationale fields must carry a visible "(AI-generated)" annotation.
307	
308	**GAP-T6 (LOW) — Session data retention not disclosed**
309	Sessions accumulate indefinitely in `~/CV/files/sessions`. There is no in-app guidance on retention, how to delete sessions, or what happens to files after in-memory eviction.
310	*Proposed US-C9*: The Sessions panel must include a note explaining where session files are stored and how to permanently delete them.

9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |

## Master CV Curator

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Always-accessible Master CV tab (Section 2, 14)** — This directly addresses GAP-41 and a critical pain point from the current review. The Master CV is no longer locked to the `finalise` stage but is listed as the first document tab and available "at any time," enabling pre-job and between-job maintenance of the shared source-of-truth.

- **Unified in-place editing with explicit Master CV save gates (Section 12)** — The proposal recognizes that Master CV writes are fundamentally different from session-scoped edits. Session documents (CV, Cover Letter, Screening) update state immediately on blur; Master CV changes require an explicit "Save" confirmation before writing. This prevents accidental data loss on the permanent record.

- **Expanded element panel with "Original" row (Section 6)** — Each element shows Original (read-only, from Master CV), Current (session-scoped edits), and Proposed (LLM suggestion). This makes the data lineage crystal clear within a single visual context, eliminating confusion about which version is being edited and what came from the master.

- **Ghost-style excluded items inline within sections (Section 9, 11)** — Hidden elements are revealed in-place rather than in a separate table, preserving the "document-is-the-UI" principle while maintaining the visual boundary between included and excluded content (strikethrough, 50% opacity, dashed border).

- **Contextual highlighting of the active workflow section (Section 7)** — A blue left-border accent on the section being worked on, paired with a breadcrumb in the chat header ("Phase: Customisation › Experience"), reinforces which part of the document is under focus. This maintains awareness of where master data ends and session scope begins.

- **Spell check surfaced inline rather than in a separate tab (Section 13)** — Grammar and spelling flagging with underline + hover/popover correction keeps the "document is the UI" philosophy intact and eliminates tab-switching for a closely related editing task.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Master CV state boundaries become harder to enforce in an always-on model** — The current design hides the Master CV tab entirely during mid-workflow stages, making it impossible to accidentally write to master data outside `init`/`refinement`. The proposal shows Master CV "at any time," which relies on backend phase gating (`_require_master_data_write_phase`) being infallible. A UI/UX burden shifts entirely to the backend; if the phase check ever fails or shows a confusing 409 error (as noted in the current review, F1), users may see "Editing not available while a job is active" inline instead of being prevented upfront from seeing the editable tab.

- **Expanded element panels and session state coupling under "Proposed" — unclear persistence model** — When a user expands an element to see the Proposed rewrite and chooses "Accept," does this state persist in the session immediately, or only after a Save/Submit action? The proposal does not clarify when Proposed suggestions are promoted to Current. In the current design, the Rewrite Review tab is discrete and applicants explicitly choose to "apply" selections. In the new design, accepting inline could create transient session state that is not formally captured until harvest.

- **Loss of explicit harvest/archive boundary (vs Section 3 in current review)** — The current design's Finalise tab has an archive section followed by a distinct harvest section with a "Skip" button and optional messaging. The proposed redesign replaces the per-section Finalise/Master CV workflow with a unified document viewer that shows "Active document rendered here." It is unclear whether the two-phase harvest workflow (1. Finalise & Archive, 2. Optional: Update Master CV) is still present or has been merged into a single document-centric flow.

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view may fragment the chat narrative (Section 4)** — Embedding inline answerable questions in the Analysis view alongside analysis data creates two parallel input streams: left-pane chat and right-pane inline answer fields. This could confuse the agent's reasoning trail or cause users to post redundant messages to chat after answering inline.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Formalize the Master CV write-confirmation flow with phase context** — In Section 12, add explicit language: "Master CV changes require a 'Save' confirmation that includes a phase check. If the session is not in `init` or `refinement`, show an inline error message: 'Cannot edit master data while a job customisation is active. Archive the job first, then return here.' This prevents the confusing 409 → session-conflict-banner bug and gives users an upfront reason why they cannot edit."

- **Clarify the Proposed → Current → Session State pipeline for suggestions** — In Section 6, specify: "Accepting a suggestion (via ✅ Accept button) moves the Proposed text into the Current field in-place, but does not write to master data. All in-session changes (Current field edits, accepted suggestions, reorders, excludes) are held in session state and written to master only if explicitly harvested post-finalisation. Changes to Master CV tab itself are never auto-harvested." Optionally add a visual indicator (e.g., a blue badge "Session") on the Current field to remind users this is temporary.

- **Preserve explicit harvest/archive boundaries with visual step sequencing** — After finalising the job (archive step), show a distinct second section or card on the Finalise document tab (or a modal/dialog) titled "Step 2: Review & Apply Master CV Updates (Optional)." List the harvest candidates (improved bullets, new skills, etc.) with the current table layout. This keeps the two-phase lifecycle visible without breaking the "document-is-the-UI" principle; it simply acknowledges that archive and harvest are distinct steps with distinct consequences.

- **Inline Analysis questions should post answers to the left-pane chat** — In Section 4, clarify: "When a user answers a clarification question inline (e.g., 'How many years of ML experience?'), the answer is posted to the left-pane chat as a message from the user, and the agent processes it as part of the analysis conversation. This ensures the full reasoning trail remains in chat and the agent can see all context." Add a visual affordance (arrow icon, "Post to chat" button) to make this flow obvious.

- **Define the Master CV expanded element panel state and save trigger** — In Section 6, when describing the Master CV tab and expanded elements: "Master CV elements may be expanded to edit any field (name, title, dates, skills, etc.). All changes are made in-place on the Current field. Before closing the panel or navigating away, a 'Save' button appears (or the panel shows unsaved indicator). Clicking Save runs `_require_master_data_write_phase` and writes to `Master_CV_Data.json` with a timestamped backup." This makes the save ceremony explicit and prevents accidental master writes on blur.

- **Add a mini-legend or inline help for the Original/Current/Proposed rows** — In Section 6, consider a small "?" icon next to the three rows in the expanded element panel that shows a tooltip: "**Original:** from your Master CV (read-only). **Current:** your session edits. **Proposed:** AI suggestion (editable; accept or decline below)." This removes ambiguity about data lineage for new users and reinforces that only Current and Proposed are mutable in the session.

## Persuasion Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document context during editing** — the CV View always shows the rendered resume with inline controls, directly addressing the core gap where editing bullets in the Bullets tab previously gave no sense of how they appear in the final output. This supports framing decisions by showing immediate impact.

- **Inline "Persuasion comments" row in expanded element panels (Section 6)** — the five-row expanded element panel now includes "Persuasion comments" (alongside Model recommendation badges) adjacent to the Original/Current/Proposed text versions. This is a major upgrade: currently, persuasion warnings surface only in the separate Rewrite Review tab; in the proposed design, they appear inline where decisions are made, significantly improving discoverability and reducing decision friction.

- **Model recommendation badges (Emphasize/Include/De-emphasize/Exclude) integrated into element expansion (Section 6)** — these badges appear directly on each expanded element alongside persuasion and ATS feedback. This consolidates signal into one place, aligning tactical recommendation with persuasive intent rather than separating them across tabs.

- **Iterative in-place editing encouraged by the design** — the expanded element panel supports editing the "Current" and "Proposed" text fields in-place before accepting, plus a "✏️ Accept with inline editing" control (Section 9). This lowers the friction to iterate on rewrite suggestions, encouraging users to refine rather than simply accept/decline.

- **Contextual highlighting of the active workflow section (Section 7)** — the section being customised receives a blue left-border accent and auto-scroll on agent reference. This keeps persuasive framing decisions anchored to intent; the user sees which role narrative is being shaped at that moment.

- **Master CV always accessible (Section 2 & 6)** — removing the "locked to finalise stage" gate (GAP-41) allows users to update source data at any time, supporting the principle that strong framing decisions should flow back to the master record rather than being one-off session edits.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Persuasion comments row is present but not shown how it's generated** — the proposal lists "Persuasion comments" as a data row in Section 6 but does not specify: (a) whether these comments are the existing eight persuasion checks (`check_strong_action_verb`, `check_passive_voice`, `check_word_count`, etc.), rendered inline; (b) who generates them (LLM, heuristic, or current backend checks); or (c) how they differ from the current collapsible persuasion warnings panel. Without detail, it is unclear if this is a redesign of the current warning panel or a new commentary system.

- **No explicit gating of submission on persuasion acknowledgement** — the current design (as of commit `732a431`) gates the "Submit All Decisions" button on `persuasionWarningsAcknowledged = true`. The proposed design's Section 9 lists element-level controls but does not specify whether a form-level gate remains (i.e., can the user still proceed past Customisation with unresolved persuasion issues?). If inline editing reduces perceived friction, users may skip reviewing persuasion flags entirely.

- **Ghost-style excluded elements may undermine persuasion coherence** — Section 11 allows excluded elements to be revealed inline with a "Show hidden" toggle. While this improves visibility, it risks surface-level cosmetic edits: a user might include a mediocre bullet in ghost view without checking persuasion comments. The proposal does not specify whether ghost elements trigger warnings or are treated as lower-priority.

- **Persuasion comments tied to expanding an element, not always visible** — the expanded element panel is opt-in (triggered by clicking the ▶/▼ toggle on Section 9). A user who never expands an element will never see its persuasion comments unless they are also rendered in the collapsed summary badge. The proposal does not clarify whether a high-priority persuasion flag (e.g., passive voice) bubbles to the collapsed view or remains hidden until expansion.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Specify the "Persuasion comments" data structure and generation** — clarify whether this row displays the existing eight checks bundled as prose ("Strong verb ✓, Has result clause ✓, Passive voice ⚠️"), or a new LLM-generated commentary ("This bullet is strong but could specify the audience/impact more."). Propose a concrete rendering (e.g., a 1-2 sentence summary with links to detailed checks).

- **Explicit persuasion gate at phase-exit** — add a visible commit to Section 9 or the phase transition flow: e.g., "Submitting this phase requires addressing all ⚠️ Persuasion flags or marking them as reviewed." This preserves the blocking acknowledgement pattern from commit `732a431` while making it visible in the in-place workflow.

- **High-priority persuasion flags surface in collapsed element view** — define a severity threshold (e.g., passive voice, hedging language, >30 words) that causes a small warning badge (⚠️ or 🔴) to appear next to the collapsed element text. This ensures users are nudged toward expansion without forcing immediate expansion on every element.

- **Persuasion comment prioritisation by impact on framing** — when rendering the "Persuasion comments" row, weight issues that directly undermine framing (passive voice, hedging, absent result clause, weak verb) above structural notes (word count, CAR pattern). This surfaces the most persuasive-intent-relevant feedback first, especially for time-pressed users.

- **Inline CAR-structure suggestion in the expanded panel** — currently, `check_car_structure` fires at `severity='info'` and does *not* propose a rewrite. In the proposed design, if an element lacks a Challenge section, add a "Suggest CAR structure" button in the expanded element panel (like "✨" in Section 9), allowing the user to generate a CAR-reframed variant in-place.

- **Cross-document framing check on phase advance** — when exiting Customisation or entering Cover Letter generation, add a lightweight check: compare the narrative threads selected in Experience bullets against the professional summary's opening statement (a partial implementation of GAP-P-05). Surface a warning if they lead with different role identities (e.g., "Your bullets emphasize **data engineering**, but your summary opens with **ML leadership**"). This aligns the proposed "live document context" to US-P6 (register consistency).

---

**Summary:** The proposed design substantially improves discoverability of persuasion feedback by moving it inline and adjacent to editing surfaces. The key risk is that accessibility without gating may reduce user engagement with persuasion signals. The enhancements above would lock in the persuasive intent of the design without relying on user discipline to expand elements and review warnings unprompted.

For high-volume users, the proposal's always-on editing surface may slow down workflows where the user wants to review *without* changing anything.

- **Auto-tab-switching could be disruptive** — if a recruiter is flipping between the Job description and the CV to do side-by-side comparison, auto-switching (Section 7) might interrupt the flow. - **Context-driven highlighting (blue borders) may fatigue** — if the active section changes frequently (e.g., agent posts a suggestion for a different section), the blue left-border accent and tint (Section 7) could create visual noise for power users scanning multiple sections at once.

- **Element expand persistence undefined** — Section 15.3 leaves open whether expanded element panels collapse when switching tabs. - **Explicit "Review-only mode"** — add a toggle in the CV settings bar (Section 5) to lock the document to read-only, disabling contenteditable and inline saves. This prevents accidental edits during rapid scanning and gives experienced users a fast path through multiple applications.

- **Tab-switch confirmation when in active edit** — if the user is editing an element or has unsaved inline changes, auto-tab-switching (Section 7) should either be suppressed or should prompt "You have unsaved changes in [section]; switch anyway?". - **Auto-tab switching may disrupt keyboard-driven workflows** — If a user is reviewing elements via keyboard (pressing ↓ to move through bullets, pressing E to expand/edit, etc.) and the auto-switch logic fires (e.g., "workflow advanced, switching to Cover Letter tab"), focus is lost and keyboard flow is broken. No mention is made of how focus is managed or whether auto-switch can be disabled. This directly conflicts with the stated power-user need for keyboard-driven workflows.

- **Expand/collapse UX for 30+ items** — The proposal uses a universal expand/collapse model (Section 6): sections are collapsed by default, showing a one-line summary badge ("3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"). For a researcher with 50+ publications or a senior engineer with 15+ experiences, collapsing sections by default may actually increase navigation overhead. Users must expand each section, then expand elements within, then collapse them again. The current DataTable, once filtered, keeps all rows visible at once. A full-text search on a DataTable row can find a single bullet in seconds; the proposed expand-then-search may be slower.

- **Inline editing on contenteditable elements introduces UX friction** — Section 12 mentions that all edits are "contenteditable or inline textarea" with save-on-blur. The proposal also notes "Undo — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough?" (Section 15). This is a real problem: contenteditable is notoriously fragile across browsers. A power user who relies on Ctrl+Z to undo rapid-fire edits will have a worse experience if the undo behavior is unpredictable. The current DataTable uses native form inputs, which have solid undo support.

- **No bulk-selection loss** — The current DataTable supports multi-row selection (checkbox column, select-all-visible header checkbox). The proposal does not mention per-element checkboxes or a "select all" affordance. If a power user wants to select and act on a subset of elements that do not fit the section-level "Accept all" model (e.g., "accept all skills in the Python category"), the proposed design offers no path. The section-level controls are coarse-grained.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add keyboard shortcuts for all hover-toolbar actions** — Implement Alt+A for "Accept this element", Alt+D for "Decline", Alt+↓ for "Move down", Alt+E for "Expand", etc. Bind these at the element level so they apply to the currently focused element (via Tab navigation). Document in a persistent keyboard help overlay (? key, discoverable from settings). This directly addresses the #1 power-user gap and makes the hover-only UI tolerable.

- **Make hover-toolbar buttons visible at rest, with opacity muting** — Instead of pure hover-reveal, render section header and element toolbars at ~30% opacity at rest, increasing to 100% on hover. This maintains the current design's clean visual hierarchy while making the affordance discoverable without accidental interaction. Reduces discoverability friction without adding clutter.

- **Add a "flat list" or "DataTable" view toggle for high-item sections** — For sections with 15+ items (publications, achievements), provide a checkbox-based DataTable view alongside the expand/collapse model. Power users can switch between "rendered view" (for final output preview) and "table view" (for bulk selection and filtering). This preserves the DataTable's speed and multi-row selection while keeping the proposal's in-place editing model as the default.

- **Implement explicit focus management and optional auto-tab-switch disable** — When the workflow phase advances and the auto-switch fires, set focus to the newly-switched tab's first interactive element (e.g., first section header or first element). Provide a Settings toggle: "Auto-switch document tabs on workflow phase change". For keyboard-driven users, auto-switch can be disabled while preserving manual tab clicking.

- **Add a "collapse all" button at the top of the CV view** — When reviewing a section with many expanded elements, provide a "Collapse all" button in the sticky settings bar. This saves users from clicking the collapse icon on every element. Paired with a "Expand all" button for sections where reviewing all details at once is necessary.

- **Expose "inline edit mode" via keyboard shortcut and preserve undo natively** — Bind Ctrl+E (or I) to enter inline edit mode on the currently focused element. Use a native `<textarea>` instead of contenteditable for all editable fields, which gives users predictable Ctrl+Z undo. If visual formatting (e.g., strikethrough on ghost items) is needed, wrap the textarea in a styled container rather than relying on contenteditable. This solves the undo-unpredictability issue while keeping inline editing fast.

## Returning User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Persistent session context via auto-tab-switching** — The proposal to auto-switch to the most relevant document tab (Section 2, "Auto-switching") as the workflow advances naturally restores the working session. A returning user reopening a saved session will automatically land on the CV tab during customisation or the Analysis tab during review, making the session feel continuous rather than requiring manual tab navigation. This directly improves US-S1.2 (current stage indicated).

- **Master CV always accessible** — Unlocking the Master CV tab from the `finalise` stage gate (Section 2, "Master CV" row) means a returning user can now verify and update foundational data at any point in the session, not just at the end. This removes the anxiety of discovering errors too late and restores control.

- **Prior decisions visible in-place via ghost items** — The inline reveal of excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (Section 11, "Hidden Element Reveal Pattern") makes a returning user's prior inclusion/exclusion choices immediately observable within the context of the rendered CV, without hunting through tabs. The **(+N hidden)** badge serves as a quick visual summary of what was excluded—addressing GAP-R1 (restored-decisions summary).

- **Inline suggestion workflow reduces tab-switching fatigue** — Pending AI suggestions appear directly on elements with amber borders (Section 10, "Has pending suggestion") rather than forcing a detour to the Rewrite Review tab. A returning user can accept/decline/edit suggestions without losing visual context of where they appear in the final output.

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Rather than being buried in the chat, inline questions (Section 4, "Clarification questions embedded inline") appear adjacent to the analysis data they relate to. A returning user resuming job analysis work immediately sees what needs clarification without scrolling chat history.

- **Live document-as-UI pattern eliminates the "resume only at layout stage" problem** — The CV view remains visible throughout customisation, rewrite, and spell-check phases. A returning user can immediately see the cumulative effect of prior decisions and new changes, making the session feel coherent rather than fragmented.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **No explicit restored-decisions summary on initial re-entry** — While ghost items and collapsed badges help, there is no "welcome back" panel or summary message (e.g., "Session restored: 4 experiences selected, 12 skills, 7 approved rewrites") that greets a returning user the moment they reload. The current design includes a confirmation message like "✅ Session restored: {positionName} ({phase})" (returning-user.md:87); the proposed design does not yet specify an equivalent. A returning user might not immediately notice their prior work is intact until expanding sections.

- **Workflow step pills location unclear—may reduce visibility of session progress** — The proposal to move step pills from the current horizontal header to a "compact top bar" or "collapsible left-sidebar strip" (Section 2, "Workflow Step Pills") risks burying the session's stage progress. The current design's horizontal step bar provides a persistent, scannable sense of "where am I in this session?" (returning-user.md:37, `SESSION_PHASE_LABELS_SHORT`). A returning user glancing at the screen should immediately see their position. If collapsed or in a sidebar, this becomes a hunt.

- **Expanded elements may not persist across tab switches** — Section 15 ("Open Design Questions") explicitly leaves unresolved whether expanded element detail panels remain open when switching tabs or auto-collapse. For a returning user mid-edit of an experience bullet, switching tabs and returning could either preserve the expanded state (intuitive continuity) or collapse it (forcing re-expansion). The design does not yet commit to either path.

- **No explicit mention of scroll position restoration** — When a returning user restores a session, should the CV view scroll back to the last-edited section, or reset to the top? The current design (returning-user.md:88) does not specify, but the proposal is silent on this detail. Returning to a multi-page CV and finding the view scrolled to the top rather than the section being worked on breaks continuity.

- **Inline editing increases state-save complexity** — Section 12 ("In-Place Editing Across All Documents") allows contenteditable fields throughout the CV. The proposal states changes "update session state immediately" for CV/Cover Letter/Screening, but does not specify debounce timing, conflict handling if the session is edited in multiple tabs, or rollback on validation failure. A returning user making a quick edit could face UI confusion if the save fails or races with the agent's updates.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a restored-decisions summary banner on session re-entry** — On initial load after session restore, display a collapsible banner below the header showing: "Session restored: 4 of 7 experiences selected • 12 skills • 3 pending rewrites • 2 clarification questions open." Include an option to dismiss or auto-hide after 10 seconds. This directly addresses GAP-R1 and gives a returning user immediate confirmation their work is intact.

- **Pin the workflow step pills to a sticky header or left-panel strip with visible labels** — If moving away from the current horizontal header, ensure step pills remain always visible with full (not abbreviated) phase names (e.g., "Job Analysis" not "Analysis"). Consider a compact sticky top bar with breadcrumb-style labels ("Phase: Customisation › Experience") or a persistent left-panel strip below the chat. A returning user glancing at the screen should know their session's position at a glance, without hovering or scrolling.

- **Define and document element expand-state persistence** — Specify in Section 15 that expanded element panels persist across tab switches (store in session state) so a returning user's in-progress edits remain visible if they briefly check another tab and return. Include a visual indicator (e.g., a small dot) on the section badge showing "N elements expanded."

- **Implement scroll position restoration on session reload** — After session restore, scroll the CV view to the section that was last active in the prior session (stored in `status.last_active_section`). Include a smooth scroll-to behavior rather than instant jump. A returning user should land exactly where they left off, not at the top of the document.

- **Specify contenteditable debounce and conflict handling** — Document (in Section 12 or a new implementation guide) that CV edits debounce with a 2-second delay before sending to `/api/update-session`, that concurrent edits from multiple tabs or agent rewrites show a "conflict detected—reload?" modal, and that failed saves rollback the UI to the last-known state. A returning user editing a bullet while the agent rewrites a skill should see clear conflict resolution, not silent overwrites.

- **Extend the Analysis view to show clarification answer history** — When a returning user resumes job analysis, show not only open clarification questions but a collapsible "Answered" section with prior responses (e.g., "You said: 10 years of Python experience"). This reinforces session continuity and prevents re-answering the same questions. Include a "Clear and re-answer" option if the user wants to revise.

## Trust & Compliance

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Expanded element panel retains original/current/proposed three-row audit trail** (Section 6). The proposed design explicitly surfaces all three versions side-by-side during inline editing, making it impossible to lose sight of what changed and why—a clear improvement over the current tab-scattered review model. Users can see the provenance of every edit at the moment of decision.

- **Inline suggestion acceptance with mandatory decision visibility** (Sections 6, 8). By anchoring AI suggestions directly on the document element they affect—with amber border boxes and toolbar buttons—the design forces users to encounter each suggestion in context, reducing the risk of accidental bulk acceptance without reviewing the actual output.

- **Ghost item reveal pattern provides explicit inclusion/exclusion audit** (Section 11). Hidden elements are rendered inline with strikethrough and 50% opacity, preserving traceability of what was excluded and why. This is a substantial improvement over the current design, where exclusion decisions are made in separate tabs and never visually reconciled with the final output.

- **Master CV always-accessible tab removes gate** (Section 2, goal row 5). The current design locks Master CV editing to the finalise stage (GAP-41), forcing users to re-run or work through undocumented side paths to update source data. Always-visible access improves trust by making the authoritative source permanently reachable.

- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** (Section 4). Current design buries clarification questions in chat-only, making it easy for users to miss context-specific follow-ups. Inline placement adjacent to the analysis data they relate to ensures users cannot accidentally ignore AI-derived questions before generating rewrites.

- **Contextual section highlighting during workflow phases** (Section 7). The blue left-border accent and subtle tint on the currently active section, combined with left-pane breadcrumb, grounds users in *which* section is being customized, reducing the risk of blind bulk-accept operations on the wrong section.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Section-level bulk "Accept all" control introduces compliance risk** (Section 8, "✅ Accept all"). While inline element-level acceptance improves visibility, the section-level accept-all button bypasses the one-at-a-time review pattern that the current rewrite-review tab enforces. If a user clicks "Accept all" on Experience suggestions without expanding any elements, they could merge dozen of LLM-proposed rewrites without seeing them. The proposal should gate this action behind the same per-item acknowledgement model as the current rewrite stage (e.g., requiring each pending element to be expanded before "Accept all" is enabled).

- **In-place contenteditable editing without explicit save-on-change confirmation** (Section 12). The proposal states that CV/Cover Letter/Screening changes "update session state immediately" on blur or explicit save. This implicit-persist model is weaker than the current explicit "Save" confirmation on Master CV writes. For high-stakes content (bullets, summary), users may inadvertently edit and lose focus, triggering an invisible state update. The design should clarify whether a "Saved" badge or undo-stack is provided, and whether session state persists to disk before explicit finalisation.

- **Element-expand persistence question left open** (Section 15.3). The proposal defers the decision: "should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?" If panels collapse on tab-switch, users viewing Job → Analysis → CV may lose context of which elements were being evaluated, reintroducing the context-loss problem the redesign aims to solve. This must be decided before implementation.

- **Undo/rollback mechanism not defined** (Section 15.5). Inline edits across CV, Cover Letter, Screening, and Master CV lack a clear undo path. The proposal notes that "Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element [may not] behave predictably," but proposes no fallback. Users who misclick or accidentally overwrite content mid-session have no documented recovery path.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Gate "Accept all" at section level behind element-expansion checkpoint.** Require that at least one pending element in the section has been expanded and explicitly accepted/edited/rejected before the "Accept all" button becomes enabled. This preserves the current rewrite-review's defense against blind bulk acceptance while keeping the control accessible.

- **Explicit "Session checkpoint" before finalisation.** Before proceeding from CV phase to layout/finalisation, display a read-only summary of all pending suggestions (by section: e.g., "Experience: 3 pending · Skills: 1 pending · Summary: 0 pending"). This mirrors the current rewrite-review acknowledgement pattern and prevents users from inadvertently accepting undecided items via "Accept all" in the final phase.

- **Add a persistent "Draft" badge and audit breadcrumb to inline edits.** When a user edits an element in-place, append a brief `(edited by user on Session #123 · 2026-06-13)` footer to the expanded element panel. This preserves traceability in session state and helps users distinguish LLM-proposed rewrites from manual edits.

- **Clarify Master CV save workflow with explicit lock/unlock pattern.** Master CV writes should require an explicit "Unlock & Save" confirmation (similar to current `_save_master` in web_app.py:1166–1188). The proposal currently states "changes to Master CV require an explicit Save," but does not explain whether that save is local-session-only or writes back to the authoritative file. Document the backup-before-write and schema-validation-on-write pattern.

- **Replace implicit blur-save with explicit Save button in contenteditable fields.** For CV, Cover Letter, and Screening edits, show an inline "Save" button that appears after the user types. Only on Save should session state update. This prevents accidental persistence and aligns with the Master CV model.

- **Embed confession-of-limitation for AI-suggested data.** In the Proposed row of each expanded element panel, add a small `(⚠ AI-generated)` label. This mirrors the current "⚠ Candidate to confirm" weak-badge pattern and ensures users apply appropriate scrutiny to LLM-generated rewrites, particularly for skill additions and summary variants.

# CV Builder UI Redesign — Persona Review

**Design doc reviewed:** [tasks/ui-redesign-proposal.md](ui-redesign-proposal.md)
**Date:** 2026-06-13
**Personas:** 14 (all active personas)
**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)

---

## Applicant

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live context preservation** — Seeing the CV rendered throughout the workflow (not just at Layout Review) closes the gap between editing suggestions in isolation and understanding their impact on the actual document.
- **Inline decision-making** — Element hover toolbars with accept/reject/edit buttons eliminate the mental context-switching burden of jumping between a Rewrite Review tab and the final output.
- **Ghost elements and inclusion visibility** — Excluded items shown inline with strikethrough and reduced opacity make it clear what's *not* going into the CV during customisation.
- **Embedded clarification questions** — Questions paired with the analysis data they relate to, rather than buried in conversation history, is a major usability win.
- **Always-available Master CV tab** — Updating baseline data at any moment rather than being forced to wait until the end of a session removes a significant workflow friction.
- **Consistent section/element expansion model** — The two-state collapse/expand pattern is predictable and reduces overwhelm when facing 20+ experience bullets or 30+ skills.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Performance and interactivity risk** — Real-time rendering of the full CV with inline hover toolbars, contenteditable fields, and inline spell-check underlines may lag as the CV grows. No performance baseline is proposed.
- **Conflation of editing surfaces** — Master CV (requires explicit Save) vs. CV session (immediate) have different interaction models living in the same right pane. The current separation, while fragmented, makes these boundaries explicit.
- **Loss of comparison workflow in Rewrite Review** — The current before/after card UI with word-level diff highlighting is absent from the proposal. The new inline "Proposed" text field loses the visual diff that helps judge rewrite magnitude.
- **Lack of workflow progression feedback** — The proposal mentions moving step pills to a "compact top bar" or "sidebar strip" but provides no concrete UX for progress visibility.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Prototype and performance-test the inline edit model** — Before committing to contenteditable, validate that the browser's DOM rendering can keep up with a 500+ bullet CV. Offer a fallback "modal edit" mode for expensive elements.
- **Preserve word-level diff for rewrites** — When an element has a "Proposed" rewrite, show before/after with LCS word-diff highlighting (removed text in red, added text in green) alongside the inline textarea.
- **Add explicit "Master CV Save" confirmation modal** — Make it visually distinct from CV session changes: a modal diff preview before write.
- **Define workflow phase indicators** — Propose a sticky breadcrumb in the left-pane chat header or a subtle badge on the primary section being worked on.
- **Specify keyboard navigation for section/element expand** — Define consistent bindings: `Ctrl+Space` to expand/collapse focused element, `Tab` to move between elements, `Ctrl+Enter` to save inline edits.
- **Add a "changes since last re-run" persistent badge** — After a re-run, changed/new elements should have a lasting orange "new" badge (not just a transient flash) so users can quickly scan which items were affected.

---

## First-Time User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document context during editing** — Users will finally see how their edits appear in the actual CV rather than working blind in isolated tabs.
- **Inline suggestion acceptance** — Instead of toggling between "Rewrites" and "Generated CV" tabs, users see pending suggestions (amber border) in-place and can accept/decline/regenerate without leaving context.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Removing the finalise-stage lock lets users update master data at any time.
- **Collapsible expand/collapse model** — The two-state pattern is consistent across sections and elements; users learn it once and apply it everywhere.
- **Ghost items clarify inclusion decisions** — Showing strikethrough/muted excluded items within the section makes include/exclude visible in context.
- **Embedded clarification questions** — Moving questions from chat-only to adjacent-to-data solves the "buried in chat" problem.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Toolbar proliferation risks cognitive overwhelm** — The element hover toolbar has 9+ buttons. A first-time user encountering this on their first bullet point may freeze. Secondary/context-dependent buttons must be hidden or deprioritized.
- **No persistent help entry point** — The proposal does not mention onboarding or persistent "?" access after the welcome modal is dismissed.
- **Settings bar competes for cognitive real estate** — The sticky settings bar occupies valuable vertical space. Testing at 1366×768 (laptop) is required.
- **Expand/collapse state persistence is underspecified** — If a user expands several bullets, switches to Screening, then returns, will all their expansions have collapsed?
- **Preview vs. Final output distinction is not addressed** — The proposal never states "this is a preview until you confirm layout" or equivalent, risking repetition of the same old failure mode.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a "Preview/Final" label in the CV View settings bar** — A badge: "🔄 Preview mode — confirm layout to finalize" / "✅ Layout confirmed — ready to download."
- **Create a three-tier help system** — (1) Inline tooltips on controls. (2) Persistent Help toggle (?) in the corner. (3) "Tips" badge on first-encounter controls.
- **Implement button visibility tiers in the element toolbar** — Show only essential buttons by default (expand, include/exclude, edit). Secondary buttons (suggest, retry) appear only in the expanded panel.
- **Add confirmation feedback for in-place Master CV edits** — Green checkmark, toast message, or persistent "Save" button state after saving.
- **Include "You've completed X. Next up: Y" stage-transition messages** — Bridge the gap where no message guides the next step after phase transitions.
- **Explicitly surface ATS score context** — Add context to the badge: "ATS Score: 87% (based on current CV)" and "Click to see which keywords are matched/missing."

---

## UX Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Document-centric paradigm** — Shifting from 26 scattered tabs to "document is the UI" directly addresses the context-switching pain point and "no sense of the whole."
- **In-place element editing and control discovery** — The dual expand/collapse model (section-level summary badges + element-level hover toolbars) is elegant and fixes the current DataTable fragmentation.
- **Ghost items for inclusion decisions** — Rendering excluded elements inline with muted/strikethrough provides context the current tables lack.
- **Inline spell check** — Moving spell-check corrections from a separate tab into inline underlines with popover corrections is a significant workflow improvement.
- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Placing questions adjacent to the requirements they relate to eliminates the chat-only burial problem.
- **Always-available Master CV tab** — Lifting the finalise-stage gate respects user autonomy.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Auto-switching document tabs risks loss of user control** — If a user is editing the Master CV and the workflow auto-advances, does the view snap away? The hybrid model (auto-switch + user override) needs a "pin this tab" control or explicit "recommended view" indicator.
- **Hover-state discoverability remains fragile** — Toolbar appearing only "on hover" hides critical actions from keyboard-only and low-vision users. Section 9 must specify how toolbars become keyboard-accessible.
- **Element expand persistence unclear** — Section 15 leaves this as an open question, but it directly impacts cognitive load. Proposal: collapse on tab-away with an optional "remember expanded state" toggle.
- **Spell-check integration timing ambiguous** — Does inline spell check replace the dedicated phase entirely, or supplement it? This must be clarified.
- **Section and element state explosion** — 8+ visual states, each relying heavily on colour. Must include non-colour indicators (e.g., "⊙ Pending suggestion" label, icon prefix) for accessibility.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Formalize auto-tab-switching with a "View Mode" setting** — *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, show a breadcrumb before switching so it isn't invisible.
- **Make hover toolbars keyboard-reachable immediately** — Each element container receives `tabindex="0"`; on focus, toolbar buttons remain visible. Consider a "Show All Controls" view toggle.
- **Add element-state badges to replace colour-only signaling** — Badges adjacent to element text: "⊙ Pending suggestion", "✓ Accepted", "✗ Declined". Ensures colour-blind users understand state.
- **Clarify spell-check phase integration** — State explicitly: "The Spell Check step displays the CV view with inline underlines. Users correct, then proceed to Layout Review."
- **Provide "collapse all / expand all" at section and document levels** — Add buttons: "[Collapse all elements]" / "[Expand all elements]" in the sticky settings bar.
- **Define the undo stack boundary for inline edits** — Inline edits add to a per-session undo stack; Ctrl+Z reverts the last edit within the active element. Never committed to Master CV until explicit save.

---

## Accessibility Specialist

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Document-centric layout reduces tab-switching cognitive load** — Fewer navigation context switches benefit users with cognitive or motor disabilities.
- **Inline editing preserves focus locality** — Keeps edits in-place, reducing the burden on users with short-term memory challenges.
- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — Eliminates the need to context-switch between chat and structured data for screen reader users.
- **Explicit keyboard alternative for drag-to-reorder** — ↑↓ buttons directly address GAP-120 and GAP-72.
- **Consistent expand/collapse model** — A single ▶/▼ toggle pattern makes expand/collapse semantics predictable for screen readers.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Removes the barrier preventing keyboard users from reaching critical data-entry in earlier phases.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Hover-only controls remain critical accessibility red flags** — Sections 8 and 9 describe toolbars that appear "on hover." This **replicates and amplifies the current hover-control gap** and fails WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus). No alternative activation method is documented.
- **Contenteditable accessibility unspecified** — No guidance on screen-reader announcements for edit-mode entry/exit, cursor positioning, or undo availability.
- **No announcement strategy for accept/decline actions** — Screen reader users will not be notified that actions succeeded without `aria-live` support.
- **Auto-scroll and flash-highlight animations conflict with prefers-reduced-motion** — Section 7's flash animation violates WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3; no alternative provided.
- **Tab bar overflow behavior unresolved** — Section 15 defers this; all overflow patterns require keyboard-operable alternatives.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Replace hover-only controls with focus-triggered disclosure** — Toolbar is a `role="toolbar"` container; appears on keyboard focus and hover. Standard keyboard navigation: Tab to move between buttons, Enter/Space to activate.
- **Document contenteditable accessibility requirements** — Each editable field carries `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, and an `aria-live="polite"` announce region. Screen readers informed when edit mode begins/ends.
- **Add live-region announcements for suggestion actions** — On ✅/❌ activate: `aria-live="assertive"` region announces "Suggestion accepted. Bullet 3 updated. Press ↑ to move, Ctrl+Z to undo."
- **Implement prefers-reduced-motion wrapper** — Flash/pulse animations replaced with static 2-second color hold under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **Define keyboard alternatives for tab-bar overflow** — "More documents" button with `aria-label`; dropdown with arrow-key navigation, Enter to select.
- **Specify reorder confirmation via live region** — "Moved up. Item 2 of 5." announced immediately after ↑/↓ activation; element receives focus after move.

## Graphical Designer

### What the proposed design gets right

- **"The document is the UI" thesis** — Editing in-place within the live preview eliminates context-switching and preserves the WYSIWYG promise throughout customisation.
- **Inline controls over separate tabs** — Hover toolbars and inline element-expand replace fragmented tab-per-section navigation, concentrating all actions near the elements they affect.
- **Ghost-item visibility pattern** — Strikethrough/50% opacity/dashed border excluded items create coherent inline visual contrast.
- **Collapsible sections with summary badges** — Creates scannability for dense documents without expanding everything on first load.
- **Sticky settings bar** — Consolidating Length, Style, ATS Score, and Regenerate eliminates hunting for controls across modals.
- **Analysis clarification questions embedded inline** — Creates stronger context and avoids the chat/viewer toggle.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline hover toolbars risk visual clutter and accidental activation** — 10+ buttons on every hover over 30+ bullets creates cognitive overload and UI flicker. Reducing to 3–4 core visible actions with a "more" menu is needed.
- **Pending-suggestion amber boxes may conflict with CV's visual hierarchy** — Amber borders on a professional resume appear as editorial artifacts rather than integrated guidance. A softer background tint would be less disruptive.
- **In-place contenteditable may not preserve final PDF fidelity** — Formatting state (bold, italic, list nesting) can be accidentally introduced; the current DataTable enforces plaintext. Strict input validation needed.
- **Expanded element panel typography may not scale** — On a typical laptop (1366px), the multi-row expanded panel grows very tall. Consider max-height with overflow scroll or a drawer alternative.
- **No guidance on undo integration with inline editing** — Contenteditable undo is browser-dependent and fragile; the proposal needs a concrete undo strategy.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Reduce the default element hover toolbar to 3 core buttons** — Keep ▼ (expand), ✗ (exclude), ↑↓ (reorder) always visible; tuck ✓, ✏️, ✨, ✅, ❌, 🔄 into a three-dot menu.
- **Apply a subtle background tint instead of amber border** — 10–15% amber background fill behind pending elements + a small 6px amber dot to the left. Less graphic competition with CV typography.
- **Require explicit Save for contenteditable fields, with a diff preview** — Side-by-side diff (original vs. edited) with "Save" and "Cancel" before persisting.
- **Constrain expanded panel height** — `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` on the element card; scrollable with visible scrollbar indicator.
- **Add font family and colour theme controls to the settings bar** — Font family (Inter/Garamond/Calibri) and theme (Professional Blue / Warm Neutral / Bold Contrast) dropdown; addresses existing gap US-G3.
- **Display a live page-break preview** — Mini page-stack icon with colour-coded warning (green ≤2 pages, amber 2–2.5, red >2.5) in the sticky settings bar. "View page breaks" toggle highlights break points in the rendered CV.

---

## Resume Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Eliminates context-switching penalty** — Editing bullets while seeing live output directly addresses the fundamental pain point.
- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Reduces friction of bouncing between chat and analysis data.
- **Expanded element panel with original/current/proposed comparison** — All three versions of content in one place is critical for resume strategy decisions.
- **Ghost item reveal pattern** — Prevents the dangerous situation where a user forgets they excluded a strong bullet.
- **Section-level bulk actions with explicit accept/decline** — Makes it possible to act on suggestions quickly.
- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Allows users to correct source data mid-session.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Bulk-accept safety risk** — "Accept all" in Experience or Skills with one click is dangerous; LLM batch suggestions may contain subtle errors requiring per-item review. The current Rewrite Review tab forces explicit per-item decisions.
- **Formatting preservation during in-place editing unclear** — If a user deletes a line break or removes parenthetical context, will formatting break? Current implementation enforces constraints via review UI, not in-place editing.
- **Missing severity sort in spell-check integration** — Spell issues shown in order-received may cause a user to address comma placement while missing a name typo.
- **ATS comments row lacks synonym grouping context** — The current review flags that synonyms (ML / Machine Learning) are not grouped; the proposal does not clarify whether they will be.
- **CV style switcher clarity ambiguous** — "Plain/ATS" in the dropdown is unclear about what it produces vs. "Sidebar."

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a confirmation modal for "Accept all" actions** — "Accept all N suggestions in [Section]?" with options to "Review each", "Accept all", or "Cancel."
- **Validate in-place edits against resume conventions** — Real-time or on-blur: line-length warning (70–85 chars ideal), fragment check, keyword consistency check; non-blocking warnings only.
- **Sort spell-check issues by severity** — Priority 1: spelling errors (names, companies). Priority 2: grammar/fragment. Priority 3: stylistic suggestions.
- **Add a "Grouped Keywords" view to ATS comments** — Group keyword matches by canonical term: **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]. Closes the existing synonym gap.
- **Clarify CV style switcher with previews** — Include "Compare styles" that renders the current section in both Sidebar and Plain/ATS side-by-side in a collapsible preview pane.
- **Preserve section-expand state across tab switches** — Store state in sessionStorage keyed on section name; prevents re-expanding a section you were working on.

## Hiring Manager

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live preview throughout customisation** — Users see immediately when a rewritten bullet becomes too long, when a skill disrupts visual balance, or when section headings are malformed.
- **In-place inline editing preserves document integrity** — Users can evaluate edits against the rendered resume context in real-time.
- **Ghost-style hidden elements solve a credibility risk** — Catches the silent failure of submitting incomplete job entries with only 1 accepted bullet.
- **Sticky settings bar for output control** — Length/Style/ATS/Pages controls always accessible without tab-switching.
- **Embedded clarification questions** — Reduces ambiguity and keeps analysis rationale transparent.
- **Element expansion panels provide rich decision context** — Original, Current, Proposed, Model recommendation, ATS comments, and Persuasion comments in one view.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks accidental quality degradation** — All CV content editable in-place can introduce formatting errors (stray newlines, copy-paste artifacts) that are not visible until Download. Strong autosave + undo and a "Preview as PDF" step are critical.
- **No mention of final validation gates before export** — The current design fires validation warnings at the Download tab. The proposal does not specify whether these gates remain or move elsewhere.
- **Master CV always-present may create version-control confusion** — If Master CV edits are not reversible, accidental writes could damage the shared source-of-truth with no recovery path.
- **No specification for style-switcher state persistence** — If the user selects "ATS Plain" and then downloads twice, is there a risk of version mismatch?

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a pre-Download validation checklist modal** — Before Download: confirm page count, persuasion warnings acknowledged, no pending inline saves, spell-check resolved.
- **Implement a "Preview as PDF" button in the settings bar** — Opens a real PDF preview in a modal before Download; catches formatting errors that HTML rendering misses.
- **Mark Master CV edits with a "dirty" indicator and require explicit confirmation** — Red dot on tab, "Unsaved changes" warning, timestamp-logged saves.
- **Add a "Revert to Session Start" option for CV edits** — Restore CV to the state at the start of Customisation. Safety valve if inline edits cascade incorrectly.
- **Specify style-switcher behavior with a visual badge** — Active style prominently displayed; Download filenames include the style (`resume_ATS.pdf` vs. `resume_Sidebar.pdf`).
- **Integrate page-count warnings into the settings bar directly** — Live color badge (green ≤2, amber 2–2.5, red >2.5) with tooltip explaining the threshold.

## HR / ATS Specialist

### What the proposed design gets right

- **ATS Score badge and drill-down in settings bar** — Constant compliance visibility eliminates the current "Compute ATS Score" empty-state button users overlook.
- **Keyword highlighting in Job view** — Amber highlighting for matched terms and red for missing required keywords teaches users what gaps remain before customisation begins.
- **ATS comments in expanded element panel** — Users making editorial decisions see ATS impact alongside persuasion and model recommendation in one place.
- **Plain/ATS style option in settings bar** — Toggle between human-readable (Sidebar) and ATS-safe layout; makes the tradeoff visible.
- **Hard-requirement keyword coverage now visible inline** — Summary badges ("3 of 7 bullets included") let users scan inclusion rate per section.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Enables mid-session skill updates and consistent skill classification.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing risks ATS-safe formatting** — If ATS DOCX generation doesn't re-normalize edited text (stripping bold/italic, standardizing line breaks), inline edits could corrupt ATS parsing.
- **ATS validation gate missing in proposed workflow** — The current File Review tab enforces a 17-check validation report. The proposal does not detail how the validation report integrates or gates downloads.
- **Spell-check underline could interfere with ATS scoring** — If underline metadata leaks into the DOCX export, it could corrupt text extraction or keyword matching.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add an "ATS Safe Editing" toggle in the settings bar** — When enabled, contenteditable fields strip formatting on blur and the settings bar shows: "Inline edits will be normalized for ATS compliance."
- **Embed ATS validation status in the settings bar** — A "Validation Status" badge (green ✓ / amber ⚠ / red ✗) that updates live; displays count of failing checks. Clicking opens the full 17-check report.
- **Add a "Hard Requirements Coverage" widget to the Analysis view** — After embedded clarification questions: **Hard Required Keywords: N / M**, with red warning if < 100%. Each unmatched keyword links to the relevant section.
- **Clarify the ATS DOCX export path from inline edits** — Document a clear rule: all text re-normalized (formatting stripped, line breaks standardized) before export; validation check compares ATS DOCX text to session state.
- **Define synonym / variant handling in ATS comments** — Note when a keyword is matched via synonym (e.g., "Matched as: 'ML' variant of 'Machine Learning'"); validation gate should apply the same synonym rules.
- **Add a "Missing Keywords" insertion suggestion in element expand** — When ATS comments note a missing hard-requirement keyword, auto-suggest an insertion point: "This bullet mentions DevOps but not Terraform. Consider appending: '… using Terraform.'"

## Master CV Curator

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Directly addresses GAP-41. No longer locked to `finalise` stage; the first document tab and available at any time.
- **Unified in-place editing with explicit Master CV save gates** — Session documents update immediately; Master CV changes require explicit "Save" confirmation. Prevents accidental writes to the permanent record.
- **Expanded element panel with "Original" row** — Shows Original (read-only, from Master CV), Current (session), and Proposed (LLM) with data lineage crystal clear in a single visual context.
- **Ghost-style excluded items inline** — Preserves the "document-is-the-UI" principle while maintaining the visual boundary between included and excluded content.
- **Contextual highlighting** — Blue left-border accent on the active section, paired with chat breadcrumb, reinforces which part is under focus and where master data ends.
- **Inline spell check** — Keeps the "document is the UI" philosophy intact and eliminates tab-switching for closely related editing.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Master CV state boundaries harder to enforce in always-on model** — The current design makes mid-workflow Master CV writes structurally impossible. The proposal relies entirely on backend phase gating being infallible; UI/UX burden shifts to the backend entirely.
- **Proposed → Current → Session state coupling unclear** — When a user expands an element and accepts a suggestion, does this promote to Current immediately, or only after a Save? The proposal doesn't clarify when Proposed suggestions are formally captured.
- **Loss of explicit harvest/archive boundary** — The proposal does not clarify whether the two-phase harvest workflow (1. Finalise & Archive, 2. Optional: Update Master CV) is preserved or merged into the unified document viewer.
- **Inline analysis answers may fragment the chat narrative** — Embedding answerable questions in Analysis view creates two parallel input streams (left-pane chat and right-pane inline). This could confuse the agent's reasoning trail.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Formalize Master CV write-confirmation with phase context** — If session is not in `init` or `refinement`, show: "Cannot edit master data while a job customisation is active. Archive the job first, then return here."
- **Clarify the Proposed → Current pipeline** — Accepting a suggestion moves Proposed to Current in-place but does not write to master data. Changes are held in session state and written to master only via explicit harvest post-finalisation. Add a "Session" badge on the Current field.
- **Preserve explicit harvest/archive boundaries** — After the archive step, show a distinct second card titled "Step 2: Review & Apply Master CV Updates (Optional)" to keep the two-phase lifecycle visible.
- **Inline Analysis answers should post to left-pane chat** — When a user answers inline, the answer posts to chat as a user message and is processed by the agent. Visual affordance (arrow icon, "Post to chat" button) makes this flow obvious.
- **Define Master CV element save trigger explicitly** — Before closing an expanded element or navigating away, show a "Save" button with unsaved indicator. Clicking Save runs `_require_master_data_write_phase` and writes with a timestamped backup.
- **Add a mini-legend for Original/Current/Proposed rows** — "?" icon with tooltip: "**Original:** from your Master CV (read-only). **Current:** your session edits. **Proposed:** AI suggestion."
