## Persuasion Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document context during editing** — Users see immediate impact of framing decisions on the rendered resume, directly supporting persuasive-intent evaluation.
- **Inline "Persuasion comments" row in expanded element panels** — Currently surfaced only in the separate Rewrite Review tab; inline placement is a major discoverability upgrade.
- **Model recommendation badges integrated into element expansion** — Consolidates Emphasize/Include/De-emphasize/Exclude signals adjacent to persuasion and ATS feedback.
- **Iterative in-place editing** — The expanded panel's "✏️ Accept with inline editing" lowers friction to iterate on rewrite suggestions.
- **Contextual highlighting of the active workflow section** — Keeps persuasive framing decisions anchored to intent.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Allows strong framing decisions to flow back to the master record rather than being one-off session edits.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Persuasion comments row is present but not specified** — The proposal lists "Persuasion comments" as a data row but does not specify: what checks it contains, who generates it, or how it differs from the current collapsible warning panel.
- **No explicit gating of submission on persuasion acknowledgement** — Current design gates "Submit All Decisions" on `persuasionWarningsAcknowledged`. The proposed design's Section 9 does not specify whether a form-level gate remains.
- **Ghost-style excluded elements may undermine persuasion coherence** — A user might include a mediocre bullet without checking persuasion comments. Proposal does not specify whether ghost elements trigger warnings.
- **Persuasion comments only visible on expand** — A high-priority persuasion flag (e.g., passive voice) does not bubble to the collapsed view unless specified, so most users will never see it.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Specify the "Persuasion comments" data structure and generation** — Clarify whether this row displays the existing eight checks as prose ("Strong verb ✓, Passive voice ⚠️") or a new LLM-generated commentary.
- **Explicit persuasion gate at phase-exit** — "Submitting this phase requires addressing all ⚠️ Persuasion flags or marking them as reviewed."
- **High-priority persuasion flags surface in collapsed element view** — A small warning badge (⚠️ or 🔴) appears next to the collapsed element text when passive voice, hedging, or absent result clause is detected.
- **Persuasion comment prioritisation by impact** — Weight passive voice, hedging, absent result clause, and weak verb above structural notes (word count, CAR pattern).
- **Inline CAR-structure suggestion in the expanded panel** — If an element lacks a Challenge component, add a "Suggest CAR structure" button in the expanded panel.
- **Cross-document framing check on phase advance** — When exiting Customisation, compare narrative threads in Experience bullets against the Summary opening. Warn if they lead with different role identities (e.g., bullets emphasise data engineering, summary opens with ML leadership).

## Power User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Persistent resume visibility** — Editing while seeing the actual document eliminates the current workflow where edits happen blind until Layout Review.
- **In-place element controls eliminate tab churn** — Hover toolbars and expand panels replace the DataTable-per-tab model.
- **Section-level batch actions** — "Accept all", "Decline all", and "Suggest section" provide the bulk-review path currently missing.
- **Inline editing across all document types** — No intermediate "save to DataTable" step; changes are session-immediate.
- **Auto-tab switching as workflow context** — Reduces the mental overhead of "which tab should I be in now?"
- **Ghost-style excluded elements stay visible** — Power users can see at a glance what's been ruled out without a filter toggle hunt.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Hover-only controls still risk discoverability** — Section-header "Accept all" is not immediately obvious; a power user unfamiliar with the new design may miss that section headers are interactive.
- **No keyboard shortcuts mentioned** — The redesign is completely silent on keyboard acceleration, which was already the #1 power-user gap. This is a significant regression.
- **Auto-tab switching may disrupt keyboard-driven workflows** — If auto-switch fires while a user is navigating via keyboard, focus is lost and keyboard flow is broken.
- **Expand/collapse UX for 30+ items may be slower** — Users must expand each section, then expand elements within. The current DataTable keeps all rows visible; full-text search on a DataTable row finds a single bullet in seconds.
- **No multi-row checkbox selection** — The current DataTable supports multi-row selection for bulk actions. The proposal offers no cross-element checkbox or "select subset" affordance.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add keyboard shortcuts for all hover-toolbar actions** — Alt+A for "Accept", Alt+D for "Decline", Alt+↓ for "Move down", Alt+E for "Expand". Bind at element level for the currently focused element. Document in a persistent keyboard help overlay (? key).
- **Make hover-toolbar buttons visible at rest, muted** — Render toolbars at ~30% opacity at rest, increasing to 100% on hover. Maintains clean visual hierarchy while making the affordance discoverable.
- **Add a "flat list" / "DataTable" view toggle for high-item sections** — For sections with 15+ items (publications, achievements), provide a checkbox-based DataTable view alongside the expand/collapse model. Power users switch to table view for bulk selection and filtering.
- **Implement explicit focus management and optional auto-tab-switch disable** — When auto-switch fires, set focus to the new tab's first interactive element. Settings toggle: "Auto-switch document tabs on workflow phase change."
- **Add a "collapse all" button in the CV view settings bar** — Save users from clicking the collapse icon on every element when reviewing a section.
- **Expose inline edit mode via keyboard shortcut with predictable undo** — Bind Ctrl+E (or I) to enter edit mode on focused element. Use native `<textarea>` instead of contenteditable for predictable Ctrl+Z undo.

## Recruiter-Ops

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document visibility** — Rendering the CV throughout customisation eliminates the context-switching cost of flipping between Bullets, Summary, and Skills tabs.
- **Section-level batch controls** — "Suggest section", "Accept all", "Decline all" directly address high-volume throughput.
- **Ghost-style excluded items inline** — No navigation step needed to see which bullets or skills were excluded.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Recruiters often need to update contact info or add a new skill mid-workflow; currently this is blocked.
- **Contextual auto-tab-switching** — Keeps the focus aligned with the current task without manual navigation.
- **Embedded clarification questions** — Keeps context near data, reducing the need to scroll back in chat history.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline editing as a throughput tax** — The always-on editing surface may slow down workflows where the user wants to review without changing anything. No "review-only mode" is proposed.
- **Auto-tab-switching could be disruptive** — A recruiter flipping between Job and CV for side-by-side comparison would be interrupted by auto-switching.
- **Contextual section highlighting (blue borders) may fatigue** — If the active section changes frequently, the blue accent could create visual noise for users scanning multiple sections.
- **Element expand persistence undefined** — If expansions collapse on tab-switch, the user loses scroll position when jumping to the Job tab and back.
- **No session-level multi-application overview** — GAP-RO4 remains unaddressed. For Recruiter-Ops managing 20+ active applications, this is still a gap.
- **Batch operations limited to section level** — No document-level or session-level "Accept all suggestions" is mentioned.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Explicit "Review-only mode"** — Toggle in the CV settings bar to lock the document to read-only, disabling contenteditable and inline saves. Fast path through multiple applications without accidental edits.
- **Session-level batch actions** — A document-level "Accept all pending suggestions across all sections" button in the CV settings bar.
- **Tab-switch confirmation when in active edit** — If the user has unsaved inline changes, auto-tab-switching should suppress or prompt "You have unsaved changes; switch anyway?"
- **Collapsed section summary badges always show suggestion count** — Ensure the summary badge ("3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions") is visible even when the section is collapsed.
- **Confirm cover letter and screening documents are in File Review** — Explicitly state that all generated documents appear in the final Download/Finalise workflow.
- **Provide a "fast finalise" flow** — A collapsible finalise summary card in the CV settings bar: generated files, ATS score, application status dropdown, and notes textarea. Allows finalisation without leaving the CV view.

## Returning User

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Persistent session context via auto-tab-switching** — Auto-switching to the relevant document tab naturally restores the working session without requiring manual navigation.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Returning users can verify and update foundational data at any point; removes the anxiety of discovering errors too late.
- **Prior decisions visible in-place via ghost items** — The **(+N hidden)** badge provides a quick visual summary of exclusions without hunting through tabs.
- **Inline suggestion workflow reduces tab-switching fatigue** — Pending suggestions appear with amber borders directly on elements; no detour to the Rewrite Review tab.
- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Returning users resuming job analysis immediately see what needs clarification without scrolling chat history.
- **Live document-as-UI eliminates the "resume only at layout stage" problem** — Users immediately see the cumulative effect of prior decisions.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **No explicit restored-decisions summary on initial re-entry** — No "welcome back" panel showing session state ("4 experiences selected, 12 skills, 7 approved rewrites"). The current "✅ Session restored: {positionName} ({phase})" confirmation should have an equivalent.
- **Workflow step pills location unclear** — Moving step pills to a compact top bar or collapsible sidebar risks burying session progress. A returning user should see their workflow position at a glance without hovering.
- **Expanded elements may not persist across tab switches** — Section 15 leaves this unresolved. A returning user mid-edit of an experience bullet switching tabs and back may find all expansions collapsed.
- **No explicit mention of scroll position restoration** — Should the CV view scroll back to the last-edited section, or reset to the top?
- **Inline editing increases state-save complexity** — The proposal doesn't specify debounce timing, conflict handling for concurrent tab edits, or rollback on validation failure.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Add a restored-decisions summary banner on session re-entry** — Collapsible banner showing: "Session restored: 4 of 7 experiences selected • 12 skills • 3 pending rewrites • 2 clarification questions open." Auto-hide after 10 seconds.
- **Pin the workflow step pills to a sticky header with visible labels** — Full phase names (not abbreviated). Persistent left-panel strip or compact sticky top bar. A returning user should know their position without hover.
- **Define and document element expand-state persistence** — Specify that expanded panels persist across tab switches (stored in session state). Visual indicator (dot on section badge) showing "N elements expanded."
- **Implement scroll position restoration on session reload** — Scroll CV view to the section that was last active in the prior session (stored in `status.last_active_section`); smooth scroll behavior.
- **Specify contenteditable debounce and conflict handling** — CV edits debounce with 2-second delay before API save; concurrent-tab conflicts show "conflict detected—reload?" modal; failed saves rollback to last-known state.
- **Extend the Analysis view to show clarification answer history** — A collapsible "Answered" section with prior responses. Include "Clear and re-answer" option for revision.

## Trust & Compliance

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Expanded element panel retains original/current/proposed three-row audit trail** — All three versions surfaced side-by-side during inline editing; provenance of every edit is visible at the moment of decision.
- **Inline suggestion acceptance with mandatory decision visibility** — Amber border boxes on each element force users to encounter suggestions in context, reducing the risk of accidental bulk acceptance.
- **Ghost item reveal pattern provides explicit inclusion/exclusion audit** — Strikethrough/50% opacity excluded items with traceability are a substantial improvement over exclusion decisions made in separate tabs.
- **Master CV always-accessible tab** — Permanent access to the authoritative source improves trust.
- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — Users cannot accidentally ignore AI-derived questions before generating rewrites.
- **Contextual section highlighting** — Grounds users in which section is being customised, reducing the risk of blind bulk-accept operations on the wrong section.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Section-level bulk "Accept all" introduces compliance risk** — One click accepts all LLM-proposed rewrites in a section without requiring the user to expand and review any of them. The current rewrite-review tab enforces explicit per-item review.
- **In-place contenteditable editing without explicit save-on-change confirmation** — The implicit-persist model (blur or explicit save) is weaker than the current explicit Master CV "Save" confirmation. Users may inadvertently edit and lose focus, triggering an invisible state update.
- **Element-expand persistence left open** — If panels collapse on tab-switch, users lose context of which elements were being evaluated; reintroduces the context-loss problem the redesign aims to solve.
- **Undo/rollback mechanism not defined** — Users who misclick or accidentally overwrite content have no documented recovery path.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Gate "Accept all" behind element-expansion checkpoint** — Require that at least one pending element has been expanded and explicitly acted upon before "Accept all" becomes enabled for that section.
- **Explicit "Session checkpoint" before finalisation** — A read-only summary of all pending suggestions per section before proceeding: "Experience: 3 pending · Skills: 1 pending · Summary: 0 pending."
- **Add a persistent "Draft" badge and audit breadcrumb to inline edits** — A brief "(edited by user on 2026-06-13)" footer in the expanded element panel distinguishes LLM-proposed rewrites from manual edits.
- **Clarify Master CV save workflow with explicit lock/unlock pattern** — "Unlock & Save" confirmation with backup-before-write and schema-validation-on-write documentation.
- **Replace implicit blur-save with explicit Save button** — Show an inline "Save" button after the user types. Only on Save does session state update. Aligns CV editing model with the Master CV model.
- **Embed "⚠ AI-generated" label on Proposed row** — Ensures users apply appropriate scrutiny to LLM-generated rewrites, particularly for skill additions and summary variants.

---

## Synthesis

### Cross-Persona Themes

Five issues were raised independently by multiple personas, indicating systemic design concerns that must be resolved before implementation:

#### Theme 1: Hover-Only Controls Are Inaccessible and Undiscoverable
**Raised by:** Accessibility Specialist, Power User, First-Time User, UX Expert, Graphical Designer (5 of 14 personas)

The biggest cross-cutting concern. All these personas flagged that hover-only toolbars exclude keyboard users, are fragile on touch devices, and are not discoverable without prior training. The current design already has critical gaps GAP-120 and GAP-72 from hover-only patterns; the proposed design amplifies rather than fixes this.

**Consensus recommendation:** Focus-triggered disclosure with toolbars as `role="toolbar"` containers. Low-opacity persistent buttons at rest (30% opacity), full opacity on hover/focus. Keyboard shortcuts (Alt+A, Alt+D, Alt+↑/↓) for all common actions.

#### Theme 2: Bulk "Accept All" Is a Compliance and Quality Risk
**Raised by:** Trust & Compliance, Resume Expert, Power User, Persuasion Expert (4 of 14 personas)

Section-level bulk accept is convenient but bypasses the per-item review that the current Rewrite Review tab enforces. One click can accept a dozen LLM rewrites across an Experience section without the user reading any of them.

**Consensus recommendation:** Require at least one explicit per-element decision in a section before enabling "Accept all" for that section. Add a count: "Accept all 7 remaining suggestions in Experience?"

#### Theme 3: Word-Level Diff View Is Missing from Element Expand Panel
**Raised by:** Applicant, Resume Expert (2 of 14 personas)

The current Rewrite Review tab shows word-level LCS diff (deleted text in red, added text in green). The new "Proposed" text field is a plain text box with no visual diff, making it harder to judge the magnitude of an AI rewrite at a glance.

**Consensus recommendation:** Render the Proposed row with LCS word-diff highlighting (removed in red strikethrough, added in green underline) alongside the editable textarea.

#### Theme 4: Undo Model Is Undefined and Contenteditable Is Fragile
**Raised by:** UX Expert, Power User, Graphical Designer, Trust & Compliance, Returning User (5 of 14 personas)

Browser contenteditable undo is unreliable across browsers and formatting contexts. Multiple personas independently raised this as a high-risk open question. The proposal acknowledges it in Section 15 but defers it.

**Consensus recommendation:** Use native `<textarea>` instead of contenteditable wherever possible. Maintain an app-level per-session undo stack. Replace blur-save with explicit "Save" buttons that appear on typing.

#### Theme 5: Auto-Tab-Switching Needs User Control
**Raised by:** UX Expert, Power User, Recruiter-Ops, Returning User (4 of 14 personas)

Automatic context switching is helpful for new users but disruptive for experienced users who are doing side-by-side comparison (Job vs. CV), keyboard-driven workflows, or multi-application throughput reviews. Auto-switch that fires while the user is mid-edit can break focus and lose work.

**Consensus recommendation:** Add a "View Mode" toggle: *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, show a breadcrumb notification before switching; suppress auto-switch if the user has unsaved changes.

---

### Top 5 Recommended Enhancements

These five enhancements address the highest-impact, cross-persona concerns and should be incorporated into the design before implementation begins.

**1. Keyboard-Accessible Focus-Triggered Controls (resolves Theme 1)**
Replace all hover-only toolbars (Sections 8, 9) with focus-triggered disclosure: element containers have `tabindex="0"`, toolbars appear on Tab focus and hover, all buttons are keyboard-operable with Alt+key shortcuts. Add `role="toolbar"` with standard Tab/Enter/Space navigation. Resolve GAP-120 and GAP-72 at the design level rather than deferring to implementation.

**2. Word-Level Diff in the Proposed Row (resolves Theme 3)**
Add LCS-based word-level diff rendering to the Proposed row in every expanded element panel. Removed text shown in red strikethrough; added text in green underline. This preserves the core value of the current Rewrite Review tab without requiring a separate tab.

**3. Gate "Accept All" Behind at Least One Element Review (resolves Theme 2)**
The section-level "Accept all" button (Section 8) is disabled until at least one element in the section has been expanded and explicitly acted upon (accepted, edited, or declined). Show a count badge: "Accept all 5 remaining suggestions." This preserves the current rewrite-review's protection against blind bulk acceptance while keeping bulk operations available.

**4. Explicit Save Button with App-Level Undo Stack (resolves Theme 4)**
Replace blur-save on contenteditable/textarea fields with an explicit inline "Save" button that appears after the user types (similar to GitHub inline comment editing). Use native `<textarea>` elements. Maintain a per-session undo stack (not relying on browser undo) so Ctrl+Z reverts the last element edit reliably.

**5. "View Mode" Toggle: Smart vs. Manual Auto-Tab-Switching (resolves Theme 5)**
Add a Settings option: *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, display a 1-second notification before switching: "Switching to CV view for Customisation phase ✕ Stay here." Suppress auto-switch entirely if the user has unsaved edits or if "Manual" is active. Default to Smart for new users, Manual for returning users who have set a preference.

---

*End of persona review. Next step: incorporate these recommendations into a revised version of [tasks/ui-redesign-proposal.md](ui-redesign-proposal.md) and create implementation tickets in [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md).*

1	<!--

8	
9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Draft — for persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-13
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md)
15	
16	---
17	
18	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
19	
20	### Problem with the Current Design
21	
22	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
23	
24	Key pain points:
25	
26	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
27	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
28	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
29	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
30	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
31	
32	### Design Thesis
33	
34	> **The document is the UI.**
35	
36	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
37	
38	### Primary Goals
39	
40	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
41	|------|---------|----------|
42	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
43	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
44	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
45	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
46	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
47	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
48	
49	---
50	
51	## 2. Layout Architecture
52	
53	```
54	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
56	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
57	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
58	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
59	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
60	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
61	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
62	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
63	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
64	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  with inline controls on hover       │  │
65	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
66	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
67	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
68	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
69	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
70	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
71	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
72	```
73	
74	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
75	
76	### Document Tabs
77	
78	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
79	|-----|---------|-----------------|
80	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
81	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
82	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
83	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
84	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
85	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
86	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
87	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
88	
89	**Auto-switching:** The viewer automatically switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. The user can always click any tab to override. The active tab is remembered and restored on session reload.
90	
91	### Workflow Step Pills
92	
93	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact top bar** with abbreviated step labels, or a **collapsible left-sidebar strip** below the chat input — keeping the main content area maximised.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 3. Job Description View
98	
99	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
100	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
101	- Scrollable; no truncation
102	
103	---
104	
105	## 4. Analysis View
106	
107	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
108	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
109	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
110	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
111	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
112	
113	---
114	
115	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
116	
117	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
118	
119	```
120	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
121	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
122	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
123	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
124	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
125	```
126	
127	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
128	|---------|---------------------|
129	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
130	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. |
131	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Click opens ATS detail overlay. |
132	| **Pages** | Estimated page count. Amber if 2–2.5 pages, red if > 2.5. |
133	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
134	
135	---
136	
137	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
138	
139	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
140	
141	### Section States
142	
143	| State | What is shown |
144	|-------|--------------|
145	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
146	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
147	
148	### Element States
149	
150	| State | What is shown |
151	|-------|--------------|
152	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Hover toolbar visible on hover. |
153	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
154	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only |
155	| | **Current** — the version active in this session, editable in-place |
156	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated), editable in-place before accepting |
157	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude` |
158	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues |
159	| | **Persuasion comments** — impact framing assessment, verb strength, specificity notes |
160	
161	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
162	
163	All text fields in the expanded element panel are **editable in-place** (contenteditable or inline textarea). Changes are saved on blur or on explicit "Save" within the element.
164	
165	---
166	
167	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
168	
169	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
170	
171	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
172	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
173	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
174	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **auto-scrolls** to that element and briefly highlights it (flash animation)
175	
176	---
177	
178	## 8. Section-Level Controls (on hover over section header)
179	
180	Each resume section header reveals a floating control bar on hover:
181	
182	| Control | Action |
183	|---------|--------|
184	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section |
185	| **👁 Show hidden (N)** | Reveal excluded elements in ghost style within this section |
186	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
187	| **✅ Accept all** | Accept all pending suggestions in this section |
188	| **❌ Decline all** | Decline all pending suggestions in this section |
189	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode for this section's elements |
190	
191	---
192	
193	## 9. Element-Level Controls (on hover over each element)
194	
195	Each bullet, skill, achievement, publication, or other element shows a **floating toolbar** on hover. The toolbar appears to the right of or above the element and disappears when focus leaves.
196	
197	| Button | Action |
198	|--------|--------|
199	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
200	| **✓** | Include this element (if currently excluded) |
201	| **✗** | Exclude this element (if currently included) |
202	| **↑ / ↓** | Move element up / down within section |
203	| **✏️** | Enter inline edit mode on the current text |
204	| **✨** | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
205	| **✅** | Accept pending suggestion |
206	| **✏️ Accept** | Accept suggestion with inline editing before confirming |
207	| **❌** | Decline pending suggestion |
208	| **🔄** | Retry suggestion generation |
209	
210	For elements with a pending suggestion, the toolbar shows the suggestion controls prominently; other controls are available but secondary.
211	
212	---
213	
214	## 10. Visual States for Elements
215	
216	| State | Visual Treatment |
217	|-------|-----------------|
218	| **Active / Included** | Normal rendering, full opacity |
219	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Shown only when section is in "show hidden" mode: muted gray, 50% opacity, strikethrough on text, dashed left border |
220	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber/yellow border box around element; amber dot in section summary badge; remains until accept/edit/decline |
221	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green flash on border, then returns to normal |
222	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red flash on border, amber border removed |
223	| **Currently active (workflow focus)** | Blue left-border accent, subtle blue background tint |
224	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow highlight fade after drop |
225	| **Inline edit mode** | White background, visible border, cursor positioned in text |
226	| **Saved / confirmed** | Brief green checkmark badge fades out |
227	
228	---
229	
230	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
231	
232	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
233	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
234	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
235	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
236	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view
237	
238	---
239	
240	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents
241	
242	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it should be editable in-place:
243	
244	| Document | Editable fields |
245	|----------|----------------|
246	| **CV** | All bullet text, summary, tagline, section headings (where user-defined), skills list items |
247	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off |
248	| **Screening** | Response text for each question |
249	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) |
250	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only; extracted data is read-only |
251	
252	Changes to the CV, Cover Letter, and Screening documents update session state immediately. Changes to Master CV require an explicit **Save** confirmation (to avoid accidental writes to the shared master record).
253	
254	---
255	
256	## 13. Spell Check Integration
257	
258	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab:
259	
260	- Flagged text is underlined (red for spelling, blue for grammar/style)
261	- Hovering shows a tooltip with the suggestion(s)
262	- Clicking the underline shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
263	- Accepting a correction updates the element text in-place
264	- A spell-check summary badge in the settings bar shows "N issues remaining"
265	
266	---
267	
268	## 14. Current Design vs. Proposed Design — Comparison
269	
270	| Aspect | Current Design | Proposed Design |
271	|--------|---------------|-----------------|
272	| Right pane | 26 tabs, one section per tab | Document viewer with 7 document tabs |
273	| Resume visibility | Only visible in Layout Review tab | Visible throughout CV phase |
274	| Element editing | DataTable per section tab | Hover toolbar + expand panel, in-place |
275	| Suggestion workflow | Rewrite Review tab (before/after cards) | Inline per-element with pending-highlight |
276	| Excluded items | Not visible in review tables | Ghost items revealed on demand within section |
277	| Workflow context | Step pills in header bar | Auto-tab-switching + section blue-highlight |
278	| Spell check | Separate Spell Check tab | Inline underline + hover correction |
279	| Master CV access | Locked to finalise stage (GAP-41) | Always-available tab |
280	| Clarification questions | Chat only | Embedded in Analysis view |
281	| Section overview | No summary; must expand tab | Collapsed summary badge per section |
282	| Element detail | No original/proposed comparison | Expanded element panel with 5 data rows |
283	| Settings | Scattered (model selector, settings modal) | Sticky settings bar above CV |
284	
285	---
286	
287	## 15. Open Design Questions
288	
289	1. **Tab bar overflow** — with 7+ document tabs, how should the tab bar handle narrow viewports? (scroll? overflow menu? auto-hide tabs not yet available?)
290	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — should the user be able to see the job description and CV side-by-side (e.g., a sub-split within the right pane)?
291	3. **Element expand persistence** — should expanded element panels persist across tab switches, or always collapse on leaving the CV tab?
292	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — how does the split pane degrade on small screens? (stacked? drawer?)
293	5. **Undo** — inline edits need a clear undo path; does Ctrl+Z on a contenteditable element behave predictably enough, or do we need a custom undo stack?
294	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — keyboard reorder (↑↓ buttons) must remain a full alternative to drag.
295
```
</details></tool-use>

482	## 17. Undo & Edit History (Theme 4)
483	
484	### App-level undo stack
485	
486	A **per-session undo stack** is maintained in the frontend, independent of browser history. It is separate from and does not interact with browser `Ctrl+Z` on `<textarea>` fields (which only reverts within the currently open field before Save).
487	
488	| Operation | What is pushed to the undo stack |
489	|-----------|----------------------------------|
490	| Save on a Current text field | Previous text of that field |
491	| Accept suggestion | Previous Current text + removal of Proposed text |
492	| Decline suggestion | Restoration of Proposed text |
493	| Include / exclude toggle | Previous include/exclude state |
494	| Move up / down | Previous position of the element |
495	| Accept all (section) | Snapshot of all element states in that section |
496	
497	### Undo / Redo controls
498	
499	- **Ctrl+Z** — undo the most recent stack entry; announce via live region: *"Undone: edit to Bullet 3."*
500	- **Ctrl+Y** — redo the most recently undone entry
501	- **Undo / Redo buttons** in the settings bar (Section 5) show the count of available steps: "↩ Undo (3)" / "↪ Redo (1)"
502	
503	### Stack boundaries
504	
505	- The undo stack is per-session and not persisted to disk — closing the browser tab clears it
506	- Master CV saves are **not** on the in-memory undo stack; they are reverted via the timestamped file backup (a separate restore path)
507	- The stack holds a maximum of 50 entries; older entries are dropped
508	- After a session is archived / finalised, the undo stack is cleared
509	
510	### Revert to session start
511	
512	A **"Revert CV to session start"** button is available in a "Danger zone" section of the Settings modal. It restores the CV to the state it was in when the user entered the Customisation phase. This is a non-undoable destructive action and requires explicit confirmation ("Revert all CV changes? This cannot be undone.").

gh issue create --repo Warnes-Innovations/cv-builder --title "feat: Position target style presets (academic/research vs. industry)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Add a **position target style** concept that captures the fundamental differences between position types and drives defaults throughout the app — page length targets, content depth, formatting style, and emphasis.

## Motivation

The current design uses fixed page-count thresholds (≤2 pages = green, etc.) and a single set of content-selection heuristics regardless of the kind of position being applied for. In practice, these differ significantly:

| Dimension | Academic / Research / Medical | Industry / Corporate |
|-----------|------------------------------|----------------------|
| Ideal CV length | 3–10+ pages (comprehensive) | 1–2 pages (concise) |
| Publications | Required, comprehensive | Omit or 2–3 highlights max |
| Teaching / service | Include | Omit |
| Bullet style | Full sentences, methodology detail | Impact-first, metric-driven |
| Summary | Research statement | 3-line career summary |
| ATS emphasis | Journal names, grant agencies, methods | Keywords, tools, outcomes |

Without a position type concept, the app either uses wrong defaults or forces the user to manually override many settings for every session.

## Proposed approach

Define a **position target style** as a named preset (stored in `config.yaml` and overridable per-session) with the following fields:

\```yaml
position_styles:
  industry:
    label: "Industry / Corporate"
    page_target: 2          # pages; used for badge thresholds in settings bar
    page_warn_pct: 10       # amber when >10% over target
    page_error_pct: 25      # red when >25% over target
    include_publications: false
    include_teaching: false
    bullet_style: "impact"  # impact-first, metric-driven
    summary_style: "career" # 3-line career summary
    ats_mode: "keywords"

  academic:
    label: "Academic / Research"
    page_target: null       # no upper limit; no colour warning
    page_warn_pct: null
    page_error_pct: null
    include_publications: true
    include_teaching: true
    bullet_style: "detail"  # full methodology
    summary_style: "statement" # research/teaching statement
    ats_mode: "methods"

  medical_clinical:
    label: "Medical / Clinical"
    page_target: null
    include_publications: true
    include_teaching: true
    bullet_style: "clinical"
    summary_style: "statement"
    ats_mode: "clinical"

  government:
    label: "Government / Federal"
    page_target: null       # federal resumes often 4–6 pages
    bullet_style: "detail"
    summary_style: "career"
    ats_mode: "keywords"
\```

The active position style would be:
1. Set during job intake (user selects or the LLM infers from the job description)
2. Overridable per-session in the settings bar
3. Used to set defaults for page-count badge thresholds, include/exclude suggestions, bullet rewrite tone, and summary style

## UI integration points

- **Job intake:** Add "Position type" selector (dropdown or LLM-inferred with confirmation)
- **Settings bar (§5 of redesign):** Show active style: "Style: Industry ▾" with override dropdown
- **Page count badge:** Use `page_target` from the active style for threshold colours instead of fixed values
- **LLM prompts:** Pass position style as context to customisation and rewrite prompts
- **Master CV tab:** Allow per-section "include by default for [style]" flags

## Out of scope for this issue

- Custom user-defined styles (future)
- Per-section style overrides (future)
- Style inference from job description (can be a separate issue)

## Related

- `tasks/ui-redesign-proposal.md` §5 (page count badge now references this issue)
- `config.yaml` — where presets would be stored
- `scripts/utils/cv_orchestrator.py` — where include/exclude and rewrite logic lives
EOF
)"

Based on my review of both documents, here is the complete updated **Applicant** section for `/Users/warnes/src/cv-builder/tasks/persona-redesign-review.md`:

---

## Applicant

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live context preservation** — Seeing the CV rendered throughout the workflow (not just at Layout Review) closes the gap between editing suggestions in isolation and understanding their impact on the actual document.
- **Inline decision-making** — Element hover toolbars with accept/reject/edit buttons eliminate the mental context-switching burden of jumping between a Rewrite Review tab and the final output. Focus-triggered controls (Theme 1) make these accessible to keyboard users and discoverable for all users.
- **Ghost elements and inclusion visibility** — Excluded items shown inline with strikethrough and reduced opacity make it clear what's *not* going into the CV during customisation.
- **Embedded clarification questions** — Questions paired with the analysis data they relate to, rather than buried in conversation history, is a major usability win.
- **Always-available Master CV tab** — Updating baseline data at any moment rather than being forced to wait until the end of a session removes a significant workflow friction.
- **Consistent section/element expansion model** — The two-state collapse/expand pattern is predictable and reduces overwhelm when facing 20+ experience bullets or 30+ skills.
- **Persistent undo across browser sessions (Change A)** — The undo stack now survives browser closes/reopens by storing to the session JSON file, eliminating the frustration of losing edit history when switching workstations.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Performance and interactivity risk** — Real-time rendering of the full CV with inline hover toolbars, contenteditable fields, and inline spell-check underlines may lag as the CV grows. No performance baseline is proposed. (Mitigated by Theme 4 replacement of contenteditable with native `<textarea>` elements, but full-document rendering stress-test still needed.)
- **Conflation of editing surfaces** — Master CV (requires explicit Save) vs. CV session (immediate) have different interaction models living in the same right pane. The current separation, while fragmented, makes these boundaries explicit.
- **Loss of word-level diff context** — The current before/after card UI with LCS word-level diff highlighting has been restored (Theme 3): the Proposed row now shows removed text in red strikethrough and added text in green underline, preserving the visual diff that helps judge rewrite magnitude at a glance.
- **Lack of workflow progression feedback** — The proposal now pins workflow step pills to a sticky header with full phase names (not abbreviated), ensuring returning users see their position at a glance.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Page count badge target awareness (Change B)** — The green/amber/red thresholds on the page count badge now reflect the user's position-style target (e.g. 2 pages for industry). Tooltip shows: "~2.1 pages · Target: 2 pages · 5% over target." Suggest adding a "targets per style" help tooltip explaining how industry/academic/medical/government defaults differ.
- **Position-style preset extensibility for publications (Change C)** — The forthcoming preset system (industry, academic, medical_clinical, government) includes publication handling. An `industry_research` sub-preset allows up to 3 most-relevant publications. Suggest: clarify in UI whether users can customize these presets after selection, or if presets are read-only defaults.
- **Validate undo stack serialization overhead** — With the undo stack now persisting to the session JSON file, confirm that 2 MB cap and FIFO eviction at 100% does not create a "lost work" scenario where old edits are silently discarded. Consider a "Undo history about to be trimmed" modal instead of one-time toast.
- **Test page-count badge across multiple position-type workflows** — Ensure the dynamic target thresholds (Industry vs. Academic vs. Medical) update correctly when the user switches position types mid-session or revisits a prior job with a different target.
- **Clarify publication citation style per preset** — Change C specifies citation style (APA/Vancouver/etc.) per publication preset, but does not clarify whether users see the active citation style in the settings bar or only in the expanded publication element.

---

31	- **Performance and interactivity risk** — Real-time rendering of the full CV with inline hover toolbars, contenteditable fields, and inline spell-check underlines may lag as the CV grows. No performance baseline is proposed.
32	- **Conflation of editing surfaces** — Master CV (requires explicit Save) vs. CV session (immediate) have different interaction models living in the same right pane. The current separation, while fragmented, makes these boundaries explicit.
33	- **Loss of comparison workflow in Rewrite Review** — The current before/after card UI with word-level diff highlighting is absent from the proposal. The new inline "Proposed" text field loses the visual diff that helps judge rewrite magnitude.
34	- **Lack of workflow progression feedback** — The proposal mentions moving step pills to a "compact top bar" or "sidebar strip" but provides no concrete UX for progress visibility.
35	
36	### Suggested enhancements
37	
38	- **Prototype and performance-test the inline edit model** — Before committing to contenteditable, validate that the browser's DOM rendering can keep up with a 500+ bullet CV. Offer a fallback "modal edit" mode for expensive elements.
39	- **Preserve word-level diff for rewrites** — When an element has a "Proposed" rewrite, show before/after with LCS word-diff highlighting (removed text in red, added text in green) alongside the inline textarea.
40	- **Add explicit "Master CV Save" confirmation modal** — Make it visually distinct from CV session changes: a modal diff preview before write.
41	- **Define workflow phase indicators** — Propose a sticky breadcrumb in the left-pane chat header or a subtle badge on the primary section being worked on.
42	- **Specify keyboard navigation for section/element expand** — Define consistent bindings: `Ctrl+Space` to expand/collapse focused element, `Tab` to move between elements, `Ctrl+Enter` to save inline edits.
43	- **Add a "changes since last re-run" persistent badge** — After a re-run, changed/new elements should have a lasting orange "new" badge (not just a transient flash) so users can quickly scan which items were affected.
44	
45	---
46	
47	## First-Time User
48	
49	### What the proposed design gets right
50	
51	- **Live document context during editing** — Users will finally see how their edits appear in the actual CV rather than working blind in isolated tabs.
52	- **Inline suggestion acceptance** — Instead of toggling between "Rewrites" and "Generated CV" tabs, users see pending suggestions (amber border) in-place and can accept/decline/regenerate without leaving context.
53	- **Master CV always accessible** — Removing the finalise-stage lock lets users update master data at any time.
54	- **Collapsible expand/collapse model** — The two-state pattern is consistent across sections and elements; users learn it once and apply it everywhere.
55	- **Ghost items clarify inclusion decisions** — Showing strikethrough/muted excluded items within the section makes include/exclude visible in context.
56	- **Embedded clarification questions** — Moving questions from chat-only to adjacent-to-data solves the "buried in chat" problem.
57	
58	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
59	
60	- **Toolbar proliferation risks cognitive overwhelm** — The element hover toolbar has 9+ buttons. A first-time user encountering this on their first bullet point may freeze. Secondary/context-dependent buttons must be hidden or deprioritized.
61	- **No persistent help entry point** — The proposal does not mention onboarding or persistent "?" access after the welcome modal is dismissed.
62	- **Settings bar competes for cognitive real estate** — The sticky settings bar occupies valuable vertical space. Testing at 1366×768 (laptop) is required.
63	- **Expand/collapse state persistence is underspecified** — If a user expands several bullets, switches to Screening, then returns, will all their expansions have collapsed?
64	- **Preview vs. Final output distinction is not addressed** — The proposal never states "this is a preview until you confirm layout" or equivalent, risking repetition of the same old failure mode.
65	
66	### Suggested enhancements
67	
68	- **Add a "Preview/Final" label in the CV View settings bar** — A badge: "🔄 Preview mode — confirm layout to finalize" / "✅ Layout confirmed — ready to download."
69	- **Create a three-tier help system** — (1) Inline tooltips on controls. (2) Persistent Help toggle (?) in the corner. (3) "Tips" badge on first-encounter controls.
70	- **Implement button visibility tiers in the element toolbar** — Show only essential buttons by default (expand, include/exclude, edit). Secondary buttons (suggest, retry) appear only in the expanded panel.
71	- **Add confirmation feedback for in-place Master CV edits** — Green checkmark, toast message, or persistent "Save" button state after saving.
72	- **Include "You've completed X. Next up: Y" stage-transition messages** — Bridge the gap where no message guides the next step after phase transitions.
73	- **Explicitly surface ATS score context** — Add context to the badge: "ATS Score: 87% (based on current CV)" and "Click to see which keywords are matched/missing."
74

77	## UX Expert
78	
79	### What the proposed design gets right
80	
81	- **Document-centric paradigm** — Shifting from 26 scattered tabs to "document is the UI" directly addresses the context-switching pain point and "no sense of the whole."
82	- **In-place element editing and control discovery** — The dual expand/collapse model (section-level summary badges + element-level hover toolbars) is elegant and fixes the current DataTable fragmentation.
83	- **Ghost items for inclusion decisions** — Rendering excluded elements inline with muted/strikethrough provides context the current tables lack.
84	- **Inline spell check** — Moving spell-check corrections from a separate tab into inline underlines with popover corrections is a significant workflow improvement.
85	- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Placing questions adjacent to the requirements they relate to eliminates the chat-only burial problem.
86	- **Always-available Master CV tab** — Lifting the finalise-stage gate respects user autonomy.
87	
88	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
89	
90	- **Auto-switching document tabs risks loss of user control** — If a user is editing the Master CV and the workflow auto-advances, does the view snap away? The hybrid model (auto-switch + user override) needs a "pin this tab" control or explicit "recommended view" indicator.
91	- **Hover-state discoverability remains fragile** — Toolbar appearing only "on hover" hides critical actions from keyboard-only and low-vision users. Section 9 must specify how toolbars become keyboard-accessible.
92	- **Element expand persistence unclear** — Section 15 leaves this as an open question, but it directly impacts cognitive load. Proposal: collapse on tab-away with an optional "remember expanded state" toggle.
93	- **Spell-check integration timing ambiguous** — Does inline spell check replace the dedicated phase entirely, or supplement it? This must be clarified.
94	- **Section and element state explosion** — 8+ visual states, each relying heavily on colour. Must include non-colour indicators (e.g., "⊙ Pending suggestion" label, icon prefix) for accessibility.
95	
96	### Suggested enhancements
97	
98	- **Formalize auto-tab-switching with a "View Mode" setting** — *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, show a breadcrumb before switching so it isn't invisible.
99	- **Make hover toolbars keyboard-reachable immediately** — Each element container receives `tabindex="0"`; on focus, toolbar buttons remain visible. Consider a "Show All Controls" view toggle.
100	- **Add element-state badges to replace colour-only signaling** — Badges adjacent to element text: "⊙ Pending suggestion", "✓ Accepted", "✗ Declined". Ensures colour-blind users understand state.
101	- **Clarify spell-check phase integration** — State explicitly: "The Spell Check step displays the CV view with inline underlines. Users correct, then proceed to Layout Review."
102	- **Provide "collapse all / expand all" at section and document levels** — Add buttons: "[Collapse all elements]" / "[Expand all elements]" in the sticky settings bar.
103	- **Define the undo stack boundary for inline edits** — Inline edits add to a per-session undo stack; Ctrl+Z reverts the last edit within the active element. Never committed to Master CV until explicit save.
104

106	
107	## Accessibility Specialist
108	
109	### What the proposed design gets right
110	
111	- **Document-centric layout reduces tab-switching cognitive load** — Fewer navigation context switches benefit users with cognitive or motor disabilities.
112	- **Inline editing preserves focus locality** — Keeps edits in-place, reducing the burden on users with short-term memory challenges.
113	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — Eliminates the need to context-switch between chat and structured data for screen reader users.
114	- **Explicit keyboard alternative for drag-to-reorder** — ↑↓ buttons directly address GAP-120 and GAP-72.
115	- **Consistent expand/collapse model** — A single ▶/▼ toggle pattern makes expand/collapse semantics predictable for screen readers.
116	- **Master CV always accessible** — Removes the barrier preventing keyboard users from reaching critical data-entry in earlier phases.
117	
118	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
119	
120	- **Hover-only controls remain critical accessibility red flags** — Sections 8 and 9 describe toolbars that appear "on hover." This **replicates and amplifies the current hover-control gap** and fails WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.13 (content on hover or focus). No alternative activation method is documented.
121	- **Contenteditable accessibility unspecified** — No guidance on screen-reader announcements for edit-mode entry/exit, cursor positioning, or undo availability.
122	- **No announcement strategy for accept/decline actions** — Screen reader users will not be notified that actions succeeded without `aria-live` support.
123	- **Auto-scroll and flash-highlight animations conflict with prefers-reduced-motion** — Section 7's flash animation violates WCAG 2.1 SC 2.3.3; no alternative provided.
124	- **Tab bar overflow behavior unresolved** — Section 15 defers this; all overflow patterns require keyboard-operable alternatives.
125	
126	### Suggested enhancements
127	
128	- **Replace hover-only controls with focus-triggered disclosure** — Toolbar is a `role="toolbar"` container; appears on keyboard focus and hover. Standard keyboard navigation: Tab to move between buttons, Enter/Space to activate.
129	- **Document contenteditable accessibility requirements** — Each editable field carries `aria-label`, `aria-describedby`, and an `aria-live="polite"` announce region. Screen readers informed when edit mode begins/ends.
130	- **Add live-region announcements for suggestion actions** — On ✅/❌ activate: `aria-live="assertive"` region announces "Suggestion accepted. Bullet 3 updated. Press ↑ to move, Ctrl+Z to undo."
131	- **Implement prefers-reduced-motion wrapper** — Flash/pulse animations replaced with static 2-second color hold under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
132	- **Define keyboard alternatives for tab-bar overflow** — "More documents" button with `aria-label`; dropdown with arrow-key navigation, Enter to select.
133	- **Specify reorder confirmation via live region** — "Moved up. Item 2 of 5." announced immediately after ↑/↓ activation; element receives focus after move.
134

136	
137	## Graphical Designer
138	
139	### What the proposed design gets right
140	
141	- **"The document is the UI" thesis** — Editing in-place within the live preview eliminates context-switching and preserves the WYSIWYG promise throughout customisation.
142	- **Inline controls over separate tabs** — Hover toolbars and inline element-expand replace fragmented tab-per-section navigation, concentrating all actions near the elements they affect.
143	- **Ghost-item visibility pattern** — Strikethrough/50% opacity/dashed border excluded items create coherent inline visual contrast.
144	- **Collapsible sections with summary badges** — Creates scannability for dense documents without expanding everything on first load.
145	- **Sticky settings bar** — Consolidating Length, Style, ATS Score, and Regenerate eliminates hunting for controls across modals.
146	- **Analysis clarification questions embedded inline** — Creates stronger context and avoids the chat/viewer toggle.
147	
148	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
149	
150	- **Inline hover toolbars risk visual clutter and accidental activation** — 10+ buttons on every hover over 30+ bullets creates cognitive overload and UI flicker. Reducing to 3–4 core visible actions with a "more" menu is needed.
151	- **Pending-suggestion amber boxes may conflict with CV's visual hierarchy** — Amber borders on a professional resume appear as editorial artifacts rather than integrated guidance. A softer background tint would be less disruptive.
152	- **In-place contenteditable may not preserve final PDF fidelity** — Formatting state (bold, italic, list nesting) can be accidentally introduced; the current DataTable enforces plaintext. Strict input validation needed.
153	- **Expanded element panel typography may not scale** — On a typical laptop (1366px), the multi-row expanded panel grows very tall. Consider max-height with overflow scroll or a drawer alternative.
154	- **No guidance on undo integration with inline editing** — Contenteditable undo is browser-dependent and fragile; the proposal needs a concrete undo strategy.
155	
156	### Suggested enhancements
157	
158	- **Reduce the default element hover toolbar to 3 core buttons** — Keep ▼ (expand), ✗ (exclude), ↑↓ (reorder) always visible; tuck ✓, ✏️, ✨, ✅, ❌, 🔄 into a three-dot menu.
159	- **Apply a subtle background tint instead of amber border** — 10–15% amber background fill behind pending elements + a small 6px amber dot to the left. Less graphic competition with CV typography.
160	- **Require explicit Save for contenteditable fields, with a diff preview** — Side-by-side diff (original vs. edited) with "Save" and "Cancel" before persisting.
161	- **Constrain expanded panel height** — `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` on the element card; scrollable with visible scrollbar indicator.
162	- **Add font family and colour theme controls to the settings bar** — Font family (Inter/Garamond/Calibri) and theme (Professional Blue / Warm Neutral / Bold Contrast) dropdown; addresses existing gap US-G3.
163	- **Display a live page-break preview** — Mini page-stack icon with colour-coded warning (green ≤2 pages, amber 2–2.5, red >2.5) in the sticky settings bar. "View page breaks" toggle highlights break points in the rendered CV.
164

167	## Resume Expert
168	
169	### What the proposed design gets right
170	
171	- **Eliminates context-switching penalty** — Editing bullets while seeing live output directly addresses the fundamental pain point.
172	- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Reduces friction of bouncing between chat and analysis data.
173	- **Expanded element panel with original/current/proposed comparison** — All three versions of content in one place is critical for resume strategy decisions.
174	- **Ghost item reveal pattern** — Prevents the dangerous situation where a user forgets they excluded a strong bullet.
175	- **Section-level bulk actions with explicit accept/decline** — Makes it possible to act on suggestions quickly.
176	- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Allows users to correct source data mid-session.
177	
178	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
179	
180	- **Bulk-accept safety risk** — "Accept all" in Experience or Skills with one click is dangerous; LLM batch suggestions may contain subtle errors requiring per-item review. The current Rewrite Review tab forces explicit per-item decisions.
181	- **Formatting preservation during in-place editing unclear** — If a user deletes a line break or removes parenthetical context, will formatting break? Current implementation enforces constraints via review UI, not in-place editing.
182	- **Missing severity sort in spell-check integration** — Spell issues shown in order-received may cause a user to address comma placement while missing a name typo.
183	- **ATS comments row lacks synonym grouping context** — The current review flags that synonyms (ML / Machine Learning) are not grouped; the proposal does not clarify whether they will be.
184	- **CV style switcher clarity ambiguous** — "Plain/ATS" in the dropdown is unclear about what it produces vs. "Sidebar."
185	
186	### Suggested enhancements
187	
188	- **Add a confirmation modal for "Accept all" actions** — "Accept all N suggestions in [Section]?" with options to "Review each", "Accept all", or "Cancel."
189	- **Validate in-place edits against resume conventions** — Real-time or on-blur: line-length warning (70–85 chars ideal), fragment check, keyword consistency check; non-blocking warnings only.
190	- **Sort spell-check issues by severity** — Priority 1: spelling errors (names, companies). Priority 2: grammar/fragment. Priority 3: stylistic suggestions.
191	- **Add a "Grouped Keywords" view to ATS comments** — Group keyword matches by canonical term: **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]. Closes the existing synonym gap.
192	- **Clarify CV style switcher with previews** — Include "Compare styles" that renders the current section in both Sidebar and Plain/ATS side-by-side in a collapsible preview pane.
193	- **Preserve section-expand state across tab switches** — Store state in sessionStorage keyed on section name; prevents re-expanding a section you were working on.

197	## Hiring Manager
198	
199	### What the proposed design gets right
200	
201	- **Live preview throughout customisation** — Users see immediately when a rewritten bullet becomes too long, when a skill disrupts visual balance, or when section headings are malformed.
202	- **In-place inline editing preserves document integrity** — Users can evaluate edits against the rendered resume context in real-time.
203	- **Ghost-style hidden elements solve a credibility risk** — Catches the silent failure of submitting incomplete job entries with only 1 accepted bullet.
204	- **Sticky settings bar for output control** — Length/Style/ATS/Pages controls always accessible without tab-switching.
205	- **Embedded clarification questions** — Reduces ambiguity and keeps analysis rationale transparent.
206	- **Element expansion panels provide rich decision context** — Original, Current, Proposed, Model recommendation, ATS comments, and Persuasion comments in one view.
207	
208	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
209	
210	- **Inline editing risks accidental quality degradation** — All CV content editable in-place can introduce formatting errors (stray newlines, copy-paste artifacts) that are not visible until Download. Strong autosave + undo and a "Preview as PDF" step are critical.
211	- **No mention of final validation gates before export** — The current design fires validation warnings at the Download tab. The proposal does not specify whether these gates remain or move elsewhere.
212	- **Master CV always-present may create version-control confusion** — If Master CV edits are not reversible, accidental writes could damage the shared source-of-truth with no recovery path.
213	- **No specification for style-switcher state persistence** — If the user selects "ATS Plain" and then downloads twice, is there a risk of version mismatch?
214	
215	### Suggested enhancements
216	
217	- **Add a pre-Download validation checklist modal** — Before Download: confirm page count, persuasion warnings acknowledged, no pending inline saves, spell-check resolved.
218	- **Implement a "Preview as PDF" button in the settings bar** — Opens a real PDF preview in a modal before Download; catches formatting errors that HTML rendering misses.
219	- **Mark Master CV edits with a "dirty" indicator and require explicit confirmation** — Red dot on tab, "Unsaved changes" warning, timestamp-logged saves.
220	- **Add a "Revert to Session Start" option for CV edits** — Restore CV to the state at the start of Customisation. Safety valve if inline edits cascade incorrectly.
221	- **Specify style-switcher behavior with a visual badge** — Active style prominently displayed; Download filenames include the style (`resume_ATS.pdf` vs. `resume_Sidebar.pdf`).
222	- **Integrate page-count warnings into the settings bar directly** — Live color badge (green ≤2, amber 2–2.5, red >2.5) with tooltip explaining the threshold.

226	## HR / ATS Specialist
227	
228	### What the proposed design gets right
229	
230	- **ATS Score badge and drill-down in settings bar** — Constant compliance visibility eliminates the current "Compute ATS Score" empty-state button users overlook.
231	- **Keyword highlighting in Job view** — Amber highlighting for matched terms and red for missing required keywords teaches users what gaps remain before customisation begins.
232	- **ATS comments in expanded element panel** — Users making editorial decisions see ATS impact alongside persuasion and model recommendation in one place.
233	- **Plain/ATS style option in settings bar** — Toggle between human-readable (Sidebar) and ATS-safe layout; makes the tradeoff visible.
234	- **Hard-requirement keyword coverage now visible inline** — Summary badges ("3 of 7 bullets included") let users scan inclusion rate per section.
235	- **Master CV always accessible** — Enables mid-session skill updates and consistent skill classification.
236	
237	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
238	
239	- **Inline editing risks ATS-safe formatting** — If ATS DOCX generation doesn't re-normalize edited text (stripping bold/italic, standardizing line breaks), inline edits could corrupt ATS parsing.
240	- **ATS validation gate missing in proposed workflow** — The current File Review tab enforces a 17-check validation report. The proposal does not detail how the validation report integrates or gates downloads.
241	- **Spell-check underline could interfere with ATS scoring** — If underline metadata leaks into the DOCX export, it could corrupt text extraction or keyword matching.
242	
243	### Suggested enhancements
244	
245	- **Add an "ATS Safe Editing" toggle in the settings bar** — When enabled, contenteditable fields strip formatting on blur and the settings bar shows: "Inline edits will be normalized for ATS compliance."
246	- **Embed ATS validation status in the settings bar** — A "Validation Status" badge (green ✓ / amber ⚠ / red ✗) that updates live; displays count of failing checks. Clicking opens the full 17-check report.
247	- **Add a "Hard Requirements Coverage" widget to the Analysis view** — After embedded clarification questions: **Hard Required Keywords: N / M**, with red warning if < 100%. Each unmatched keyword links to the relevant section.
248	- **Clarify the ATS DOCX export path from inline edits** — Document a clear rule: all text re-normalized (formatting stripped, line breaks standardized) before export; validation check compares ATS DOCX text to session state.
249	- **Define synonym / variant handling in ATS comments** — Note when a keyword is matched via synonym (e.g., "Matched as: 'ML' variant of 'Machine Learning'"); validation gate should apply the same synonym rules.
250	- **Add a "Missing Keywords" insertion suggestion in element expand** — When ATS comments note a missing hard-requirement keyword, auto-suggest an insertion point: "This bullet mentions DevOps but not Terraform. Consider appending: '… using Terraform.'"

254	## Master CV Curator
255	
256	### What the proposed design gets right
257	
258	- **Always-accessible Master CV tab** — Directly addresses GAP-41. No longer locked to `finalise` stage; the first document tab and available at any time.
259	- **Unified in-place editing with explicit Master CV save gates** — Session documents update immediately; Master CV changes require explicit "Save" confirmation. Prevents accidental writes to the permanent record.
260	- **Expanded element panel with "Original" row** — Shows Original (read-only, from Master CV), Current (session), and Proposed (LLM) with data lineage crystal clear in a single visual context.
261	- **Ghost-style excluded items inline** — Preserves the "document-is-the-UI" principle while maintaining the visual boundary between included and excluded content.
262	- **Contextual highlighting** — Blue left-border accent on the active section, paired with chat breadcrumb, reinforces which part is under focus and where master data ends.
263	- **Inline spell check** — Keeps the "document is the UI" philosophy intact and eliminates tab-switching for closely related editing.
264	
265	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
266	
267	- **Master CV state boundaries harder to enforce in always-on model** — The current design makes mid-workflow Master CV writes structurally impossible. The proposal relies entirely on backend phase gating being infallible; UI/UX burden shifts to the backend entirely.
268	- **Proposed → Current → Session state coupling unclear** — When a user expands an element and accepts a suggestion, does this promote to Current immediately, or only after a Save? The proposal doesn't clarify when Proposed suggestions are formally captured.
269	- **Loss of explicit harvest/archive boundary** — The proposal does not clarify whether the two-phase harvest workflow (1. Finalise & Archive, 2. Optional: Update Master CV) is preserved or merged into the unified document viewer.
270	- **Inline analysis answers may fragment the chat narrative** — Embedding answerable questions in Analysis view creates two parallel input streams (left-pane chat and right-pane inline). This could confuse the agent's reasoning trail.
271	
272	### Suggested enhancements
273	
274	- **Formalize Master CV write-confirmation with phase context** — If session is not in `init` or `refinement`, show: "Cannot edit master data while a job customisation is active. Archive the job first, then return here."
275	- **Clarify the Proposed → Current pipeline** — Accepting a suggestion moves Proposed to Current in-place but does not write to master data. Changes are held in session state and written to master only via explicit harvest post-finalisation. Add a "Session" badge on the Current field.
276	- **Preserve explicit harvest/archive boundaries** — After the archive step, show a distinct second card titled "Step 2: Review & Apply Master CV Updates (Optional)" to keep the two-phase lifecycle visible.
277	- **Inline Analysis answers should post to left-pane chat** — When a user answers inline, the answer posts to chat as a user message and is processed by the agent. Visual affordance (arrow icon, "Post to chat" button) makes this flow obvious.
278	- **Define Master CV element save trigger explicitly** — Before closing an expanded element or navigating away, show a "Save" button with unsaved indicator. Clicking Save runs `_require_master_data_write_phase` and writes with a timestamped backup.
279	- **Add a mini-legend for Original/Current/Proposed rows** — "?" icon with tooltip: "**Original:** from your Master CV (read-only). **Current:** your session edits. **Proposed:** AI suggestion."

283	## Persuasion Expert
284	
285	### What the proposed design gets right
286	
287	- **Live document context during editing** — Users see immediate impact of framing decisions on the rendered resume, directly supporting persuasive-intent evaluation.
288	- **Inline "Persuasion comments" row in expanded element panels** — Currently surfaced only in the separate Rewrite Review tab; inline placement is a major discoverability upgrade.
289	- **Model recommendation badges integrated into element expansion** — Consolidates Emphasize/Include/De-emphasize/Exclude signals adjacent to persuasion and ATS feedback.
290	- **Iterative in-place editing** — The expanded panel's "✏️ Accept with inline editing" lowers friction to iterate on rewrite suggestions.
291	- **Contextual highlighting of the active workflow section** — Keeps persuasive framing decisions anchored to intent.
292	- **Master CV always accessible** — Allows strong framing decisions to flow back to the master record rather than being one-off session edits.

294	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
295	
296	- **Persuasion comments row is present but not specified** — The proposal lists "Persuasion comments" as a data row but does not specify: what checks it contains, who generates it, or how it differs from the current collapsible warning panel.
297	- **No explicit gating of submission on persuasion acknowledgement** — Current design gates "Submit All Decisions" on `persuasionWarningsAcknowledged`. The proposed design's Section 9 does not specify whether a form-level gate remains.
298	- **Ghost-style excluded elements may undermine persuasion coherence** — A user might include a mediocre bullet without checking persuasion comments. Proposal does not specify whether ghost elements trigger warnings.
299	- **Persuasion comments only visible on expand** — A high-priority persuasion flag (e.g., passive voice) does not bubble to the collapsed view unless specified, so most users will never see it.
