372	
373	## Returning User
374	
375	### What the proposed design gets right
376	
377	- **Persistent session context via auto-tab-switching** — Auto-switching to the relevant document tab naturally restores the working session without requiring manual navigation.
378	- **Master CV always accessible** — Returning users can verify and update foundational data at any point; removes the anxiety of discovering errors too late.
379	- **Prior decisions visible in-place via ghost items** — The **(+N hidden)** badge provides a quick visual summary of exclusions without hunting through tabs.
380	- **Inline suggestion workflow reduces tab-switching fatigue** — Pending suggestions appear with amber borders directly on elements; no detour to the Rewrite Review tab.
381	- **Clarification questions embedded in Analysis view** — Returning users resuming job analysis immediately see what needs clarification without scrolling chat history.
382	- **Live document-as-UI eliminates the "resume only at layout stage" problem** — Users immediately see the cumulative effect of prior decisions.
383	
384	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
385	
386	- **No explicit restored-decisions summary on initial re-entry** — No "welcome back" panel showing session state ("4 experiences selected, 12 skills, 7 approved rewrites"). The current "✅ Session restored: {positionName} ({phase})" confirmation should have an equivalent.
387	- **Workflow step pills location unclear** — Moving step pills to a compact top bar or collapsible sidebar risks burying session progress. A returning user should see their workflow position at a glance without hovering.
388	- **Expanded elements may not persist across tab switches** — Section 15 leaves this unresolved. A returning user mid-edit of an experience bullet switching tabs and back may find all expansions collapsed.
389	- **No explicit mention of scroll position restoration** — Should the CV view scroll back to the last-edited section, or reset to the top?
390	- **Inline editing increases state-save complexity** — The proposal doesn't specify debounce timing, conflict handling for concurrent tab edits, or rollback on validation failure.
391	
392	### Suggested enhancements
393	
394	- **Add a restored-decisions summary banner on session re-entry** — Collapsible banner showing: "Session restored: 4 of 7 experiences selected • 12 skills • 3 pending rewrites • 2 clarification questions open." Auto-hide after 10 seconds.
395	- **Pin the workflow step pills to a sticky header with visible labels** — Full phase names (not abbreviated). Persistent left-panel strip or compact sticky top bar. A returning user should know their position without hover.
396	- **Define and document element expand-state persistence** — Specify that expanded panels persist across tab switches (stored in session state). Visual indicator (dot on section badge) showing "N elements expanded."
397	- **Implement scroll position restoration on session reload** — Scroll CV view to the section that was last active in the prior session (stored in `status.last_active_section`); smooth scroll behavior.
398	- **Specify contenteditable debounce and conflict handling** — CV edits debounce with 2-second delay before API save; concurrent-tab conflicts show "conflict detected—reload?" modal; failed saves rollback to last-known state.
399	- **Extend the Analysis view to show clarification answer history** — A collapsible "Answered" section with prior responses. Include "Clear and re-answer" option for revision.
400	
401	---
402	
403	## Trust & Compliance
404	
405	### What the proposed design gets right
406	
407	- **Expanded element panel retains original/current/proposed three-row audit trail** — All three versions surfaced side-by-side during inline editing; provenance of every edit is visible at the moment of decision.
408	- **Inline suggestion acceptance with mandatory decision visibility** — Amber border boxes on each element force users to encounter suggestions in context, reducing the risk of accidental bulk acceptance.
409	- **Ghost item reveal pattern provides explicit inclusion/exclusion audit** — Strikethrough/50% opacity excluded items with traceability are a substantial improvement over exclusion decisions made in separate tabs.
410	- **Master CV always-accessible tab** — Permanent access to the authoritative source improves trust.
411	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — Users cannot accidentally ignore AI-derived questions before generating rewrites.
412	- **Contextual section highlighting** — Grounds users in which section is being customised, reducing the risk of blind bulk-accept operations on the wrong section.
413	
414	### Concerns or regressions vs current design
415	
416	- **Section-level bulk "Accept all" introduces compliance risk** — One click accepts all LLM-proposed rewrites in a section without requiring the user to expand and review any of them. The current rewrite-review tab enforces explicit per-item review.
417	- **In-place contenteditable editing without explicit save-on-change confirmation** — The implicit-persist model (blur or explicit save) is weaker than the current explicit Master CV "Save" confirmation. Users may inadvertently edit and lose focus, triggering an invisible state update.
418	- **Element-expand persistence left open** — If panels collapse on tab-switch, users lose context of which elements were being evaluated; reintroduces the context-loss problem the redesign aims to solve.
419	- **Undo/rollback mechanism not defined** — Users who misclick or accidentally overwrite content have no documented recovery path.
420	
421	### Suggested enhancements
422	
423	- **Gate "Accept all" behind element-expansion checkpoint** — Require that at least one pending element has been expanded and explicitly acted upon before "Accept all" becomes enabled for that section.
424	- **Explicit "Session checkpoint" before finalisation** — A read-only summary of all pending suggestions per section before proceeding: "Experience: 3 pending · Skills: 1 pending · Summary: 0 pending."
425	- **Add a persistent "Draft" badge and audit breadcrumb to inline edits** — A brief "(edited by user on 2026-06-13)" footer in the expanded element panel distinguishes LLM-proposed rewrites from manual edits.
426	- **Clarify Master CV save workflow with explicit lock/unlock pattern** — "Unlock & Save" confirmation with backup-before-write and schema-validation-on-write documentation.
427	- **Replace implicit blur-save with explicit Save button** — Show an inline "Save" button after the user types. Only on Save does session state update. Aligns CV editing model with the Master CV model.
428	- **Embed "⚠ AI-generated" label on Proposed row** — Ensures users apply appropriate scrutiny to LLM-generated rewrites, particularly for skill additions and summary variants.
429	
430	---
431	
432	## Synthesis
433	
434	### Cross-Persona Themes
435	
436	Five issues were raised independently by multiple personas, indicating systemic design concerns that must be resolved before implementation:
437	
438	#### Theme 1: Hover-Only Controls Are Inaccessible and Undiscoverable
439	**Raised by:** Accessibility Specialist, Power User, First-Time User, UX Expert, Graphical Designer (5 of 14 personas)
440	
441	The biggest cross-cutting concern. All five personas flagged that hover-only toolbars exclude keyboard users, are fragile on touch devices, and are not discoverable without prior training. The current design already has critical gaps GAP-120 (viewer tab `<div>` elements have no `tabindex`) and GAP-72 (workflow step pills have no `tabindex`); the proposed design amplifies rather than fixes these.
442	
443	**Why hover-only fails across user groups:**
444	
445	| User group | How hover-only breaks down |
446	|------------|---------------------------|
447	| Keyboard-only users | No hover event is ever fired; toolbars never appear; controls are completely unreachable |
448	| Touch / tablet users | Hover events are unreliable or absent on touch screens; a tap typically fires click, not hover |
449	| Low-vision / screen magnification | At 4× zoom, only a small viewport region is visible; hover over an element outside that region is impractical |
450	| Screen reader users | Toolbars invisible to the accessibility tree unless focus enters them; `aria-haspopup` never signalled |
451	| First-time users (mouse) | Controls are invisible until the user happens to hover over the right element; there is no affordance indicating that hovering is meaningful |
452	| Power users (keyboard-driven) | Accept/decline/move shortcuts require mouse movement interrupting a keyboard flow |
453	
454	**WCAG criteria that hover-only violates:**
455	
456	- **SC 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (AA):** Content triggered by hover must be dismissable, hoverable, and persistent — but SC 1.4.13 does *not* require that the same content also be keyboard-triggerable. A stricter reading of SC 2.1.1 (Keyboard, A) applies: any functionality available via pointer must also be available via keyboard without specific timings. If the only way to reach the Accept button is to hover over the element, that is a keyboard-accessibility failure at Level A.
457	- **SC 2.1.1 Keyboard (A):** All functionality must be operable through a keyboard interface. A hover-only toolbar that exposes Include/Exclude/Edit/Accept/Decline fails this criterion outright.
458	- **SC 2.4.3 Focus Order (A):** Focus must move through interactive elements in an order that preserves meaning and operability. Hidden toolbars that do not enter the focus order violate this.
459	- **SC 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value (A):** Each UI component must expose its name, role, and state programmatically. A toolbar that only exists in the DOM on hover and is not exposed to the accessibility tree fails this.
460	
461	**The three-tier control visibility model (recommended design pattern):**
462	
463	Rather than a binary visible/hidden hover model, use three tiers:
464	
465	```
466	Tier 1 — Always visible (section level):
467	  ▶/▼ expand toggle  |  (+N hidden) badge  |  N pending badge
468	  These are permanent; no hover required.
469	
470	Tier 2 — Visible on hover OR keyboard focus (element level):
471	  [✗ Exclude] [↑] [↓] [▶ Expand]
472	  Low-opacity (30%) at rest; full opacity on :hover or :focus-within.
473	  Keyboard: Tab into element container → toolbar revealed.
474	
475	Tier 3 — Visible only in expanded element panel:
476	  [✨ Suggest] [✅ Accept] [✏️ Edit] [❌ Decline] [🔄 Retry]
477	  Only rendered when the element detail panel is open.
478	  No hover required — the panel is persistent until collapsed.
479	```
480	
481	This model ensures that keyboard-only users can reach all controls via Tab navigation (Tier 2 is revealed on `:focus-within`), touch users can tap to expand (Tier 3), and mouse users get the full hover experience. Advanced actions (suggest, retry, accept-with-edit) are never hover-gated because they live in the always-visible expanded panel.
482	
483	**Keyboard interaction specification:**
484	
485	```
486	Tab              Move focus to next element container
487	Shift+Tab        Move focus to previous element container
488	Enter / Space    Expand/collapse the focused element detail panel
489	Alt+X            Exclude focused element (toggle include/exclude)
490	Alt+↑            Move focused element up within section
491	Alt+↓            Move focused element down within section
492	Alt+A            Accept pending suggestion on focused element
493	Alt+D            Decline pending suggestion on focused element
494	Alt+E            Open inline edit mode on focused element Current field
495	Escape           Close expanded panel / exit inline edit without saving
496	Ctrl+Enter       Save inline edit and close edit mode
497	Ctrl+Z           Undo last edit (app-level undo stack, not browser)
498	?                Open keyboard shortcut help overlay
499	```
500	
501	Keyboard shortcuts are scoped to the element that currently holds focus, so Alt+A does not fire globally — only on the focused element. This prevents accidental bulk actions.
502	
503	**ARIA markup requirements:**
504	
505	```html
506	<!-- Element container -->
507	<div
508	  class="cv-element"
509	  tabindex="0"
510	  role="article"
511	  aria-label="Bullet: Led migration of data pipeline to AWS. Pending suggestion."
512	  aria-expanded="false"
513	>
514	  <!-- Tier 2 toolbar (revealed on :focus-within or :hover) -->
515	  <div role="toolbar" aria-label="Element controls">
516	    <button aria-label="Exclude this bullet">✗</button>
517	    <button aria-label="Move up">↑</button>
518	    <button aria-label="Move down">↓</button>
519	    <button aria-label="Expand element details">▶</button>
520	  </div>
521	
522	  <!-- Tier 3 panel (rendered when aria-expanded="true") -->
523	  <div role="region" aria-label="Element details">
524	    ...
525	  </div>
526	</div>
527	
528	<!-- Live region for action confirmations -->
529	<div aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true" class="sr-only" id="cv-action-announce"></div>
530	```
531	
532	When an action completes, inject a brief message into `#cv-action-announce`:
533	- Accept: *"Accepted. Bullet 3 of 7 updated."*
534	- Decline: *"Declined. Suggestion removed from bullet 3."*
535	- Move up: *"Moved up. Now item 2 of 7."*
536	- Exclude: *"Excluded. Bullet 3 hidden. +1 hidden shown in section badge."*
537	
538	**Consensus recommendation:** Adopt the three-tier control visibility model above. Replace all hover-only toolbars in Sections 8 and 9 of the design proposal. Resolve GAP-120 and GAP-72 at the design level by specifying that all element containers carry `tabindex="0"` and Tier 2 toolbars are revealed on `:focus-within` in addition to `:hover`.
539	
540	#### Theme 2: Bulk "Accept All" Is a Compliance and Quality Risk
541	**Raised by:** Trust & Compliance, Resume Expert, Power User, Persuasion Expert (4 of 14 personas)
542	
543	Section-level bulk accept is convenient but bypasses the per-item review that the current Rewrite Review tab enforces. One click can accept a dozen LLM rewrites across an Experience section without the user reading any of them.
544	
545	**Consensus recommendation:** Require at least one explicit per-element decision in a section before enabling "Accept all" for that section. Add a count: "Accept all 7 remaining suggestions in Experience?"
546	
547	#### Theme 3: Word-Level Diff View Is Missing from Element Expand Panel
548	**Raised by:** Applicant, Resume Expert (2 of 14 personas)
549	
550	The current Rewrite Review tab shows word-level LCS diff (deleted text in red, added text in green). The new "Proposed" text field is a plain text box with no visual diff, making it harder to judge the magnitude of an AI rewrite at a glance.
551	
552	**Consensus recommendation:** Render the Proposed row with LCS word-diff highlighting (removed in red strikethrough, added in green underline) alongside the editable textarea.
553	
554	#### Theme 4: Undo Model Is Undefined and Contenteditable Is Fragile
555	**Raised by:** UX Expert, Power User, Graphical Designer, Trust & Compliance, Returning User (5 of 14 personas)
556	
557	Browser contenteditable undo is unreliable across browsers and formatting contexts. Multiple personas independently raised this as a high-risk open question. The proposal acknowledges it in Section 15 but defers it.
558	
559	**Consensus recommendation:** Use native `<textarea>` instead of contenteditable wherever possible. Maintain an app-level per-session undo stack. Replace blur-save with explicit "Save" buttons that appear on typing.
560	
561	#### Theme 5: Auto-Tab-Switching Needs User Control
562	**Raised by:** UX Expert, Power User, Recruiter-Ops, Returning User (4 of 14 personas)
563	
564	Automatic context switching is helpful for new users but disruptive for experienced users who are doing side-by-side comparison (Job vs. CV), keyboard-driven workflows, or multi-application throughput reviews. Auto-switch that fires while the user is mid-edit can break focus and lose work.
565	
566	**Consensus recommendation:** Add a "View Mode" toggle: *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, show a breadcrumb notification before switching; suppress auto-switch if the user has unsaved changes.
567	
568	---
569	
570	### Top 5 Recommended Enhancements
571	
572	These five enhancements address the highest-impact, cross-persona concerns and should be incorporated into the design before implementation begins.
573	
574	**1. Keyboard-Accessible Focus-Triggered Controls (resolves Theme 1)**
575	Replace all hover-only toolbars (Sections 8, 9) with focus-triggered disclosure: element containers have `tabindex="0"`, toolbars appear on Tab focus and hover, all buttons are keyboard-operable with Alt+key shortcuts. Add `role="toolbar"` with standard Tab/Enter/Space navigation. Resolve GAP-120 and GAP-72 at the design level rather than deferring to implementation.
576	
577	**2. Word-Level Diff in the Proposed Row (resolves Theme 3)**
578	Add LCS-based word-level diff rendering to the Proposed row in every expanded element panel. Removed text shown in red strikethrough; added text in green underline. This preserves the core value of the current Rewrite Review tab without requiring a separate tab.
579	
580	**3. Gate "Accept All" Behind at Least One Element Review (resolves Theme 2)**
581	The section-level "Accept all" button (Section 8) is disabled until at least one element in the section has been expanded and explicitly acted upon (accepted, edited, or declined). Show a count badge: "Accept all 5 remaining suggestions." This preserves the current rewrite-review's protection against blind bulk acceptance while keeping bulk operations available.
582	
583	**4. Explicit Save Button with App-Level Undo Stack (resolves Theme 4)**
584	Replace blur-save on contenteditable/textarea fields with an explicit inline "Save" button that appears after the user types (similar to GitHub inline comment editing). Use native `<textarea>` elements. Maintain a per-session undo stack (not relying on browser undo) so Ctrl+Z reverts the last element edit reliably.
585	
586	**5. "View Mode" Toggle: Smart vs. Manual Auto-Tab-Switching (resolves Theme 5)**
587	Add a Settings option: *Smart (auto-switch, user can override)* vs. *Manual (user controls tab)*. In Smart mode, display a 1-second notification before switching: "Switching to CV view for Customisation phase ✕ Stay here." Suppress auto-switch entirely if the user has unsaved edits or if "Manual" is active. Default to Smart for new users, Manual for returning users who have set a preference.
588	
589	---

9	# CV Builder UI Redesign Proposal
10	
11	**Status:** Revised Draft — post persona review
12	**Date:** 2026-06-15
13	**Author:** Greg Warnes / Claude Code
14	**Related:** [tasks/gaps.md](gaps.md), [tasks/ui-review.md](ui-review.md), [tasks/persona-redesign-review.md](persona-redesign-review.md)
15	
16	> **Revision notes (2026-06-15):** Incorporates the five cross-persona themes from the persona review synthesis:
17	> Theme 1 — hover-only → focus-triggered controls (Sections 8, 9, 16);
18	> Theme 2 — "Accept all" gating (Section 8);
19	> Theme 3 — word-level diff in Proposed row (Section 6);
20	> Theme 4 — explicit Save + app-level undo (Sections 12, 17);
21	> Theme 5 — Smart/Manual auto-tab-switch (Section 2).
22	> Additional changes: settings bar validation badge + preview/final label (Section 5),
23	> non-colour state indicators (Section 10), prefers-reduced-motion spec (Section 7),
24	> session-restore banner (Section 2), spell-check severity ordering (Section 13),
25	> resolved open design questions (Section 15).
26	
27	---
28	
29	## 1. Overview & Design Goals
30	
31	### Problem with the Current Design
32	
33	The current UI uses a **tab-per-section model**: the right panel exposes 26 viewer tabs (Job, Analysis, Experience, Bullets, Skills, Achievements, Tagline, Summary, Publications, ATS Score, Rewrites, Spell Check, Layout Review, Generated Files, Master CV, Cover Letter, Screening, Interview Prep, etc.). Users must navigate between tabs to review and edit each section, with no persistent view of the final output.
34	
35	Key pain points:
36	
37	- **Context switching** — editing bullets in the Bullets tab gives no sense of how they appear in the actual document
38	- **No sense of the whole** — the resume only becomes visible at the Layout Review stage
39	- **Fragmented workflow** — suggestions (rewrites), spell corrections, inclusion decisions, and ordering are handled in separate tabs with separate UIs
40	- **Master CV gate** — the Master CV tab is only accessible in the `finalise` stage (GAP-41), even though users may need to update it at any time
41	- **Clarification questions buried** — questions surface in chat only, not adjacent to the analysis data they relate to
42	
43	### Design Thesis
44	
45	> **The document is the UI.**
46	
47	All editing, review, suggestion-acceptance, and ordering happens *in place* within a live view of the document being worked on. The left pane handles conversation and command input; the right pane is a context-aware document viewer that automatically shows the most relevant document and always permits direct editing.
48	
49	### Primary Goals
50	
51	| Goal | Current | Proposed |
52	|------|---------|----------|
53	| See final output while editing | ❌ Only at layout stage | ✅ CV always visible |
54	| Edit elements in-place | ❌ DataTable per tab | ✅ Inline on the rendered document |
55	| Understand include/exclude decisions in context | ❌ Checkbox in table, separate from output | ✅ Ghost items inline within section |
56	| Act on AI suggestions without tab-switching | ❌ Rewrite Review tab, separate from output | ✅ Inline accept/decline on each element |
57	| Access Master CV at any time | ❌ Locked to finalise stage | ✅ Always-present tab |
58	| Clarify analysis questions near the relevant data | ❌ Chat only | ✅ Embedded inline in Analysis view |
59	
60	---
61	
62	## 2. Layout Architecture
63	
64	```
65	┌────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────┐
66	│  LEFT PANE (~35%)      │  RIGHT PANE: Document Viewer (~65%)        │
67	│  Agent Chat & Input    │                                            │
68	│                        │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐  │
69	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  │ [Master CV][Job][Analysis][CV]       │  │
70	│  │ Conversation     │  │  │ [Cover Letter][Screening][Prep] ...  │  │
71	│  │ history          │  │  │  ← document tabs (auto-switch)       │  │
72	│  │                  │  │  ├──────────────────────────────────────┤  │
73	│  │  Agent messages  │  │  │                                      │  │
74	│  │  and responses   │  │  │  Active document rendered here       │  │
75	│  │  scroll here     │  │  │  controls on hover or focus          │  │
76	│  │                  │  │  │  (for editable documents)            │  │
77	│  └──────────────────┘  │  │                                      │  │
78	│  ┌──────────────────┐  │  └──────────────────────────────────────┘  │
79	│  │ Input field      │  │                                            │
80	│  │ + action buttons │  │                                            │
81	│  └──────────────────┘  │                                            │
82	└────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────┘
83	```
84	
85	**Core design principle:** The left pane is for interaction (chat, commands, agent responses, action buttons). The right pane is a document viewer — it renders whichever document is most relevant to the current workflow phase and permits direct editing within that document.
86	
87	### Document Tabs
88	
89	| Tab | Content | When auto-shown |
90	|-----|---------|-----------------|
91	| **Master CV** | Master CV data editor (structured, always editable) | Before job intake; any time |
92	| **Job** | Raw job description with keyword highlighting | Job intake phase |
93	| **Analysis** | Job analysis with embedded clarification questions | Job analysis phase |
94	| **CV** | Live HTML-rendered resume with inline controls | Customisation, rewrite, spell check, layout |
95	| **Cover Letter** | Generated cover letter (editable in-place) | Cover letter phase |
96	| **Screening** | Screening question responses (editable) | Screening phase |
97	| **Interview Prep** | Interview prep materials | Interview prep phase |
98	| **Thank You** | Thank-you letter draft | Thank-you phase |
99	
100	**Auto-switching — Smart / Manual mode (Theme 5):**
101	
102	The viewer supports two modes, selectable in Settings:
103	
104	| Mode | Behaviour |
105	|------|-----------|
106	| **Smart** (default for new users) | Switches to the most relevant tab as the workflow advances. Before switching, a 1-second notification appears: *"Switching to CV view for Customisation phase ✕ Stay here."* Auto-switch is suppressed if the user has unsaved edits in the current tab. |
107	| **Manual** (default for returning users who have set a preference) | No automatic switching. The breadcrumb in the left-pane chat header always shows the recommended tab: *"Suggested: CV ▶"* — but the pane does not switch without explicit user action. |
108	
109	The active tab is always remembered and restored on session reload. When a session is restored, a collapsible **session-restore banner** appears briefly at the top of the right pane:
110	
111	> *"Session restored: 4 of 7 experiences selected · 12 skills · 3 pending rewrites · 2 clarification questions open."*
112	
113	The banner auto-hides after 10 seconds or on dismiss.
114	
115	### Workflow Step Pills
116	
117	Move from the current horizontal step header to a **compact sticky top bar** with full phase names (not abbreviated) — never collapsed by default. A returning user must be able to see their workflow position at a glance without hovering or toggling. Example:
118	
119	```
120	[Job Input] → [Analysis] → [Customise ●] → [Rewrites] → [Spell] → [Layout] → [Download]
121	```
122	
123	The active step is visually distinguished (filled circle, bold label). Completed steps show a checkmark. The bar is always visible; it does not collapse.
124	
125	---
126	
127	## 3. Job Description View
128	
129	- Job description text rendered with **keyword highlighting** — terms matching the CV's skills and extracted requirements are highlighted in amber; missing required terms highlighted in red
130	- Sticky mini-header shows: job title, company, ATS match score badge
131	- Scrollable; no truncation
132	
133	---
134	
135	## 4. Analysis View
136	
137	- Displays structured job analysis: extracted requirements (must-have vs. nice-to-have), keyword map, ATS score breakdown, identified gaps
138	- **Clarification questions embedded inline** — each open question appears adjacent to the analysis section it relates to, not only in the chat:
139	  - Example: a question about "years of ML experience" appears within the Requirements section, next to the "Machine Learning" requirement row
140	  - Answering a question inline posts the answer to the left-pane chat and immediately updates the analysis state
141	- Analysis sections are collapsible (see Section 6 for the universal expand/collapse model)
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
146	
147	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
148	
149	```
150	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
151	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
152	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
153	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
154	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
155	```
156	
157	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
158	|---------|---------------------|
159	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
160	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. Active style is always shown in the label (e.g. "Style: ATS Plain ▾"). Download filenames include the style (`resume_ATS.pdf`, `resume_Sidebar.pdf`). |
161	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Label: "ATS: 87% (current CV)". Click opens ATS detail overlay showing matched/missing keywords. |
162	| **Pages** | Estimated page count with mini page-stack icon. Colour is based on the user's **target page length** (configured per-session or globally in settings): green when within target, amber when 10–25% over target, red when > 25% over target. Target defaults are position-type-aware when a position type is set (see [#126](https://github.com/Warnes-Innovations/cv-builder/issues/126)). Tooltip shows: "~2.1 pages · Target: 2 pages · 5% over target." |
163	| **Layout status** | Badge: "🔄 Preview — confirm to finalise" when layout is unconfirmed; "✅ Layout confirmed — ready to download" when confirmed. Clicking "🔄" opens the layout confirmation flow. |
164	| **Validation** | Badge: "✓ Valid" / "⚠ 3 issues" / "✗ 1 error". Updates live as the user edits. Click opens the full 17-check ATS validation report. |
165	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
166	| **Undo / Redo** | Undo (Ctrl+Z) / Redo (Ctrl+Y) buttons for session-scoped edits. Shows count of undo steps available. See Section 17. |
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
171	
172	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
173	
174	### Section States
175	
176	| State | What is shown |
177	|-------|--------------|
178	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
179	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
180	
181	### Element States
182	
183	| State | What is shown |
184	|-------|--------------|
185	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Tier-2 toolbar visible on hover or keyboard focus (see Section 9). High-severity flags (passive voice, missing result clause) show a small ⚠ badge inline with the text so they are visible without expanding. |
186	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
187	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only. Labelled "(from Master CV — read only)". |
188	| | **Current** — the version active in this session. Editable via explicit ✏️ Edit button (see Section 12). |
189	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated). Displayed with **word-level diff** (Theme 3): removed words in red strikethrough, added words in green underline, against the Current text. Editable before accepting. |
190	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude`, with one-sentence rationale. |
191	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues. Keywords grouped by canonical term (e.g. **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]). Missing hard-requirement terms shown with a suggested insertion point. |
192	| | **Persuasion comments** — the eight persuasion checks rendered as prose: "Strong verb ✓ · Passive voice ⚠ · Result clause ✓ · Word count ✓". Issues weighted by persuasive impact (passive voice and missing result clause first). |
193	
194	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. The panel is `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` so it does not push the rest of the resume off-screen on small viewports. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
195	
196	Expanded element panel state **persists across document tab switches** within the same session (stored in session state). A dot indicator on the section summary badge shows "N elements expanded" so users can see at a glance that panels are open.
197	
198	All text fields in the expanded element panel are edited via explicit **Save / Cancel** buttons (see Section 12 and Section 17 — not blur-save).

202	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
203	
204	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
205	
206	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
207	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
208	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
209	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **scrolls** to that element and highlights it
210	
211	**Motion sensitivity (prefers-reduced-motion):** All animations (flash highlights, scroll animations, border transitions) must respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Under reduced motion: scroll is instant (no smooth scroll), highlights are a static 2-second coloured background (no pulse or flash), and border transitions are instant. CSS:
212	
213	```css
214	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
215	  .cv-element-highlight { animation: none; background-color: #fffacd; }
216	  html { scroll-behavior: auto; }
217	}
218	```

222	## 8. Section-Level Controls — Three-Tier Model (Theme 1)
223	
224	Controls use a **three-tier visibility model** so all actions are reachable by mouse, keyboard, and touch without relying solely on hover.
225	
226	### Tier 1 — Always visible (no hover required)
227	
228	These appear permanently in the section header:
229	
230	| Control | Action |
231	|---------|--------|
232	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section (keyboard: Enter or Space when header is focused) |
233	| **(+N hidden)** badge | Count of excluded elements; click to reveal ghost items inline |
234	| **N pending** badge | Count of elements with unresolved suggestions; click to jump to first pending element |
235	
236	### Tier 2 — Visible on hover OR keyboard focus (`:hover`, `:focus-within`)
237	
238	These appear when the mouse enters the section header or it receives keyboard focus:
239	
240	| Control | Action |
241	|---------|--------|
242	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
243	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode (keyboard: use ↑↓ per-element buttons in Tier 2 below) |
244	
245	### Section-level "Accept all" — gated (Theme 2)
246	
247	The **Accept all** and **Decline all** buttons appear in the section header but are **disabled** (greyed out with tooltip "Review at least one suggestion first") until the user has explicitly expanded and acted on at least one pending element in the section. Once the gate is cleared, the buttons become active and show a count:
248	
249	> "✅ Accept all 5 remaining · ❌ Decline all 5 remaining"
250	
251	This preserves the protection against blind bulk-acceptance while keeping the batch workflow available.

255	## 9. Element-Level Controls — Three-Tier Model (Theme 1)
256	
257	Each element container has `tabindex="0"` and `role="article"`, making it keyboard-focusable. Controls are split across three tiers:
258	
259	### Tier 1 — Always visible
260	
261	These appear permanently in the collapsed element view, requiring no hover:
262	
263	| Control | Condition | Action |
264	|---------|-----------|--------|
265	| **⚠ badge** | High-severity persuasion flag (passive voice, missing result clause) | Visible in collapsed view; click to expand element and see full persuasion comments |
266	| **⊙ Pending** badge | Element has unresolved suggestion | Visible in collapsed view; amber colour + text label (not colour-only) |
267	
268	### Tier 2 — Visible on hover OR keyboard focus
269	
270	Rendered at 30% opacity at rest; full opacity on `:hover` or `:focus-within` on the element container. Keyboard users reach these by tabbing to the element, then tabbing through the toolbar buttons.
271	
272	| Button | Keyboard shortcut | Action |
273	|--------|------------------|--------|
274	| **▶/▼** | Enter / Space | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
275	| **✗ / ✓** | Alt+X | Exclude (if included) or Include (if excluded) |
276	| **↑** | Alt+↑ | Move element up within section |
277	| **↓** | Alt+↓ | Move element down within section |
278	
279	After ↑ or ↓, an `aria-live="assertive"` region announces: *"Moved up. Item 2 of 7."*
280	
281	### Tier 3 — Visible only in expanded element panel
282	
283	These appear inside the expanded detail panel, which is always persistent (never hover-gated):
284	
285	| Button | Keyboard shortcut | Action |
286	|--------|------------------|--------|
287	| **✏️ Edit** | Alt+E | Open edit mode on Current text field |
288	| **✨ Suggest** | — | Generate LLM suggestion for this element |
289	| **✅ Accept** | Alt+A | Accept pending suggestion |
290	| **✏️ Accept & Edit** | — | Accept suggestion, then open it in edit mode before saving |
291	| **❌ Decline** | Alt+D | Decline pending suggestion |
292	| **🔄 Retry** | — | Retry suggestion generation |
293	
294	Keyboard shortcuts are scoped to the element that currently has focus — Alt+A does not fire globally.
295	
296	A **keyboard shortcut help overlay** is available at any time via the **?** key (or the ⌨ icon in the settings bar). See Section 16 for the full shortcut table.

300	## 10. Visual States for Elements
301	
302	Every state uses **both colour and a non-colour indicator** (icon, label, or border pattern) so colour-blind users and screen reader users can distinguish states without relying on colour alone.
303	
304	| State | Colour | Non-colour indicator | Screen reader announcement |
305	|-------|--------|---------------------|---------------------------|
306	| **Active / Included** | Normal | No badge | — |
307	| **Excluded / Hidden** | Muted gray, 50% opacity | Strikethrough text + dashed left border + "excluded" label | "Excluded" in `aria-label` |
308	| **Has pending suggestion** | Amber left border + amber background tint | "⊙ Pending suggestion" text badge (Tier 1, always visible) | `aria-label` includes "Pending suggestion" |
309	| **Suggestion accepted** | 500ms green border flash | "✓ Accepted" badge fades out over 1s | Live region: "Accepted. Bullet N updated." |
310	| **Suggestion declined** | 300ms red border flash | "✗ Declined" badge fades out over 1s | Live region: "Declined. Suggestion removed." |
311	| **Workflow focus** | Blue left-border accent + blue background tint | Section badge labelled "Current focus" | — |
312	| **Just moved / reordered** | 300ms yellow fade | "↕ Moved" badge fades out | Live region: "Moved up. Item N of M." |
313	| **In edit mode** | Visible input border | Textarea cursor + "Editing" label above field | Focus moves to textarea; `aria-label="Editing: [field name]"` |
314	| **Saved / confirmed** | Green checkmark fades | "✓ Saved" text fades out | Live region: "Saved." |
315	| **High-severity flag** | — | ⚠ badge inline in collapsed text (always visible, no hover) | `aria-label` includes "Warning: [flag name]" |
316	
317	All flash/fade animations respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (see Section 7).

321	## 11. Hidden Element Reveal Pattern
322	
323	- Each section header shows a **(+N hidden)** badge when excluded elements exist
324	- Clicking the badge — or activating "Show hidden" from the section hover toolbar — reveals ghost-style excluded items **inline** within the section, in their last-known position
325	- Ghost elements show all element toolbar buttons, but the ✓/✗ button shows **"Include"** rather than "Exclude"
326	- Ghost elements cannot be reordered until included
327	- Clicking "Show hidden" again collapses them back out of view

331	## 12. In-Place Editing Across All Documents (Theme 4)
332	
333	Wherever content appears in the right pane, it is editable in-place. All editable fields use native `<textarea>` elements (not `contenteditable`) for predictable keyboard behaviour, reliable Ctrl+Z within the field, and clean plaintext output to the session state.
334	
335	| Document | Editable fields | Save model |
336	|----------|----------------|------------|
337	| **CV** | Bullet text, summary, tagline, user-defined section headings, skills list items | Explicit Save (see below) |
338	| **Cover Letter** | All paragraph text, salutation, sign-off | Explicit Save |
339	| **Screening** | Response text for each question | Explicit Save |
340	| **Master CV** | All fields (name, contact, experience entries, skills, achievements, publications, summary variants) | Explicit Save + phase check + timestamped backup |
341	| **Analysis** | Clarification question answer fields only | Posts to chat immediately on submit; no separate save step |
342	
343	### Explicit Save model (replaces blur-save)
344	
345	When the user clicks ✏️ Edit on an element (Tier 3 control, Section 9):
346	
347	1. The Current text field opens as a `<textarea>` with the cursor at end of text
348	2. An **"Editing" label** appears above the field (`aria-label="Editing: [field name]"`)
349	3. Two buttons appear below: **Save** (Ctrl+Enter) and **Cancel** (Escape)
350	4. Typing does **not** update session state — state is only written on explicit **Save**
351	5. On Save: the new text is pushed to the app-level undo stack, session state is updated, the textarea collapses back to rendered text, and a "✓ Saved" badge fades out
352	6. On Cancel: textarea collapses with no state change; undo stack is not modified
353	
354	For **Master CV fields**, Save additionally:
355	- Runs `_require_master_data_write_phase` (blocks write if a job customisation is active, showing: *"Cannot edit master data while a job customisation is active. Archive the job first."*)
356	- Creates a timestamped backup of `Master_CV_Data.json` before writing
357	- Runs schema validation before write
358	- Shows a dirty indicator (red dot on the Master CV tab) until saved; "Unsaved changes" tooltip on the tab
359	
360	A **"Review-only mode"** toggle is available in the settings bar. When enabled, all ✏️ Edit buttons are hidden and `<textarea>` fields are non-interactive, so users can scan without accidentally triggering edits.
361

364	## 13. Spell Check Integration
365	
366	Spell and grammar issues are surfaced **inline** on the CV view rather than in a separate tab. The dedicated Spell Check workflow step now routes to the CV view with issues highlighted, rather than a separate tab.
367	
368	- Flagged text is underlined — red for spelling errors, blue dashes for grammar/style
369	- Clicking the underline (or pressing Enter when the underlined text is focused) shows an inline popover: correction options + "Ignore" + "Ignore all"
370	- Accepting a correction pushes the change to the app-level undo stack and updates the element text in-place
371	- The settings bar shows a **"Spell: N issues"** badge (red if any spelling errors, amber if grammar-only). The badge counts down as issues are resolved.
372	
373	**Severity ordering:** Issues are surfaced in this priority order, not document order:
374	
375	1. Spelling errors in proper nouns (company names, degree names, technology names)
376	2. All other spelling errors
377	3. Grammar / sentence structure issues in bullet text
378	4. Style suggestions (comma placement, word choice)
379	
380	This ensures a missed name typo is never buried below a comma suggestion.
381	
382	**ATS safety:** Spell-check underlines and popover HTML are never included in DOCX or PDF export. All markup is stripped at generation time.

411	## 15. Resolved Design Questions
412	
413	Previously open; resolved by persona review recommendations.
414	
415	1. **Tab bar overflow** — Overflow tabs appear behind a "More ▾" button with `aria-label="Show more documents"`. Clicking opens a keyboard-navigable dropdown (arrow keys, Enter to select). The active tab is always in the visible bar, never in the overflow.
416	
417	2. **Simultaneous CV + Job view** — Not implemented in the initial redesign. The Analysis view already embeds inline context from the job. A future enhancement could offer a sub-split, but the tab model is sufficient for v1.
418	
419	3. **Element expand persistence** — Expanded element panels **persist across document tab switches** within the same session (stored in session state). Panels do not collapse on tab-away. A dot indicator on section summary badges shows how many elements are currently expanded. See Section 6.
420	
421	4. **Mobile / narrow window** — Below 900px viewport width, the split pane stacks vertically: left pane (chat) above, right pane (document viewer) below. A toggle button switches between panes to recover vertical space. Not a priority for v1 (local desktop app), but the CSS grid must not break at narrow widths.
422	
423	5. **Undo** — Resolved via app-level undo stack (Section 17). Native `<textarea>` elements replace `contenteditable`. Ctrl+Z within an open textarea reverts within the field (browser-native, reliable for `<textarea>`); Ctrl+Z after Save reverts the last committed edit via the app undo stack.
424	
425	6. **Drag-to-reorder accessibility** — Keyboard reorder via ↑/↓ Tier 2 buttons (Section 9) is the **primary** reorder interface. Drag-to-reorder is an enhancement for mouse users. After each ↑/↓ key press, `aria-live="assertive"` announces the new position. Drag-and-drop is never the only path to any action.

429	## 16. Keyboard Navigation & Accessibility Specification
430	
431	### Focus order
432	
433	```
434	[Workflow step bar pills] → [Left pane: chat messages] → [Left pane: input field]
435	→ [Right pane: document tabs] → [Right pane: section headers (Tier 1 controls)]
436	→ [Right pane: elements within section] → [Right pane: element Tier 2 toolbar]
437	→ [Right pane: expanded panel Tier 3 controls]
438	```

440	Tab order follows visual left-to-right, top-to-bottom reading order. The workflow step bar, document tabs, section headers, and element containers all carry `tabindex="0"`. No `tabindex` values > 0 are used.
441	
442	### Keyboard shortcuts (global scope)
443	
444	| Key | Action |
445	|-----|--------|
446	| **?** | Open keyboard shortcut help overlay |
447	| **Ctrl+Z** | Undo last committed edit (app undo stack) |
448	| **Ctrl+Y** | Redo |
449	| **Ctrl+/** | Toggle Review-only mode (lock/unlock all editing) |

452	
453	| Key | Action |

455	| **Enter / Space** | Expand / collapse element detail panel |
456	| **Alt+X** | Toggle include / exclude |
457	| **Alt+↑** | Move element up within section |
458	| **Alt+↓** | Move element down within section |
459	| **Alt+E** | Open edit mode on Current text field (opens Tier 3 panel if not already open) |

462	| **Ctrl+Enter** | Save edit (when in edit mode) |

465	### ARIA requirements
466	
467	- Each element container: `role="article"`, `tabindex="0"`, `aria-label="[element type]: [text]. [state flags]"` (e.g. `"Bullet: Led migration of pipeline to AWS. Pending suggestion."`)
468	- Each section header: `role="heading"` at appropriate level, `aria-expanded`, `tabindex="0"`
469	- Section Tier 2 toolbar: `role="toolbar"`, `aria-label="[Section name] controls"`
470	- Element Tier 2 toolbar: `role="toolbar"`, `aria-label="Element controls"`
471	- Document tabs: `role="tablist"` / `role="tab"` / `aria-selected` / `tabindex` (ARIA tabs pattern)
472	- Live region for action feedback: `<div role="status" aria-live="assertive" aria-atomic="true" class="sr-only">` — updated after every user action that changes element state
473	- Expanded element panel: `role="region"`, `aria-label="[element text] — details"`
474	
475	### Resolves
476	
477	- GAP-120 (Tab `<div>` elements keyboard-inaccessible) — all interactive containers carry `tabindex="0"` and keyboard event handlers
478	- GAP-72 (Workflow step pills have no `tabindex`) — step pills carry `tabindex="0"` and Enter/Space activation

480	---
481	
482	## 17. Undo & Edit History (Theme 4)
483	
484	### App-level undo stack
485	
486	An **undo stack is stored in the session JSON file** for each job, persisting across browser sessions. Closing and reopening the browser (or switching to a different computer using the same session directory) fully restores the undo/redo stack. The stack is separate from and does not interact with browser `Ctrl+Z` on `<textarea>` fields (which only reverts within the currently open field before Save).
487	
488	| Operation | What is pushed to the undo stack |
489	|-----------|----------------------------------|
490	| Save on a Current text field | Previous text of that field + field path |
491	| Accept suggestion | Previous Current text + Proposed text (so decline is also reversible) |
492	| Decline suggestion | Proposed text (restores it to Proposed on undo) |
493	| Include / exclude toggle | Previous include/exclude state of the element |
494	| Move up / down | Previous position index of the element |
495	| Accept all (section) | Full snapshot of all element states in that section |
496	
497	Each stack entry is a small JSON object: `{ "op": "edit", "path": "experience[2].bullets[0].current", "prev": "...", "ts": 1749945600 }`. The stack is stored in the session file under `undo_stack` and `redo_stack` keys.
498	
499	### Undo / Redo controls
500	
501	- **Ctrl+Z** — undo the most recent stack entry; announce via live region: *"Undone: edit to Bullet 3."*
502	- **Ctrl+Y** — redo the most recently undone entry
503	- **Undo / Redo buttons** in the settings bar (Section 5) show the count of available steps: "↩ Undo (3)" / "↪ Redo (1)"
504	
505	### Stack size limit and user warning
506	
507	The combined serialized size of `undo_stack` + `redo_stack` in the session file is capped at **2 MB**. This is large enough for hundreds of typical edits (each entry is ~200–500 bytes) but prevents unbounded growth on long-running sessions.
508	
509	When the stack approaches the limit:
510	
511	| Threshold | Behaviour |
512	|-----------|-----------|
513	| 80% of 2 MB used | Amber warning badge appears on the Undo button in the settings bar: "↩ Undo (147) ⚠". Tooltip: "Undo history is 80% full. Oldest entries will be discarded when the limit is reached." |
514	| 100% of 2 MB used | Oldest entries are **silently dropped** from the bottom of `undo_stack` to make room (FIFO eviction). A one-time toast notification: "Undo history is full. The oldest edits can no longer be undone." The redo stack is cleared when the limit is first hit. |
515	
516	The 2 MB cap can be adjusted in `config.yaml` under `undo_history_max_bytes`. The default is chosen to be generous for normal use while staying well within typical session file size budgets.
517	
518	### Stack boundaries
519	
520	- The undo stack **persists across browser sessions** — it is stored in the session JSON file on disk, not in browser memory
521	- Returning to a session fully restores the undo/redo state as of the last browser close
522	- Master CV saves are **not** on the session undo stack; they are reverted via the timestamped file backup (a separate restore path accessible from the Master CV tab)
523	- After a session is archived / finalised, the undo stack is cleared and the `undo_stack` key is removed from the session file to reclaim space
524	
525	### Revert to session start
526	
527	A **"Revert CV to session start"** button is available in a "Danger zone" section of the Settings modal. It restores the CV to the state it was in when the user entered the Customisation phase (stored as a snapshot in the session file). This is a non-undoable destructive action and requires explicit confirmation: *"Revert all CV changes? This cannot be undone. The undo history will also be cleared."*
528

## Graphical Designer

### What the proposed design gets right

- **"The document is the UI" thesis** — Editing in-place within the live preview eliminates context-switching and preserves the WYSIWYG promise throughout customisation.
- **Inline controls over separate tabs** — Hover toolbars and inline element-expand replace fragmented tab-per-section navigation, concentrating all actions near the elements they affect.
- **Ghost-item visibility pattern** — Strikethrough/50% opacity/dashed border excluded items create coherent inline visual contrast.
- **Collapsible sections with summary badges** — Creates scannability for dense documents without expanding everything on first load.
- **Sticky settings bar** — Consolidating Length, Style, ATS Score, and Regenerate eliminates hunting for controls across modals.
- **Analysis clarification questions embedded inline** — Creates stronger context and avoids the chat/viewer toggle.
- **(A) Undo persistence eliminates anxiety about experimentation** — Undo stack survives browser close; the 2 MB cap with visual indicators (amber badge at 80%, toast at 100% with graceful FIFO eviction) means layout designers can iterate and revert freely without losing work across sessions.
- **(B) Page count badge reflecting user targets makes layout decisions data-driven** — When the badge shows "~2.1 pages · Target: 2 pages · 5% over target," the designer has objective feedback on whether a layout choice is within acceptable bounds, rather than subjective judgment.
- **(C) Position-type presets reduce layout surprises across preset switches** — The academic preset (multi-page, full publication format) vs. industry preset (2-page, publications omitted or abbreviated) are now front-and-center at the settings bar, so switching presets happens with full visibility of how page count will shift.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Inline hover toolbars risk visual clutter and accidental activation** — 10+ buttons on every hover over 30+ bullets creates cognitive overload and UI flicker. Reducing to 3–4 core visible actions with a "more" menu is needed.
- **Pending-suggestion amber boxes may conflict with CV's visual hierarchy** — Amber borders on a professional resume appear as editorial artifacts rather than integrated guidance. A softer background tint would be less disruptive.
- **(A) Undo history visual indicators (amber badge, toast) could clutter the settings bar during rapid iteration** — If a user is rapidly undoing/redoing layout changes over many sessions, the amber warning badge and FIFO-eviction toast notifications may create visual noise. Consider whether toast severity/frequency can be tuned for power users.
- **(B) Page target thresholds (10–25% over target = amber, >25% = red) may not align with design intent** — If the target is 2 pages and the designer wants to push to 2.3 pages for visual balance, the red badge triggers prematurely. The thresholds should be user-configurable or position-preset-specific.
- **(C) Industry vs. academic preset switch creates layout reflow** — Switching from academic (full publications section, multi-page) to industry (publications omitted entirely) causes dramatic vertical whitespace changes. No preview-of-preset-change is documented, so designers may discover layout breakage after committing the switch.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Reduce the default element hover toolbar to 3 core buttons** — Keep ▼ (expand), ✗ (exclude), ↑↓ (reorder) always visible; tuck ✓, ✏️, ✨, ✅, ❌, 🔄 into a three-dot menu.
- **Apply a subtle background tint instead of amber border** — 10–15% amber background fill behind pending elements + a small 6px amber dot to the left. Less graphic competition with CV typography.
- **(A) Add a "pause undo history" toggle for long editing sessions** — If the 2 MB cap is approaching, users can opt to freeze the stack and start fresh, reducing session bloat while keeping active undo/redo available.
- **(B) Make page-count threshold colors configurable per-preset** — In position-type preset settings, expose: "Target page length: [2 pages]. Warn when: [10% over ○ 20% over ○ 30% over]". Industry presets default to 10%, academic to 20%.
- **(B) Add a "Target vs. Actual" mini chart in the settings bar** — A small bar-chart icon showing the target (blue) vs. current (green/amber/red) page count side-by-side. Clicking opens a detailed page-break visualiser.
- **(C) Add a preset-switch preview modal** — Before switching between industry/academic presets, show a side-by-side layout preview: "Switching to Academic (full publications, 3.2 pages estimated) — current layout shows 2.1 pages." Offer "Preview" and "Apply" buttons.
- **Constrain expanded panel height** — `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` on the element card; scrollable with visible scrollbar indicator.
- **Add font family and colour theme controls to the settings bar** — Font family (Inter/Garamond/Calibri) and theme (Professional Blue / Warm Neutral / Bold Contrast) dropdown; addresses existing gap US-G3.
- **Display a live page-break preview** — Mini page-stack icon with colour-coded warning (green ≤2 pages, amber 2–2.5, red >2.5) in the sticky settings bar. "View page breaks" toggle highlights break points in the rendered CV.
```

Perfect. Now I have all the context I need. Let me synthesize the three design changes with the existing Persuasion Expert section to create a comprehensive updated version:

## Persuasion Expert

### What the proposed design gets right

- **Live document context during editing** — Users see immediate impact of framing decisions on the rendered resume, directly supporting persuasive-intent evaluation.
- **Inline "Persuasion comments" row in expanded element panels** — Currently surfaced only in the separate Rewrite Review tab; inline placement is a major discoverability upgrade.
- **Model recommendation badges integrated into element expansion** — Consolidates Emphasize/Include/De-emphasize/Exclude signals adjacent to persuasion and ATS feedback.
- **Iterative in-place editing enabled by session undo persistence (Change A)** — Undo stack survives browser close (2 MB cap, amber warning at 80%, FIFO eviction + toast at 100%), directly lowering the friction to iterate boldly on rewrite suggestions without fear of unrecoverable loss.
- **Contextual highlighting of the active workflow section** — Keeps persuasive framing decisions anchored to intent.
- **Master CV always accessible** — Allows strong framing decisions to flow back to the master record rather than being one-off session edits.
- **Page count warnings informed by position targets (Change B)** — Colour thresholds on the page-count badge (green/amber/red) now driven by user-configured position-type targets (industry, academic, medical_clinical, government presets), making it clear when length choices conflict with role expectations.

### Concerns or regressions vs current design

- **Position style presets may not align persuasive strategy to target genre (Change C)** — Presets set `bullet_style` (impact vs. detail) and `summary_style` (career vs. statement) globally per position, but do not explicitly map to persuasion intent. An "impact" preset may omit methodological detail that peer-reviewed research audiences expect; a "statement" summary may lack the career-narrative coherence that industry hiring managers seek. The mapping between preset + style + persuasion checks needs clarification.
- **Publication handling per preset (Change C) risks strategic incoherence** — Each preset has a publication strategy (include/exclude, selection logic, format). If an academic preset excludes publications but the role's JD emphasizes peer-reviewed work, the ATS warning fires—but the persuasion frame (research leadership vs. practical impact) may already be misaligned. The warning flags ATS gaps, not persuasion gaps.
- **Ghost-style excluded elements may undermine persuasion coherence** — A user might include a mediocre bullet without checking persuasion comments. Proposal does not specify whether ghost elements trigger warnings.
- **High-priority persuasion flags only visible on expand** — A critical persuasion issue (passive voice, absent result clause) does not surface in the collapsed view unless explicitly specified, so most users skip past weak-verb bullets without noticing.
- **No explicit gating of submission on persuasion acknowledgement** — Current design gates "Submit All Decisions" on `persuasionWarningsAcknowledged`. The proposed design does not specify whether a phase-exit gate remains.

### Suggested enhancements

- **Clarify persuasive intent alignment for position-style presets (Change C)** — Document the persuasion strategy per preset: *Industry preset: lead with business impact, minimize methodology detail, emphasise results and scale.* *Academic preset: establish research rigor, include methodological depth, frame contributions to peer scholarship.* *Medical/Clinical preset: prioritise patient outcomes and regulatory compliance, include certification/credential depth.* *Government preset: emphasise mission alignment and security/compliance rigor.* Provide a settings option to override preset-chosen `bullet_style` / `summary_style` per job to allow mismatch correction.
- **Surface high-priority persuasion flags in collapsed element view (Change A+)** — A small ⚠ badge appears next to the collapsed element text when passive voice, hedging language, missing result clause, or weak verb is detected. Clicking expands the element to see the full persuasion comments. This brings critical issues into the decision-making path even without explicit expand.
- **Explicit persuasion gate at phase-exit** — "Submitting this phase requires addressing all ⚠️ Persuasion flags or explicitly acknowledging them as reviewed. Proceed without review?"
- **Persuasion comment prioritisation by impact** — Weight passive voice, hedging, absent result clause, and weak verb above structural notes (word count, CAR pattern). Specification: the first three checks (passive, hedging, result clause) appear first in the prose; word-count and CAR notes follow.
- **Publication inclusion warnings tied to persuasion narrative (Change C)** — When a preset excludes publications but the JD emphasizes peer-reviewed work, the warning should state: "Publications are excluded in this preset, but the role lists peer-reviewed work as a requirement. Include publications to support research-focused narrative?" rather than a generic ATS gap.
- **Inline CAR-structure suggestion in the expanded panel** — If an element lacks a Challenge component, add a "Suggest CAR structure" button in the expanded panel to strengthen narrative framing.
- **Cross-document framing check on phase advance** — When exiting Customisation, compare narrative threads in Experience bullets against the Summary opening. Warn if they lead with different role identities (e.g., bullets emphasise data engineering, summary opens with ML leadership).
- **Session undo encourages iterative reframing (Change A)** — Document that the 2 MB session-persisted undo stack (with amber warning at 80%, FIFO eviction at 100%) is designed to reduce the friction cost of experimental rewrites. Users can confidently try bold rephrasing, accept suggestions, and undo if the result feels inauthentic. This aligns with "bolder iterative rewrites" goal.
```

145	## 5. CV View — Settings Bar
146	
147	A **sticky settings bar** appears above the rendered resume, always visible while scrolling:
148	
149	```
150	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
151	│  Length: [● Combined pages ○ Resume+Bib pages ○ Characters]     │
152	│  Style:  [Sidebar ▾]   ATS Score: 87%   Pages: ~2.1            │
153	│  [↺ Regenerate Preview]                                         │
154	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
155	```
156	
157	| Control | Options / Behaviour |
158	|---------|---------------------|
159	| **Length** | Radio: Combined pages · Resume + Bibliography pages · Character count. Updates the page-count/char-count indicator live. |
160	| **Style** | Dropdown: Sidebar (human-readable) · Plain/ATS · [additional registered styles]. Switching style triggers a preview regeneration. Active style is always shown in the label (e.g. "Style: ATS Plain ▾"). Download filenames include the style (`resume_ATS.pdf`, `resume_Sidebar.pdf`). |
161	| **ATS Score** | Live badge (green/amber/red). Label: "ATS: 87% (current CV)". Click opens ATS detail overlay showing matched/missing keywords. |
162	| **Pages** | Estimated page count with mini page-stack icon. Colour is based on the user's **target page length** (configured per-session or globally in settings): green when within target, amber when 10–25% over target, red when > 25% over target. Target defaults are position-type-aware when a position type is set (see [#126](https://github.com/Warnes-Innovations/cv-builder/issues/126)). Tooltip shows: "~2.1 pages · Target: 2 pages · 5% over target." |
163	| **Layout status** | Badge: "🔄 Preview — confirm to finalise" when layout is unconfirmed; "✅ Layout confirmed — ready to download" when confirmed. Clicking "🔄" opens the layout confirmation flow. |
164	| **Validation** | Badge: "✓ Valid" / "⚠ 3 issues" / "✗ 1 error". Updates live as the user edits. Click opens the full 17-check ATS validation report. |
165	| **Regenerate** | Re-renders the preview with current selections. |
166	| **Undo / Redo** | Undo (Ctrl+Z) / Redo (Ctrl+Y) buttons for session-scoped edits. Shows count of undo steps available. See Section 17. |
167	
168	---
169	
170	## 6. Universal Expand / Collapse Model
171	
172	Every document in the right pane follows a **consistent two-state model** for sections and their contained elements. A single ▶/▼ toggle on the left of each section header controls the state.
173	
174	### Section States
175	
176	| State | What is shown |
177	|-------|--------------|
178	| **Collapsed** (default) | Section heading + a one-line summary badge: e.g. `"3 of 7 bullets included • 2 pending suggestions"` or `"Skills: Python, R, SQL +4 more"` |
179	| **Expanded** | Full section content — all included elements in final rendering order, plus excluded/hidden elements in ghost style (see Section 9) |
180	
181	### Element States
182	
183	| State | What is shown |
184	|-------|--------------|
185	| **Collapsed** (default) | Final/current text rendered as it will appear in the output. Tier-2 toolbar visible on hover or keyboard focus (see Section 9). High-severity flags (passive voice, missing result clause) show a small ⚠ badge inline with the text so they are visible without expanding. |
186	| **Expanded** | Multi-row detail panel (grows in-place, no modal): |
187	| | **Original** — text from Master CV as imported, read-only. Labelled "(from Master CV — read only)". |
188	| | **Current** — the version active in this session. Editable via explicit ✏️ Edit button (see Section 12). |
189	| | **Proposed** — LLM-suggested rewrite (if generated). Displayed with **word-level diff** (Theme 3): removed words in red strikethrough, added words in green underline, against the Current text. Editable before accepting. |
190	| | **Model recommendation** — badge: `Emphasize` · `Include` · `De-emphasize` · `Exclude`, with one-sentence rationale. |
191	| | **ATS comments** — keyword match notes, missing terms, density issues. Keywords grouped by canonical term (e.g. **Machine Learning** [ML, ML Ops]). Missing hard-requirement terms shown with a suggested insertion point. |
192	| | **Persuasion comments** — the eight persuasion checks rendered as prose: "Strong verb ✓ · Passive voice ⚠ · Result clause ✓ · Word count ✓". Issues weighted by persuasive impact (passive voice and missing result clause first). |
193	
194	Expanding an element keeps it **in-place within the section** — no modal, no side panel. The element card grows vertically. The panel is `max-height: 60vh; overflow-y: auto` so it does not push the rest of the resume off-screen on small viewports. Collapsing restores the single-line rendered view.
195	
196	Expanded element panel state **persists across document tab switches** within the same session (stored in session state). A dot indicator on the section summary badge shows "N elements expanded" so users can see at a glance that panels are open.
197	
198	All text fields in the expanded element panel are edited via explicit **Save / Cancel** buttons (see Section 12 and Section 17 — not blur-save).
199	
200	---
201	
202	## 7. Workflow Integration — Contextual Highlighting
203	
204	As the workflow phase advances, the right pane's CV view provides visual cues:
205	
206	- The **section currently being worked on** receives a blue left-border accent and a subtle background tint
207	- **Sections not currently active** are at normal opacity — still readable, still editable, just not emphasised
208	- The left-pane chat header shows a breadcrumb: `Phase: Customisation › Experience`
209	- When the agent posts a message that references a specific element, the right pane **scrolls** to that element and highlights it
210	
211	**Motion sensitivity (prefers-reduced-motion):** All animations (flash highlights, scroll animations, border transitions) must respect `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. Under reduced motion: scroll is instant (no smooth scroll), highlights are a static 2-second coloured background (no pulse or flash), and border transitions are instant. CSS:
212	
213	```css
214	@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
215	  .cv-element-highlight { animation: none; background-color: #fffacd; }
216	  html { scroll-behavior: auto; }
217	}
218	```
219	
220	---
221	
222	## 8. Section-Level Controls — Three-Tier Model (Theme 1)
223	
224	Controls use a **three-tier visibility model** so all actions are reachable by mouse, keyboard, and touch without relying solely on hover.
225	
226	### Tier 1 — Always visible (no hover required)
227	
228	These appear permanently in the section header:
229	
230	| Control | Action |
231	|---------|--------|
232	| **▶/▼** | Expand / collapse section (keyboard: Enter or Space when header is focused) |
233	| **(+N hidden)** badge | Count of excluded elements; click to reveal ghost items inline |
234	| **N pending** badge | Count of elements with unresolved suggestions; click to jump to first pending element |
235	
236	### Tier 2 — Visible on hover OR keyboard focus (`:hover`, `:focus-within`)
237	
238	These appear when the mouse enters the section header or it receives keyboard focus:
239	
240	| Control | Action |
241	|---------|--------|
242	| **✨ Suggest section** | Trigger LLM include/exclude/reorder suggestions for all elements in this section |
243	| **↕ Reorder** | Enter drag-to-reorder mode (keyboard: use ↑↓ per-element buttons in Tier 2 below) |
244
```
